Return any entry whose support does not carry the posted figure.
Release within the close window so the entry is not posted late.

title.en: Search the ledger for postings that never passed a reviewer

description.en: Test the control from the ledger's side rather than the approval queue's, finding entries that reached a reported balance with no approval and establishing the route by which each one got there.

text.en: Extract every posting in the period with its approval status attached.
Isolate entries above the threshold carrying no approver or a self-release.
Trace each exception to what allowed it, whether configuration or emergency access.
Report the exceptions with their value and the balances they reached.

templates.title: Account reconciliations prepared and reviewed on cycle
templates.description: Each account on the reconciliation inventory is agreed to an independent source on its stated cycle, reviewed by someone other than the preparer, and its reconciling items cleared within an age limit rather than carried forward indefinitely.
templates.objective: To ensure every account on the reconciliation inventory is agreed to an independent source on its cycle, reviewed independently of its preparer, and its open items cleared within a stated age.
templates.successCriteria:
A reconciliation inventory names every account carrying a balance, with its owner, its cycle and the source it is agreed to.
Each reconciliation agrees the ledger balance to that source, with the difference itemised rather than shown as a net figure.
A reviewer other than the preparer signs each reconciliation within the days the close calendar allows for it.
Open items carry an age, an owner and a clearing action, and anything beyond the age limit is escalated rather than rolled.
Accounts on the trial balance appearing on no reconciliation are added to the inventory or excluded on a recorded basis.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the reconciliation inventory and the trial balance at period end; together they define the population, which is every account carrying a balance.
Collect the completed reconciliations for the periods selected, with the preparer and reviewer sign-offs and their dates.
Request the independent sources behind the sampled accounts: bank statements, custodian reports, subledger extracts and counterparty confirmations.
Obtain the open item log showing the age of every unresolved reconciling item.
Collect the close calendar entries that fix when each reconciliation falls due.

Analysis:
Reconcile the inventory against the trial balance in full, listing accounts with a balance and no reconciliation and inventory entries with no balance.
Sample thirty reconciliations weighted to cash, intercompany, suspense, accrual and any account carrying a prior period exception.
Agree the ledger figure on each sampled reconciliation to the trial balance and the source figure to the independent document behind it.
Compare preparer and reviewer identities, and set each sign-off date against the calendar date it was due.
Age the open items on the sampled accounts and test whether those past the limit were escalated or simply carried.

Output:
Schedule of accounts with a balance but no reconciliation, and of reconciliations for accounts no longer in use.
Sample results by account type, stating how many were tested and what was found in each.
List of reconciliations signed by the preparer alone, or reviewed after the date the calendar set.
Aged analysis of open reconciling items, naming those beyond the limit and the owner of each.

title.en: Inventory the accounts to be reconciled, and to what source

description.en: Draw the reconciliation population from the trial balance rather than from habit, settling for each account the independent source it will be agreed to and how often that has to happen.

text.en: List every account carrying a balance at the period end.
Name the independent source each account will be agreed to.
Set the cycle for each account: monthly, quarterly or on movement.
Record a basis for every account left out of the inventory.
Assign a preparer and a separate reviewer to each account.

title.en: Draft a reconciliation format that itemises the difference

description.en: Give preparers one format that forces the difference to be broken into items with owners and dates, so an unexplained balance cannot hide inside a single summarised line.

text.en: Show the ledger balance and the source balance side by side.
Break the difference into items, each with a date, a cause and an owner.
Carry the age of every open item forward from the prior period.
Provide dated sign-off blocks for the preparer and the reviewer.

title.en: Prepare each reconciliation inside the days the calendar allows

description.en: Perform the reconciliation on cycle: agree both sides to their sources as at the same date, itemise whatever remains, and put it to the reviewer before it falls due.

evidenceHint.en: The signed reconciliation for the account and period, showing both balances agreed to their sources with the itemised difference attached.

text.en: Pull the ledger balance and the independent source as at the same date.
Itemise every difference rather than presenting a net amount.
Attach the document supporting each item above the threshold.
Submit the reconciliation to the reviewer by the date it falls due.

title.en: Close out the open items before they pass the age limit

description.en: Work the open items instead of rolling them forward, chasing each to the action that clears it and escalating whatever survives the age limit rather than letting it enter another period.

evidenceHint.en: The aged open item log for the period, showing each item's age, its owner, the action taken and the escalations raised past the limit.

text.en: Age every unresolved item from the date it first arose.
Assign each item to the person able to clear it.
Escalate anything past the age limit to the account owner's manager.
Write off or provide for items that cannot be cleared, with approval.

title.en: Compare the inventory against the trial balance at period end

description.en: Test the completeness of the population itself, which no individual reconciliation can demonstrate: an account carrying a balance and appearing on no reconciliation is the gap this looks for.

text.en: Match every trial balance account to an entry in the inventory.
List accounts holding a balance for which nothing was reconciled.
Identify inventory entries for accounts no longer used.
Refer unreconciled balances to the controller with their value.

templates.title: Significant estimates and judgements reviewed
templates.description: Each estimate the statements depend on carries a written methodology and inputs that can be traced outside the model, is reviewed for the judgement it embodies rather than its arithmetic, and is compared afterwards against what actually settled.
templates.objective: To ensure each significant estimate rests on a recorded methodology and traceable inputs, is challenged independently before posting, and is measured afterwards against the amount that settled.
templates.successCriteria:
A register lists every significant estimate with its methodology, its key inputs and the individual accountable for the figure.
The methodology applied in the period is the one recorded, and any change to it carries a stated reason and an approval.
Every key input can be traced to a source outside the model that computes the estimate.
The reviewer records the range considered and why the point selected sits where it does, not merely that the figure was approved.
Prior estimates are measured against the amounts that settled, and a difference falling consistently one way is reported rather than absorbed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of significant estimates; the population is every estimate carrying a stated methodology, typically credit loss allowances, inventory and warranty provisions, impairment, incentive accruals and tax positions.
Collect the working papers behind the estimates selected, including the model, its inputs and the version approved for the period.
Request the reviewer's note showing the range considered and the basis on which the point was selected.
Obtain the prior period estimates together with the amounts that have since settled against them.
Collect the approvals for any change of methodology or key assumption during the period.

Analysis:
Test every estimate whose value exceeds performance materiality and sample three below it, so the population is covered by value rather than by count.
Trace each key input to its source: the aged debt listing, the claims history, the rate published externally, the forecast the board approved.
Re-perform the calculation on one estimate per method to confirm the model applies the methodology recorded for it.
Compare the assumptions used against the prior period and against the approved forecast, investigating any movement with no stated cause.
Measure at least two prior estimates against what settled and judge the direction of the difference on each.

Output:
Population of estimates with the value of each, and the sample selected with the basis on which it was chosen.
Exceptions where the methodology applied differs from the one recorded, with the effect on the figure reported.
List of key inputs that could not be traced beyond the model that consumed them.
Table of estimate, outcome and difference by period, naming any bias that runs consistently one way.

title.en: Catalogue the figures that rest on judgement, and their drivers

description.en: Identify which amounts in the statements depend on judgement rather than measurement, recording for each the driver that moves it most and the individual accountable for the number.

text.en: List the balances and charges that depend on a judgement.
Record the driver that moves each of them most.
Name the individual accountable for the figure, not the team.
Rank them by value against performance materiality.

title.en: Document the methodology and the inputs behind each estimate

description.en: Write down how each estimate is computed and where its inputs come from, so the figure can be re-performed by someone who did not build the model that produces it.

text.en: State the method, the population and the period each estimate covers.
Name the source system or document behind every key input.
Record each assumption and the range it was selected from.
Version the model and record who approved the version in use.

title.en: Challenge the assumptions before the figure enters the ledger

description.en: Conduct the review as a challenge to the judgement rather than a check of the arithmetic, testing whether the assumptions still hold and recording the range considered before anything is posted.

evidenceHint.en: The reviewer's note for the period, stating the range considered, the point selected and the reason, signed and dated ahead of posting.

text.en: Compare each assumption against the evidence available at the reporting date.
Compute the figure at both ends of the reasonable range before accepting a point.
Record why the selected point sits where it does within that range.
Return the estimate to its preparer where an assumption cannot be supported.

title.en: Back-test prior estimates against the amounts that settled

description.en: Look at estimates whose outcome is now known and judge whether the method produces figures that land near the truth, or drifts consistently in one direction period after period.

text.en: Select estimates from earlier periods whose outcome has now settled.
Measure each recorded figure against the amount finally realised.
Judge whether the differences fall on one side across periods.
Refer a persistent bias to the audit committee with the method behind it.

templates.title: Consolidation and intercompany eliminations performed
templates.description: Component results enter the group at the approved ownership and rate, intercompany balances and trading are matched between the two entities that recorded them, and whatever remains after elimination is resolved rather than posted to a plug.
templates.objective: To ensure components consolidate on the approved structure, ownership and rates, with intercompany positions matched between counterparties and eliminated leaving no unexplained difference.
templates.successCriteria:
Every entity inside the boundary submits on the group chart, and each submission is agreed to that component's own ledger.
Intercompany balances and trading are matched pair by pair, and a difference above tolerance is resolved before elimination.
Each elimination journal is supported by the matched position it removes, with no balancing entry that lacks a counterparty.
Ownership percentages, translation rates and non-controlling interests agree to the source the board approved.
The group figures are agreed back to the components plus the adjustments posted, and that schedule is reviewed at group level.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the consolidation structure for the period; the population is every entity inside the boundary, each with its ownership percentage and functional currency.
Collect the component submissions and the reconciliation of each one to the component's own ledger.
Request the intercompany matching report showing every counterparty pair and the difference standing on each.
Obtain the elimination and adjustment journals posted at group level, with the support behind each.
Collect the rate table used for translation and the published source it was taken from.

Analysis:
Reconcile the consolidated entity list to the legal entity register in full, so an entity omitted from the group is visible rather than assumed absent.
Test every intercompany pair whose difference exceeds tolerance, and sample ten pairs below it to confirm matching actually took place.
Agree the ownership percentage and translation rate for eight entities chosen by value and by currency exposure.
Re-perform the addition from component submissions through eliminations to the group figure for one primary statement.
Examine every group-level adjustment for support, treating one that balances to a suspense or plug account as an exception.

Output:
Statement of whether the consolidated entity list matches the legal entity register, naming any difference either way.
Schedule of intercompany differences by pair, with the value, the age and the counterparty answerable for each.
Exceptions in ownership, rate or non-controlling interest, with the effect of each on the group figures.
List of group adjustments lacking support, including any posted to a plug or suspense account.

title.en: Scope the entities consolidated and the pairs trading between them

description.en: Fix the consolidation population before the close: which entities come in, at what ownership, in which currency, and which counterparty pairs will have positions needing to be matched.

text.en: List each entity inside the boundary with its ownership percentage.
Record the functional currency and the rate source for each component.
Identify the counterparty pairs that trade or hold balances with each other.
Set the tolerance above which a pair difference must be resolved.

title.en: Establish the group chart and the rules that remove each pair

description.en: Put the mapping and elimination logic into the consolidation system itself, so components report on one chart and intercompany positions are removed by rule rather than by a manual journal at the top.

text.en: Map each component's local accounts onto the group chart.
Define the elimination rule for every intercompany account pair.
Load the approved rate table and ownership percentages into the tool.
Restrict who may post a manual adjustment at group level.

title.en: Match the intercompany positions and resolve what differs

description.en: Run the matching between counterparties before the consolidation closes and make the two sides agree with each other, rather than letting the difference disappear into an elimination.

evidenceHint.en: The matching report for the period, showing each counterparty pair, the difference before and after resolution, and the journals that cleared it.

text.en: Circulate the matching report to both sides of every pair.
Require the counterparties to agree a difference or state its cause.
Post the correcting entries in the component ledgers, not at the top.
Escalate a pair still outside tolerance to the group controller.

title.en: Consolidate the components and agree the group figures back

description.en: Perform the consolidation itself and prove the result, so the group figures follow from the components plus the adjustments posted, with each adjustment traceable to the support behind it.

evidenceHint.en: The consolidation pack for the period, carrying the component-to-group reconciliation and every elimination and adjustment journal with its support.

text.en: Load each component submission and confirm it ties to the local ledger.
Post the eliminations and record the support behind each one.
Agree the group total to the components plus the adjustments posted.
Investigate any balancing entry with no counterparty behind it.

title.en: Examine the adjustments posted above component level

description.en: Look at what was added at the top rather than in the components, because a group-level adjustment is the entry least likely to have been seen by anyone outside the consolidation team.

text.en: List every journal posted at group level during the period.
Test each one for its support and for the approval it required.
Identify adjustments repeated each period with no stated cause.
Report entries posted to a plug or suspense account with their value.

templates.title: Disclosures reviewed against a disclosure checklist
templates.description: The statements and notes are worked through line by line against a current disclosure checklist, each answer tied to the note that satisfies it or to a recorded reason for not applying, and re-performed independently before approval.
templates.objective: To ensure the statements are worked against a current disclosure checklist line by line, with every answer tied to the note supporting it and re-performed independently before approval.
templates.successCriteria:
The checklist edition matches the framework and the reporting date, including pronouncements effective for the first time.
Every line carries an answer, and an answer of not applicable carries the reason it does not apply to the entity.
Each applicable line names the note, caption or page satisfying it, so the answer can be verified rather than assumed.
A reviewer independent of the preparer re-performs a defined portion of the checklist before the statements are approved.
Lines answered affirmatively but unsupported by the draft, and disclosures that no line called for, are both resolved before filing.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the completed disclosure checklist for the reporting date; the population is every line in it, and the sample is drawn from those answered as applicable.
Collect the draft statements as they stood when the checklist was completed, and the version finally approved.
Request the source and issue date of the checklist edition, with the list of pronouncements first effective this period.
Obtain the preparer and reviewer sign-offs with their dates, together with the reviewer's re-performance notes.
Collect the minute of the committee or board that approved the statements.

Analysis:
Compare the checklist edition against the framework in force and confirm it covers standards first effective in the period.
Sample forty applicable lines weighted to new pronouncements, judgement-heavy notes and areas restated since the prior year.
Trace each sampled line to the note or caption it names and judge whether that text actually satisfies the requirement.
Test every line answered not applicable in an area where the entity carries a balance, treating an unexplained answer as an exception.
Work the other direction on one primary statement: take each note in the draft and find the line that called for it.

Output:
Population of checklist lines by answer type, with the sample size and the basis on which it was selected.
Exceptions where the cited note does not support the answer given, naming the requirement involved.
List of not applicable answers carrying no reason, and those contradicted by a balance in the accounts.
Statement of whether the reviewer's sign-off preceded the approval of the statements, with any that did not.

title.en: Select the checklist edition matching the framework in force

description.en: Start from the right instrument: the edition tied to the framework the statements are prepared under, the reporting date reached, and the standards becoming effective for the first time this period.

text.en: Confirm the framework and version the statements are prepared under.
Obtain the checklist edition issued for that framework and date.
Add lines for pronouncements first effective in this period.
Remove sections for transactions the entity does not enter, with a reason.

title.en: Assign each checklist section to a preparer and a reviewer

description.en: Divide the checklist so every section has someone who answers it and someone else who tests the answer, with the dates both of them must meet fixed against the reporting calendar.

text.en: Split the checklist into sections by note and by statement.
Name a preparer for each section from the reporting team.
Name an independent reviewer for the portion to be re-performed.
Set the dates both must meet before the statements go for approval.

title.en: Complete every line against the draft and cite what satisfies it

description.en: Work through the checklist against the drafted statements, recording for each applicable line the note that satisfies it and for each exclusion the reason the entity does not reach it.

evidenceHint.en: The completed checklist for the reporting date, every line carrying its answer, the reference cited and the preparer and reviewer sign-offs.

text.en: Answer each line against the draft as it currently stands.
Cite the note, caption or page number that satisfies the line.
State the reason behind every answer of not applicable.
Raise a drafting action where the draft does not yet satisfy a line.
Sign the section off and pass it to the named reviewer.

title.en: Test the answers back against the statements finally approved

description.en: Check the checklist against the document that was actually approved rather than the draft it was completed on, looking in both directions so a note with no line is found as readily as a line with no note.

text.en: Re-perform a sample of lines against the approved statements.
Identify notes in the statements that no checklist line called for.
Confirm late drafting changes were re-checked after the answer was given.
Report unresolved lines to the disclosure committee before filing.

templates.title: Access provisioning approved by the system or data owner
templates.description: Access to an in-scope financial system is created only after the named owner of that system or its data has approved the specific entitlement, and what the administrator built is compared with what was approved before the request is closed.
templates.objective: To ensure an entitlement in an in-scope financial system is created only on the approval of that system's named owner, and that the access built matches the access approved.
templates.successCriteria:
Every in-scope system names one accountable owner, and a request reaching an administrator without that owner's approval is refused rather than built.
The approval names the role or entitlement asked for, not merely the person and the system.
The access actually created is compared with the approved request before the request is closed.
Accounts that never passed the request path are found against the ConnectedIdentityAccount enumeration and either approved afterwards or removed.
Each approval is attached to this control as Evidence through ControlEvidenceLink.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
The list of in-scope financial systems with the owner named against each and the date that naming was approved.
The population of accounts and entitlements created in the period, drawn from each system's own administration log rather than from the ticket queue.
The request records for the same period carrying requester, approver, entitlement and approval time.
The ConnectedIdentityAccount rows the nightly sync returned for those systems, as an independent account population.
The joiner and internal-move records HR raised in the period.

Analysis:
Reconcile the administration log to the directory enumeration, so the population is known to be complete rather than merely supplied.
Sample twenty-five grants stratified by system and by privilege level, and match each to an approval timed before the account or entitlement existed.
Compare the entitlement built against the entitlement approved, treating a wider grant as an exception even where an approval exists.
Test that the approver was the named owner or a delegate recorded as such, rather than a manager standing in.
Isolate directory accounts with no request behind them and establish by what route each was created.

Output:
Population and sample sizes per system with the strata used, so coverage can be judged rather than assumed.
List of grants created before an approval, or with none at all, naming the entitlement each conferred.
Schedule of grants wider than the approval that authorised them.
Exceptions where the approver held no owner or delegate authority over the system concerned.

title.en: Establish who owns each in-scope system and what they may approve

description.en: Settle for every application, database and interface in scope which single person answers for its data, and how far their approval authority runs before a second approver is needed.

text.en: Take the application list from the significant account and process scoping.
Record one accountable owner per system, with a named deputy for absences.
State which entitlements that owner may approve alone and which need a second.
Note where access is granted outside the identity platform, in the system itself.
Have each named owner accept the systems and entitlements put to them.

title.en: Route every access request to that owner before an administrator acts

description.en: Put the approval where the grant is actually made, so the administrator's queue carries the owner's decision with it rather than the requester's assurance that one was given.

text.en: Build the request form so the entitlement asked for is named, not described.
Address each request to the owner of the system it names, or to the deputy.
Hold the request in the administrator's queue until the decision is recorded.
Capture requester, approver, entitlement and both timestamps on the request.
Close the direct-creation route for everyone but break-glass administrators.

title.en: Grant only what the owner approved, and evidence the match

description.en: Perform the provisioning itself: build the entitlement named in the approval, compare what the system now shows against what was asked for, and attach the pair as the evidence of the grant.

evidenceHint.en: The closed request showing the owner's decision and its time, beside a reading of the account as the system holds it, linked to this control through Evidence and ControlEvidenceLink.

text.en: Build the entitlement the approval names and nothing adjacent to it.
Read the account back from the system and set it beside the approved request.
Return the request where the build is wider than the decision allowed.
Attach the approval and the read-back to the control as one evidence record.
Stamp the joiner or move record with the date access became usable.

title.en: Detect accounts that appeared without passing the request path

description.en: Work from the directory rather than the queue, finding accounts and entitlements that exist in a system with no approval behind them, and establishing how each came into being.

evidenceHint.en: The comparison run of ConnectedIdentityAccount rows against the period's approved requests, with the disposition recorded against each unmatched account.

text.en: Compare the directory enumeration against the requests approved in the period.
Separate integration and migration accounts from unexplained user accounts.
Put each unexplained account to the system owner for approval or removal.
Record what created it, so the route can be closed rather than re-swept.
Re-run the comparison after removal to confirm the account is gone.

title.en: Re-perform the owner check against what the systems now hold

description.en: Test the gate independently of its own records by starting from live entitlements and working back to the approval that should exist for each, which is the direction that exposes a grant nobody logged.

text.en: Select entitlements reaching the ledger, payments and master data first.
Trace each back to an approval and read who gave it against the owner list.
Judge whether the approval covers the entitlement or merely the system.
Report grants with no approval, separating the unlogged from the unapproved.
State whether the gate can be relied on for the period under review.

templates.title: Access removed on termination or transfer within SLA
templates.description: Access held by a worker who has left or moved is withdrawn inside the agreed interval: through the platform identity-lifecycle chain where the directory is connected, and through a named manual route where it is not, with each account's withdrawal evidenced.
templates.objective: To ensure access held by a terminated or transferred worker is withdrawn inside the agreed interval, and that every account the directory holds for that person is accounted for.
templates.successCriteria:
Termination and transfer reach the identity chain from the HR record, so a leaver is acted on from a stated status, never inferred from absence.
The leaver pass acts only through an IdentityAccountLink a completed sync re-observed, refusing a stale or contradicted one.
Every disable carries an IdentityWriteJournal row written before the provider call, and none is left PENDING or UNKNOWN past the operator sweep.
Systems no connected directory reaches have a named manual route recorded against the same leaver.
The interval from effective date to the last account withdrawn is measured against the SLA.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
The period's terminations and internal moves from the HR record with effective dates; this is the population the control is tested over.
The IdentityWriteJournal rows for the period with action, mode, outcome, attemptedAt and settledAt on each.
The tenant's identityLeaverMode and its history, since DISABLED and DRY_RUN decide without writing to any directory.
ConnectedIdentityAccount status per leaver from the first sync that ran after the withdrawal.
The manual withdrawal records for systems outside the connected directories.

Analysis:
Test every leaver who held privileged or financial-system access, and sample twenty-five of the remainder stratified by month and by business unit.
Measure the effective date against the settledAt of that leaver's last account and compare the interval with the SLA in force.
Account for every account still ACTIVE in the later sync, by a protection flag, a documented retention or an exception.
Read the refusals the pass recorded — stale link, contradicted link, connection disabled — and follow each to the manual withdrawal that had to replace it.
Establish the write mode in force on each date, because in DISABLED or DRY_RUN the journal records intent and removal must be evidenced elsewhere.

Output:
Schedule of leavers and movers with the count of accounts withdrawn for each.
List of withdrawals outside the SLA, with elapsed days and the system concerned.
Journal rows still PENDING, FAILED or UNKNOWN at the period end, with the account each names.
Exceptions where an account stayed enabled with no protection flag and no recorded reason.

title.en: Pair each in-scope system with the route that withdraws its access

description.en: Determine which systems the connected directories actually reach and which have to be handled by hand, because the manual remainder is where a leaver's access survives unnoticed.

text.en: Mark which in-scope systems authenticate through a connected directory.
Name the manual route and its performer for every system that does not.
Set the interval allowed from effective date to withdrawal for each route.
Identify accounts that must survive a departure, such as running integrations.
Agree the routes and the interval with HR and the system owners.

title.en: Connect the HR termination record to the nightly identity sync

description.en: Wire the trigger end of the chain: the employment status HR records is what the leaver pass reads, and the link between account and person is what lets it act on the right one.

text.en: Feed employment status and effective date from the HR system of record.
Let the sync enumerate each directory into ConnectedIdentityAccount nightly.
Reconcile those accounts to Employee rows as IdentityAccountLink pairings.
Set the tenant's write mode deliberately, starting at DISABLED or DRY_RUN.
Resolve accounts no link explains before relying on the pass to be complete.

title.en: Revoke the leaver's remaining access inside the agreed interval

description.en: Carry out the withdrawal for one departure: let the pass act on the links it can prove, and perform the manual route for every system it cannot reach, inside the interval the SLA sets.

evidenceHint.en: The IdentityWriteJournal rows for that person, each naming provider, write mode and the outcome the directory returned, held with the signed manual withdrawals for the unconnected systems.

text.en: Let the pass select links a completed sync re-observed, and no others.
Disable each connected account through the journalled write path.
Perform the named manual route for every system the pass cannot reach.
Transfer ownership of shared mailboxes, jobs and files before disabling.
Record the completion time of each withdrawal against the leaver.

title.en: Settle every journal row the pass left unresolved

description.en: Close out the writes whose outcome is not yet known, since a row that never settled is an account nobody can say is disabled, and an unknown outcome is not a failure.

evidenceHint.en: The operator sweep over IdentityWriteJournal outcomes for the period, naming each PENDING or UNKNOWN row and what the directory was found to hold.

text.en: List journal rows still PENDING or UNKNOWN after the pass has finished.
Read the account's current state directly from the provider concerned.
Retry or withdraw by hand where the directory still shows it enabled.
Record the settled outcome and the reason on the journal row itself.
Refer repeated failures on one provider to the connection's owner.

title.en: Measure the period's removals against the interval the SLA sets

description.en: Test the control by timing rather than by presence: count from each effective date to the last account actually withdrawn, and separate a late removal from one that never happened.

text.en: Draw the leaver population from HR, not from the identity chain's own output.
Time each departure to the withdrawal of that person's last account.
Check the directory after the interval expired for accounts still enabled.
Separate breaches of the interval from accounts never withdrawn at all.
Report both counts with the systems and privileges the access carried.

templates.title: User access reviewed periodically by the system owner
templates.description: Each quarter the owner of every in-scope system decides account by account whether the entitlements people currently hold are still warranted, deciding against a frozen snapshot, and the revocations that result are carried through to the system.
templates.objective: To ensure the owner of each in-scope system decides every quarter whether the entitlements currently held are still warranted, and that the revocations reach the system.
templates.successCriteria:
An AccessReview campaign exists per in-scope system for the quarter, carrying its period, reviewer and due date.
Decision rows cover every account the scope returned, so the reviewer works from a frozen snapshot, not a list the reviewed assembled.
Each AccessReviewDecision records CONFIRM, MODIFY or REVOKE with the decider and the time, and anything but CONFIRM carries a reason.
A revocation is executed against the membership or connected account and stamped as executed, not assumed from the decision.
The campaign closes with its evidence artefact attached, and one past its due date is escalated.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Every AccessReview raised for the quarter with scope, period, reviewer, due date and closure time.
The AccessReviewDecision and AccessReviewConnectedDecision rows for those campaigns, carrying the snapshot decided against, the decision, the decider and the execution stamp.
The live entitlement list per in-scope system as at the campaign start, obtained independently of the campaign.
The closeout artefact for each closed campaign, and the escalations raised for the overdue.
The remediation records for revocations that had to be carried out in the system by hand.

Analysis:
Reconcile the decision rows to the independently drawn entitlement list, so an account the scope never returned becomes visible.
Test that the decider was the system owner or a recorded delegate, and in no case the holder of the entitlement being decided.
Take every REVOKE and twenty-five CONFIRM decisions, and re-perform each against the entitlement the system holds today.
Compare the decision time with the execution time on each revocation and measure the interval against the remediation expectation.
Read the reasons recorded on a sample of decisions, to judge whether the reviewer decided or merely cleared a queue.

Output:
Coverage schedule per system: accounts live at campaign start, accounts decided, accounts never returned by the scope.
List of revocations not executed, naming the entitlement still held and the days elapsed.
Schedule of campaigns closed late, or closed with decisions outstanding.
Exceptions where a reviewer decided their own access or held no authority over the system.

title.en: Delimit which accounts each quarter's campaign has to return

description.en: Decide before the campaign opens what its scope must sweep in — memberships, connected directory accounts, contractors and service identities — because an account the scope never returns is never reviewed and never shows as missing.

text.en: List the systems whose entitlements a quarter's review must cover.
Choose the campaign scope that returns every account in those systems.
Name the reviewer for each system and the deputy who stands in.
Decide how contractor and non-human accounts enter or leave the scope.
Set the due date against the quarter, not against the day it was raised.

title.en: Raise the campaign with its scope, reviewer and period set

description.en: Open the review in the platform so the entitlement snapshot is frozen at creation and each account becomes a decision row the reviewer must answer, rather than a spreadsheet circulated by mail.

text.en: Create the AccessReview with period, reviewer and due date recorded.
Let it seed a decision row per account the chosen scope returns.
Check the snapshot shows role, status and administrative rights per row.
Brief the reviewer on what confirming an entitlement commits them to.
Leave the reminder and overdue escalation jobs to chase the deadline.

title.en: Judge each account against the snapshot the campaign froze

description.en: Do the review itself: take each decision row, test the entitlement against what the person's current duties need, and confirm, reduce or revoke it with the reason recorded.

evidenceHint.en: The closed AccessReview with its decision rows, each naming the reviewer, the time decided, the snapshot decided against and the reason recorded for anything but a confirmation.

text.en: Work the decision rows one account at a time rather than in bulk.
Compare the snapshot entitlement with the duties the holder performs now.
Record CONFIRM, MODIFY or REVOKE with a reason on every reduction.
Refer accounts whose holder you cannot identify to the system owner.
Close the campaign only once no row is left undecided.

title.en: Remove the entitlements the reviewers revoked

description.en: Carry the decisions into the systems, because a campaign that closes with revocations unexecuted has recorded an opinion about access the holder still has.

evidenceHint.en: Decision rows stamped as executed with the executor and time, set beside the system's own entitlement list read after the campaign closed.

text.en: Take the revocations and reductions the closed campaign produced.
Apply each to the membership or connected account it names.
Stamp the decision row with who executed it and when.
Chase revocations in systems that need a manual change to complete.
Read the entitlement back to confirm the change actually took effect.

title.en: Recompute the campaign's coverage from the systems themselves

description.en: Test the review from outside its own records by drawing the entitlement population directly from each system and asking which of those accounts a campaign ever put in front of anybody.

text.en: Extract the live entitlement list from each in-scope system directly.
Match it against the decision rows the quarter's campaigns produced.
Name the accounts no campaign returned, and establish why the scope missed them.
Re-test a sample of confirmations against the holder's current duties.
Report coverage and unexecuted revocations to the audit committee.

templates.title: Privileged and administrative access restricted and reviewed
templates.description: Administrative rights over in-scope financial systems and the databases beneath them are held by as few named people as the work requires, held apart from those people's ordinary accounts, and what the rights were used for is examined each month.
templates.objective: To ensure administrative rights over in-scope financial systems are held only by named people whose duties require them, and that what those rights did is examined each month.
templates.successCriteria:
Privileged entitlements are enumerated at the level each system grants them, not inferred from holders' job titles.
A privileged right is exercised through an account separate from the holder's ordinary one.
The accounts the nightly sync marks isAdmin are reconciled monthly to the approved holder list, and an unapproved administrator removed or approved that month.
Privileged sessions leave activity records the holder cannot alter, examined each month by someone holding no such right.
Standing privilege no current duty justifies becomes a time-boxed grant whose expiry is set when it is issued.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
The approved privileged-holder list per in-scope system, with the duty that justifies each name and the date it was approved.
The accounts the nightly directory sync marked isAdmin across the period, per provider.
Each system's own administrator group membership, read from the system rather than from the directory.
The monthly privileged-activity examinations with the examiner and the date of each.
The time-boxed grants issued in the period with their expiry, and the records of withdrawal.

Analysis:
Compare three populations — the approved list, the directory administrators and each system's own administrator group — and treat membership of one but not the others as an exception.
Test every privileged holder rather than a sample: the population is small enough that sampling discards the point of the control.
Trace each holder to duties that require the right and to an account separate from their ordinary one.
Re-perform one month's activity examination from the raw records and compare the queries raised with those the examiner recorded.
Check each time-boxed grant against its expiry, so a silent renewal is distinguished from a decision to extend.

Output:
Three-way reconciliation per system of approved holders, directory administrators and system group members.
List of privileged rights exercised through an ordinary user account.
Schedule of months whose examination is missing, late, or performed by someone holding the right.
Exceptions where privilege outlived the duty behind it or the expiry set on it.

title.en: Enumerate what counts as privileged in each in-scope system

description.en: Write down, per system, which entitlements can change configuration, alter data outside the application, or grant access to others, since privilege is what an account can do and not what its holder is called.

text.en: List the entitlements that can alter configuration or posting rules.
Add database and operating-system access beneath each application.
Include rights that can grant or approve access for other people.
State the duty that would justify holding each of those rights.
Have the system owner accept the resulting privileged entitlement list.

title.en: Separate administrative rights from the holder's everyday account

description.en: Put privilege in a second, named account so that ordinary mail, browsing and day-to-day transactions do not run with rights that can rewrite the ledger or its configuration.

text.en: Issue a distinct administrative account to each approved holder.
Strip privileged entitlements from the ordinary accounts that carry them.
Require a second factor at elevation, not only at first sign-on.
Turn on session recording or command logging for the privileged accounts.
Deny the holders the ability to edit or delete their own activity records.

title.en: Reconcile the month's administrators against the approved holders

description.en: Run the monthly comparison between who actually holds administrative rights and who was approved to, in all three places that can answer the question differently.

evidenceHint.en: The month's reconciliation listing every account carrying administrative rights in each system and in the directory, the approval behind it, and the disposition of every unmatched one.

text.en: Pull the isAdmin accounts from the month's directory enumeration.
Read each system's administrator group from the system itself.
Set both against the approved holder list and isolate what differs.
Remove or approve each unmatched administrator inside the month.
Note removals that required an emergency change and why.

title.en: Examine the month's privileged sessions for work nobody requested

description.en: Look at what the rights were used for rather than who holds them, testing the recorded activity against the changes, incidents and requests that should explain it.

evidenceHint.en: The activity extract the examiner worked from for the month, the queries put to each holder, and the answers accepted, retained whether or not anything was found.

text.en: Extract the period's privileged sessions and the commands they ran.
Match each session to a change record, an incident or a service request.
Query any direct data change made outside the application's own screens.
Escalate unexplained activity to the system owner before the month closes.
Keep the extract and the answers as the record of the examination.

title.en: Contest standing privilege that no current duty requires

description.en: Challenge the holder list itself rather than its administration, asking of each standing right whether the duty behind it still exists and whether it could be issued for an hour instead of held for a year.

text.en: Take each standing holder and the duty recorded as justifying the right.
Test that duty against what the person's role now actually involves.
Propose a time-boxed grant wherever the right is used a few times a year.
Report holders whose justification has lapsed to the system owner.
Re-check after the next month's reconciliation that the right has gone.

templates.title: Authentication configuration enforces policy
templates.description: The authentication settings actually in force in each in-scope system — federation, second factor, password rules, session and lockout behaviour — are read out of the systems themselves and compared with the approved standard each year and after any change to it.
templates.objective: To ensure the authentication settings in force in each in-scope system match the approved standard, read out of the systems themselves rather than from the policy text.
templates.successCriteria:
An approved standard states, setting by setting, the value each system must hold and what an exception requires.
The values compared are read out of each system's own configuration, never from a policy document or a vendor default.
Second-factor enrolment is measured over the account population the directory returns, so an unenrolled account is named, not lost in a rate.
Paths that avoid federation — local logins, legacy protocols, break-glass accounts — are listed with an owner each.
Differences are corrected or carry a dated approved exception, and the comparison re-runs when the standard changes.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
The approved authentication standard with its effective date and the settings it fixes for each class of system.
A configuration export from every in-scope system, taken by the tester or witnessed as it was taken.
The mfaEnrolled and status fields per account from the nightly ConnectedIdentityAccount enumeration.
The register of local, service and break-glass accounts able to authenticate outside federation.
The exception approvals that were in force during the period, with their expiry dates.

Analysis:
Compare setting by setting rather than in aggregate, since a system meeting most of the standard fails on the settings it does not meet.
Compute second-factor coverage across the whole ACTIVE population and name the accounts making up the shortfall rather than reporting a rate.
Attempt an authentication down a non-federated path in a test tenant, to establish that the path is closed rather than merely undocumented.
Test each exception for an owner, an expiry and approval at the level the standard demands.
Set the export date against the date the standard last changed, because a comparison older than the standard evidences nothing about today.

Output:
Setting-by-setting comparison per system, showing the value held beside the value required.
Count and list of ACTIVE accounts carrying no second factor, by system and by privilege.
Register of authentication paths that avoid federation, with the owner and reason for each.
Exceptions carrying no approval, no expiry, or an expiry that has already passed.

title.en: Define the value every authentication setting must hold

description.en: Turn the access policy into a settings standard an engineer can apply and a tester can compare against: a required value per setting, per class of system, with the route to an exception stated.

text.en: Group the in-scope systems by what their platforms can actually enforce.
State the required value for each factor, password and session setting.
Set lockout and idle-timeout values against the sensitivity of the data.
Say who may approve an exception and for how long it may stand.
Have the standard approved and dated before anything is measured against it.

title.en: Configure federation, second factor and lockout to those values

description.en: Apply the standard in each platform's own configuration, so the enforcement lives where authentication actually happens rather than in a document people are asked to follow.

text.en: Point each in-scope system at the identity provider for sign-on.
Require a second factor for every interactive account, privileged first.
Apply the password, lockout and session values the standard fixes.
Record where a platform cannot meet a value and what compensates for it.
Re-apply the settings after any platform upgrade that can reset them.

title.en: Close the authentication paths that skip federation entirely

description.en: Find and shut the side doors — legacy protocols, local application logins, shared break-glass credentials — because a single open path makes every setting above it optional.

text.en: Enumerate the protocols and local login routes each system still accepts.
Disable the ones no current integration or process depends on.
Vault the break-glass credentials and alarm on their use.
Give every remaining path an owner, a reason and a review date.
Test from outside that a closed path now refuses an authentication.

title.en: Export the live configuration and compare it with the standard

description.en: Perform the comparison itself once a year and after any change to the standard, working from a dated export of what each system currently enforces rather than from what it was configured to enforce.

evidenceHint.en: The dated configuration export from each in-scope system beside the comparison sheet, showing value held, value required and the disposition of every difference.

text.en: Export the authentication configuration from each system on one date.
Set each exported value beside the value the standard requires.
Raise a correction or an exception for every difference found.
Stamp the comparison with the standard version it was made against.
Repeat the comparison within the month whenever the standard changes.

title.en: Measure second-factor coverage across the accounts the sync returned

description.en: Check the claim that a second factor is enforced against the account population a directory enumeration returns, which is the only place an account excluded from enrolment becomes visible.

text.en: Take the ACTIVE accounts from the latest ConnectedIdentityAccount sync.
Split them by whether the directory records an enrolled second factor.
Name every unenrolled account and the rights it holds, rather than a rate.
Test whether each exclusion carries an approved and unexpired exception.
Report the shortfall to the system owners with a date to clear it by.

templates.title: Generic, shared and service accounts inventoried and governed
templates.description: Every account in an in-scope system that no single person answers for — shared logins and mailboxes, application, integration and batch accounts — is on an inventory carrying a named human custodian and a stated purpose, and is re-attested each quarter.
templates.objective: To ensure every account that no single person answers for carries a named human custodian and a stated purpose, and that the quarter confirms both are still true.
templates.successCriteria:
The inventory is derived from the directory itself: ConnectedIdentityAccount rows no IdentityAccountLink resolves to an Employee are the candidate population.
Each entry names a human custodian, the purpose served and the systems reached, and one whose custodian has left is reassigned inside the quarter.
Credentials are vaulted with issue and rotation recorded, and are rotated when a holder changes.
An account automation must never disable carries the account-protection flag, so a leaver pass refuses it.
Entries serving no remaining purpose are disabled, and the attestation records who attested and when.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
The ConnectedIdentityAccount rows the nightly sync returned, with status, isAdmin and whether an IdentityAccountLink resolves each to an Employee.
The inventory of generic, shared and service accounts with custodian, purpose and systems reached per entry.
Vault records showing credential issue and rotation for those accounts across the period.
The quarter's attestation returns with the attester and the date on each.
The protection flags set on accounts automation must not disable, and the leaver-pass refusals they produced.

Analysis:
Compare unlinked directory accounts against the inventory in both directions: an unlinked account absent from the inventory, and an entry no directory account matches.
Test every custodian against the current HR roster, since a custodian who has left leaves the account answerable to nobody.
Sample fifteen service accounts and trace each to the job or integration it runs and to the date its credential was last rotated.
Test whether the accounts carrying a protection flag are the ones a disable would actually break, and whether any ordinary user account carries one.
Attempt an interactive sign-on with a shared account whose purpose does not require it, in a controlled test.

Output:
Two-way reconciliation of unlinked directory accounts to inventory entries, with counts on each side.
List of accounts with no custodian, or a custodian no longer on the roster.
Schedule of credentials past the rotation interval, naming the systems each reaches.
Exceptions where a protection flag shields an account that is not a service account.

title.en: Derive the candidate list from accounts no link resolves

description.en: Build the population from the directory rather than from memory: the accounts a nightly sync returned that the reconciler could not pair with an employee are the ones nobody personally answers for.

text.en: Take the accounts the latest sync returned for each connected directory.
Set aside every account an IdentityAccountLink resolves to an employee.
Add local accounts in systems no connected directory enumerates.
Classify what remains as shared, application, integration or batch.
Put the unclassifiable remainder to the system owner for a decision.

title.en: Name the custodian answerable for each shared or service account

description.en: Give every entry a person who answers for it, a purpose written plainly enough to test, and the systems it can reach, so the account stops being a thing that merely exists.

text.en: Record one human custodian and a deputy against every entry.
State the purpose in terms of the job or integration the account serves.
List the systems and data the account can reach with its entitlements.
Flag the accounts automation must never disable, and set the protection flag.
Deny interactive sign-on where the purpose does not require a person.

title.en: Rotate the shared credentials on the interval the inventory sets

description.en: Hold the credentials somewhere they can be issued and changed without being known to everybody, and change them when the set of people who could know them changes.

evidenceHint.en: The vault's issue and rotation record for each entry over the quarter, showing the date, the reason and the systems the credential reaches.

text.en: Move every shared credential into the vault and remove local copies.
Rotate on the interval set, and whenever a person with access departs.
Record who checked out a credential and for what piece of work.
Replace embedded credentials in jobs and scripts as they are rotated.
Raise a finding where a credential cannot be rotated without an outage.

title.en: Confirm each entry with its custodian before the quarter closes

description.en: Put the inventory back to the people named on it each quarter and make them answer for the purpose, the entitlements and whether the account is needed at all.

evidenceHint.en: The quarter's attestation return per entry: custodian, purpose confirmed or amended, entitlements accepted, and the disposition of accounts found no longer needed.

text.en: Send each custodian the entries they hold with the current entitlements.
Require a decision to keep, reduce or retire on every single entry.
Reassign entries whose custodian has left or changed role this quarter.
Disable the accounts confirmed as serving no remaining purpose.
Record the attester and the date against each entry attested.

title.en: Contrast the inventory with what the directory currently returns

description.en: Test the inventory from the directory's side, since the failure that matters is a live account nobody has written down, and it cannot be found by reading the inventory alone.

text.en: Draw the unlinked accounts from the latest directory enumeration.
Match them against the inventory and count the misses in both directions.
Trace a sample of entries to the integration or job said to need them.
Test the custodians named against the current employee roster.
Report unattributed live accounts with the entitlements each carries.

templates.title: Changes requested, documented and approved pre-implementation
templates.description: Every change to a system carrying financial reporting data starts as a written request naming what will change, which reports depend on it and why it is wanted, approved by someone other than the person who raised it before implementation begins.
templates.objective: To ensure every change to an in-scope financial system is raised as a written request stating its reason and approved by an authorised approver before implementation begins.
templates.successCriteria:
Every production change to an in-scope system traces to a request naming the requester, the systems touched and its reason.
The approval is recorded before the implementation timestamp, and the approver is neither the requester nor the implementer.
An approver acts inside a delegation naming them for that system, and an approval given outside it is refused rather than ratified later.
Changes altering calculation, posting logic or a key report carry a second approval from the process owner relying on the output.
Requests refused or withdrawn are closed with the reason, and none appears in the deployment log.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the production change population for the period from the deployment log of each in-scope system, not from the change register, so completeness is tested against the pipeline.
Export the change request records for the same window, carrying requester, approver, approval time and target system.
Obtain the delegation of authority naming who may approve changes for each in-scope system, with its effective dates.
Collect the approvals already filed as Evidence against this control through ControlEvidenceLink.
Request the subset of changes touching calculation, posting or key report logic and the process owner approvals for them.

Analysis:
Reconcile the deployment log to the request register in full for one month, so a change made with no request is visible rather than sampled around.
Sample 25 changes across the period, stratified by system and weighted to calculation and posting changes, with at least two per in-scope system.
Compare each approval timestamp with the implementation timestamp, treating an approval recorded afterwards as a failure rather than a late filing.
Test approver authority against the delegation in force on the approval date, not the version current at fieldwork.
Check that requester, approver and implementer are three people, or that a compensating review is named where the team is too small.

Output:
Count of production changes carrying no approved request, by system and by month.
Schedule of approvals recorded after implementation, with the elapsed time on each.
List of approvals given outside the delegation, naming the approver and the system.
Statement of whether the request population is complete against the deployment log.

title.en: Classify which systems and change types the gate covers

description.en: Decide where the approval gate bites by naming the systems whose output reaches the financial statements and separating the change types that must pass through it from those deliberately left outside.

text.en: Name the applications, interfaces and reports whose output reaches the financial statements.
Separate configuration changes from code changes and say who approves each.
Mark the change types left outside the gate, such as content edits with no posting effect.
Agree that exclusion list with the finance owner who relies on each system's output.
Publish the scope decision with the date it takes effect and the systems it names.

title.en: Design the request record and the approval it cannot bypass

description.en: Turn the scope decision into a working gate: a request record that captures the reason and the reporting effect, and a pipeline that refuses to carry a change whose request is unapproved.

text.en: Add fields for the reason, the systems touched and the expected effect on reporting.
Require an approver drawn from the delegation for that system before work opens.
Block the pipeline from accepting a change whose request is unapproved or withdrawn.
Stamp the approval time onto the request so it can be set against the deployment time.
Route calculation, posting and key report changes for a second approval by the process owner.

title.en: Approve or refuse every request under the delegation in force

description.en: Work the gate as changes arrive, judging each request on what it alters and who is entitled to authorise it, and closing the ones that are refused so they cannot reappear quietly.

evidenceHint.en: The approved change request for each production change, carrying an approver named in the delegation and an approval time earlier than the deployment it authorised, filed as Evidence and attached through ControlEvidenceLink.

text.en: Read the request for what it alters and which reports depend on it.
Confirm the approver is named in the delegation covering that system.
Refuse a request carrying no reason or no named target system.
Send calculation and posting changes to the process owner for the second approval.
Close a withdrawn request with its reason so it cannot be revived silently.

title.en: Cross-check deployments against the requests that authorised them

description.en: Look back over the quarter from the deployment side rather than the register side, so a change that reached production with no approved request is found by the control rather than by the auditor.

text.en: Pull every production change the deployment log shows for the quarter.
Match each one to a request approved before its deployment time.
Investigate the unmatched changes with the engineer who made them.
Report changes that went in unapproved to the control owner as exceptions.
Amend the gate where a class of change keeps escaping it.

templates.title: Changes tested with results evidenced before release
templates.description: A change reaches release only once the tests it was meant to pass have run against the build actually being shipped, with the result set kept as an artefact that names the build rather than asserted in a comment on the ticket.
templates.objective: To ensure every change is tested against acceptance criteria written beforehand, with results kept as an artefact naming the build tested and the person who accepted it.
templates.successCriteria:
Each released change carries a test result set naming the build identifier, the tests run and the outcome of each.
Acceptance criteria are written before testing starts, and the result set answers each one rather than reporting a pass rate.
The build tested is the build released, traced by identifier rather than by branch name or by date.
A failing or skipped test stops the release unless a named approver accepts it in writing and the defect is left open.
Changes to calculation, posting or a key report carry a user acceptance sign-off from the finance owner of the affected output.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the release population for the period from the deployment log of each in-scope system; these commonly run from 40 to 400 releases a year.
Export the test result artefacts for those releases, each naming the build identifier and the tests executed.
Collect the acceptance criteria recorded on the corresponding change requests.
Request the written acceptances for releases shipped with a failing or skipped test, and the defects left open behind them.
Obtain the user acceptance sign-offs for changes touching calculation, posting or a key report.

Analysis:
Sample 25 releases stratified by system and weighted to calculation and posting changes, and add every release shipped with a failing test.
Trace the build identifier on each artefact to the identifier in the deployment record, treating a mismatch as untested.
Compare the acceptance criteria against the result set and confirm each criterion is answered rather than covered by a summary pass rate.
Test whether the artefact predates the release using pipeline timestamps rather than the file's upload time.
Re-perform two tests from the sample in the test environment and set the outcome against the filed result.

Output:
Count of releases carrying no test artefact, by system and by month.
Schedule of releases whose tested build differs from the build deployed.
List of failing or skipped tests accepted at release, with the approver and the open defect.
Statement of whether user acceptance was obtained for each calculation change in the sample.

title.en: State the acceptance criteria each class of change must meet

description.en: Settle in advance what proof a change of each risk class owes before it may be released, so that testing depth is a decision taken once rather than an argument had at each release.

text.en: Group changes by the damage their failure would do to reporting.
Set the tests each group must pass before a release is permitted.
Name the finance owner who accepts changes to each key report.
Decide what a test run has to leave behind for it to count as evidence.
Agree the depth expected of configuration changes that carry no code.

title.en: Bind each test result set to the build identifier it ran against

description.en: Make the pipeline produce proof that cannot drift from what shipped, by emitting a result file stamped with the same build identifier the deployment record carries and storing it beyond the run that made it.

text.en: Emit a result file from the pipeline naming every test and its outcome.
Stamp the build identifier onto both the result file and the deployment record.
Store the artefact where it outlives the pipeline run that produced it.
Fail the release automatically when a required test did not run at all.
Open an approval path for a release that ships with a known failing test.

title.en: Exercise the agreed tests and file the outcome before release

description.en: Run the criteria the change was scoped against on the candidate build, and put the result where the release decision can be traced to it, escalating a failure instead of quietly repeating the run.

evidenceHint.en: The test result artefact for each release, naming the build identifier, every test executed and its outcome, attached to this control as Evidence through ControlEvidenceLink.

text.en: Build the candidate and note the identifier the tests will quote.
Run the acceptance criteria written on the change request against it.
Attach the result set to the request before asking for release.
Escalate a failing test to the named approver rather than re-running it silently.
Obtain the finance owner's sign-off where a key report changes.

title.en: Spot-check filed results by re-running them in the test environment

description.en: Judge whether the filed artefacts describe what actually happened, by repeating a couple of the recorded tests and by following the build identifier through to the deployment it claims to cover.

text.en: Select releases from the quarter weighted towards calculation changes.
Re-perform two of the filed tests and compare the outcome recorded.
Trace the tested build identifier through to the deployment record.
Report artefacts that do not match the build they claim to cover.

templates.title: Development, test and production environments segregated
templates.description: Separate places to build, to test and to run the financial systems, holding separate credentials and separate data, so work in progress cannot reach the ledger and nobody can alter what production runs except through the release path.
templates.objective: To ensure development, test and production run as separate environments with separate credentials and data, so nothing reaches production except through the release path.
templates.successCriteria:
An environment register names every instance of each in-scope system and the environment it serves.
Credentials do not span environments: an account that authenticates to development cannot authenticate to production.
Nobody holds standing write access to both the source of a change and the production instance running it, unless a compensating review is named.
Production data copied into a lower environment is masked or separately approved, and each copy is recorded with its date and requester.
Configuration altered directly in production, outside the release path, is blocked or raises an alert that is answered.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the environment register listing every instance of each in-scope system, commonly three to five instances per system.
Export the account list for each environment; where environments are entered through the corporate directory, the nightly identity sync's ConnectedIdentityAccount rows give that population.
Request the record of production data refreshes into lower environments for the period, with the masking applied to each.
Collect the alerts raised for configuration changed directly in production outside the release path.
Obtain the hosting and network configuration showing the boundary between environments.

Analysis:
Reconcile the register against the hosting inventory in full, so an instance nobody listed is visible rather than sampled around.
Intersect the production and development account lists and examine every account appearing in both, rather than a sample of them.
Sample five data refreshes and confirm the masking recorded was applied by inspecting the data that landed, not the request that asked for it.
Test the boundary in a witnessed attempt to authenticate to production with a development credential.
Trace each direct production change alert to a ticket, treating an unexplained one as an exception.

Output:
List of accounts holding access in more than one environment, with the role each holds.
Count of instances found in hosting but absent from the environment register.
Schedule of production data refreshes with the masking applied and the approver of each.
Statement of whether an unmasked production copy sits in a lower environment at the review date.

title.en: Diagram the environments each in-scope system runs in

description.en: Establish what separation currently exists by walking the hosting inventory, naming every instance of every in-scope system and drawing the path a change travels from a developer's machine to the ledger.

text.en: Walk the hosting inventory and name every instance of each in-scope system.
Mark which instance is production and which environments feed into it.
Draw the path a change takes from a developer's machine to the ledger.
Name the interfaces that cross an environment boundary and why they do.
Agree the register with the engineering and finance owners of each system.

title.en: Separate the credentials and the data each environment holds

description.en: Make the boundary real rather than nominal: distinct credentials per environment, no standing production write access from development accounts, and lower environments fed with masked or synthetic data.

text.en: Issue distinct credentials per environment and retire any account shared across them.
Remove standing production write access from accounts used to develop.
Mask or synthesise the production data copied into a lower environment.
Alert on configuration altered in production outside the release path.
Document the compensating review where one person must hold both sides.

title.en: Track each refresh of production data into a lower environment

description.en: Handle copies of live data as events that leave a record, so the question of what production data sits outside production can be answered from a register rather than from memory.

evidenceHint.en: The refresh register for the period, each entry naming the requester, the target, the masking routine applied and the approver where live records were carried across.

text.en: Log the requester, the date and the target environment for each copy.
Apply the agreed masking before the data is made available to users.
Obtain approval where a copy must carry unmasked live records.
Delete the copy once the work that needed it has finished.
File the register entry as Evidence linked to this control.

title.en: Cross-reference the environment account lists for people on both

description.en: Test the separation from the identity side each quarter by taking the account lists of every environment at one moment and challenging each person who appears in more than one of them.

text.en: Export the account list for every environment at the same moment.
Identify the accounts appearing in both development and production.
Challenge each one against the compensating review recorded for it.
Escalate an unexplained crossing to the control owner as an exception.

templates.title: Production deployment authorization restricted
templates.description: A short, named roster of people and service principals able to put a change into production, enforced by the pipeline rather than by convention, with every deployment in the period traceable to one of them.
templates.objective: To ensure the ability to deploy to production is held by a recorded few, enforced by the pipeline, and that every deployment traces to one of them carrying an approved change.
templates.successCriteria:
A deployer roster names every person and service principal able to release to production, with the systems each one covers.
The pipeline enforces that roster: a deployment attempted by an identity outside it fails rather than succeeding with a warning.
Every production deployment names the identity that triggered it and the change request it carried.
The roster is re-attested monthly through an AccessReview campaign scoped to deployment rights, with a decision recorded against each account.
Access granted for a single release is time-boxed and observably withdrawn rather than left standing afterwards.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the deployer roster in force at each month end in the period, with the systems each entry covers.
Export the production deployment log from each in-scope pipeline; populations commonly run from 50 to 500 deployments a year.
Collect the AccessReview campaigns scoped to deployment rights, with the AccessReviewDecision and AccessReviewConnectedDecision rows they carry.
Request the grant and withdrawal records for temporary deployment access issued during the period.
Obtain the pipeline configuration that enforces the roster, with its own change history.

Analysis:
Reconcile every deployment in the log to the roster in force on its date, in full rather than by sample, because the population is machine readable.
Take each monthly campaign and confirm a decision exists against every account in scope, with none left undecided at close.
Test the enforcement in a witnessed attempt to deploy from an account the roster does not name.
Compare temporary grants with their withdrawal records and measure how long each stayed live after its release.
Examine, for 15 deployments drawn from calculation changes, whether the deployer also wrote the change.

Output:
List of deployments whose triggering identity is absent from the roster in force that day.
