Count of accounts holding deployment rights at each month end, with the movement between months.
Schedule of temporary grants with the time each stayed live beyond its release.
Statement of whether every monthly re-attestation closed with each account decided.

title.en: Enumerate the identities able to release to production today

description.en: Find out who can actually reach production before deciding who should, reading the pipeline and platform permissions rather than the organisation chart, and keeping this roster separate from the recertification run over the whole estate.

text.en: Read the pipeline and platform permissions for every identity that can reach production.
Decide which of them the business genuinely needs to hold that right.
Attach each entry to the systems it covers rather than granting it broadly.
Set how a temporary grant is requested, time-boxed and withdrawn.
Separate this roster from the periodic access recertification run for the whole estate.

title.en: Enforce the roster in the pipeline rather than in a document

description.en: Move the restriction from a list somebody maintains to a check the deployment job performs, so an unauthorised release is impossible rather than merely discouraged and every deployment records who triggered it.

text.en: Restrict the production deployment job to the identities the roster names.
Reject a deployment triggered by an identity the roster does not carry.
Require the change request identifier as an input to the deployment job.
Emit a deployment record naming the identity, the build and the request.
Expire a temporary grant automatically at the end of its window.

title.en: Correlate each production deployment with an authorised deployer

description.en: Close every month by setting the deployment log against the roster that was in force, so an unauthorised release is found within weeks rather than at the year-end audit.

evidenceHint.en: The monthly reconciliation of the deployment log to the roster, naming each release whose triggering identity was not authorised on the day it ran, filed as Evidence against this control.

text.en: Export the month's production deployments with their triggering identities.
Match each identity to the roster entry in force on that date.
Investigate a release with no matching entry before the month closes.
Confirm every temporary grant issued in the month has been withdrawn.
File the completed reconciliation with the month's control evidence.

title.en: Recertify the deployer roster in an access review campaign

description.en: Put the roster in front of the person who owns the pipeline each month as a campaign with a decision per account, and act on the revocations rather than leaving them recorded.

evidenceHint.en: The closed AccessReview campaign for the month, its decision rows carrying a confirm, modify or revoke against each account, with the closeout artefact generated at close.

text.en: Open a campaign scoped to deployment rights alone, not the whole estate.
Assign the reviewer who owns the pipeline rather than the account holders.
Decide each AccessReviewDecision row as confirm, modify or revoke.
Execute the revocations and confirm the account can no longer deploy.
Close the campaign so its evidence artefact is generated for the month.

title.en: Contrast the roster against who actually deployed in the period

description.en: Judge whether the roster has stayed as small as it claims by setting the names on it against the names appearing in the deployment log, and by asking what the dormant entries are still for.

text.en: Count the accounts holding deployment rights at each month end.
Identify roster entries that deployed nothing across two quarters.
Question whether each dormant entry still needs the right it holds.
Report the exceptions the monthly reconciliations raised and their outcome.

templates.title: Emergency changes documented and retrospectively approved
templates.description: The exception path written down in advance: what qualifies as an emergency, who may declare one, the record made while the change is happening, and the approval that has to follow within a stated number of days once the system is running again.
templates.objective: To ensure an emergency change is made only on stated grounds, recorded as it happens, and approved afterwards within a fixed window by someone who neither made nor declared it.
templates.successCriteria:
A written definition states what qualifies as an emergency change and which roles may declare one.
Every emergency change carries a record raised at the time, naming the trigger, the system touched and the person who made it.
Retrospective approval is recorded within the stated window, commonly five business days, by someone other than the implementer.
The emergency population reconciles to the deployment log, so a change that skipped the normal gate without being labelled is visible.
An emergency change arising from an Incident cites it, and the Incident record names the change made in response.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the emergency change definition in force and the list of roles entitled to declare one.
Export the emergency change population for the period from the change register; in a settled pipeline this is commonly two to five per cent of all changes.
Obtain the full production deployment log for the same window, so completeness is tested against the pipeline rather than the register.
Collect the retrospective approvals with their timestamps and the Incident records the changes cite.
Request the post-implementation reviews written for those changes and any follow-up work they raised.

Analysis:
Test every emergency change in the period rather than a sample: the population is small and it is the one an auditor examines first.
Reconcile the deployment log to the change register and examine each deployment carrying neither a prior approval nor an emergency label.
Measure the elapsed time from implementation to retrospective approval against the stated window, in business days.
Confirm the approver is neither the implementer nor the person who declared the emergency.
Trace changes citing an Incident to that record and compare the two narratives of the same event.

Output:
Schedule of emergency changes with the elapsed days to retrospective approval on each.
Count of changes deployed without prior approval and never labelled as emergencies.
List of retrospective approvals given by the implementer or by the declarer.
Statement of how the emergency rate moved across the period and which systems drove it.

title.en: Qualify what counts as an emergency and who may declare one

description.en: Write the exception path down before it is needed, so the grounds for bypassing the normal gate are a decision taken calmly rather than a judgement made at two in the morning.

text.en: Write the conditions that justify bypassing the normal approval gate.
Name the roles entitled to declare an emergency and their deputies.
Set the window inside which the retrospective approval must follow.
Decide what the record must capture at the moment of the change.
Agree the definition with finance so a convenience release cannot qualify.

title.en: Open a labelled path the pipeline records as an exception

description.en: Give the emergency route its own machinery, so using it is an observable act that starts a clock and notifies an approver rather than a normal deployment with the paperwork skipped.

text.en: Add an emergency flag the deployment job requires and records.
Require the declarer, the trigger and the system on that record.
Notify the approver automatically as soon as the flag is used.
Start the retrospective approval clock from the deployment time.
Link the record to the Incident that prompted it where one exists.

title.en: Approve emergency changes after the fact inside the stated window

description.en: Judge each bypass once the system is stable again: whether the grounds held, whether the declarer was entitled to declare, and what follow-up work the hurried fix has left behind.

evidenceHint.en: The emergency change record with its retrospective approval, naming the trigger, the implementer and an approver who was neither, filed as Evidence against this control.

text.en: Review what was altered and why the normal gate was bypassed.
Confirm the declarer was entitled to declare an emergency.
Decide approval or rejection within the window, with the reason.
Raise follow-up work where the fix was partial or temporary.
Attach the record and its approval through ControlEvidenceLink.

title.en: Sweep the deployment log for emergencies nobody labelled

description.en: Test the completeness of the exception population from the pipeline side, because the change that skipped the gate and was never called an emergency is the one the register can never show.

text.en: Pull every deployment that carried no prior approval.
Subtract the changes the register labels as emergencies.
Investigate what remains with the engineer who deployed it.
Report unlabelled bypasses and the pattern behind them.
Revise the definition where a recurring case was never anticipated.

templates.title: Scheduled jobs monitored and failures resolved
templates.description: The batch runs and interfaces that move data into the accounting records, watched so that a run which failed or never started is found and put right before the figures it feeds are relied on.
templates.objective: To ensure every job on the processing schedule is confirmed to have run, and that a failed or skipped run is corrected and its data proven complete before the period's figures are relied on.
templates.successCriteria:
The schedule names every automated run a reported figure depends on, each with an owner, a run window and what breaks when it misses.
Each day's execution records resolve every watched job to completed, failed or never started, with no run unaccounted for.
A failure carries its cause, the corrective action taken, and the date the affected data was confirmed complete.
Failure alerts reach a named on-call recipient rather than an unattended mailbox, and an unacknowledged alert escalates.
A job failure that degraded service or corrupted data is raised as an incident and worked there, not closed twice.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export the job schedule as at period end, giving each job's name, run window, owner and the data it feeds.
Export the execution records for the period, giving start time, status, duration and error text against every run.
For jobs operated in this platform, take the definitions from SCHEDULED_JOBS in src/app-layer/jobs/schedules.ts and the outcomes from the execution record each run writes.
Obtain the alerting configuration and the on-call rota each failure alert was routed to.
Obtain the tickets and rerun records raised against the period's failures.

Analysis:
Population is every job on the schedule at period end. Test all of them for a named owner, a run window and an alert route, since a sample cannot show a job nobody watches.
Select 25 job-days across the period, weighted to period-end dates and to the jobs feeding the general ledger, and trace each to an execution record.
Test every failed run in the period rather than a sample, through to the rerun and the confirmation that the recovered data reconciled to source.
Compare the distinct jobs appearing in the execution records against the jobs the schedule holds, to find entries that were disabled or silently removed.
Match each alert recipient to the roster, and measure the gap between a failure and its first acknowledgement.

Output:
A completeness result stating, per job-day tested, the status recorded and whether the schedule expected a run at all.
A failure register for the period naming cause, corrective action and the date the data was confirmed complete.
An exception list of scheduled jobs with no owner, no alert route, or no execution record anywhere in the period.

title.en: Enumerate the scheduled jobs a reported figure depends on

description.en: Draw the watched population from the data flows behind the accounts rather than from whatever the scheduler happens to hold, so a job nobody owns is visible before the night it fails.

text.en: Trace each significant account back to the interfaces and batch runs that feed it.
Open the scheduler and match every traced flow to a job definition that actually exists.
Include the jobs operated in this platform, taken from SCHEDULED_JOBS in src/app-layer/jobs/schedules.ts, where a control leans on one.
Name one owner per job, and the window inside which the run must complete.
State what goes wrong downstream when each job misses its window entirely.

title.en: Configure a failure alert that reaches a named on-call owner

description.en: Wire the scheduler's own failure signal to a person and a response clock, because an unread alert in a shared mailbox is how a missed overnight run survives until month end.

text.en: Turn on both failure and did-not-start alerting across the watched set.
Route each alert to a named on-call rota rather than to a shared mailbox.
Set the acknowledgement window after which an unread alert escalates upward.
Fire a deliberate test failure and confirm it reached the rota holder on duty.
Hold the alert route on the job record so the wiring can be audited later.

title.en: Triage each overnight job failure before the ledger is used

description.en: Work the previous night's failures at the start of the day, so a broken feed is caught while the postings it affects can still be corrected cheaply.

evidenceHint.en: The daily run-status review: the execution records for the night with a status against every watched job, the failures picked up, and the initials and time of the operator who worked them.

text.en: Open the execution records for the night and sort them by outcome.
Confirm every watched job produced a record, rather than inferring success from silence.
Assign each failure to a handler with the hour it has to be cleared by.
Hold the downstream posting or report until the affected feed is back.
Note the outcome against the run so the next reviewer inherits the history.

title.en: Run the recovery for each failed job and confirm what landed

description.en: Rerunning is only half of it: the control is proven when the record count or control total from the recovered run is matched back to the source system it came from.

evidenceHint.en: The rerun record for every failed job, carrying the reconciliation of recovered data to its source totals and the acceptance of the owner who took the figures back.

text.en: Establish whether the failed attempt left partial data that must be backed out first.
Rerun the job from the restart point the run book specifies for it.
Match the recovered record count or control total back against the source system.
Obtain the data owner's acceptance that the affected figures are now complete.
Raise an incident where the failure reached users or disturbed a reported figure.

title.en: Reconcile the period's run log against the job schedule itself

description.en: Test completeness from the schedule side, since a run log can only show the jobs that started and says nothing at all about one that was disabled or quietly deleted.

text.en: Export the schedule as it stood at the start and again at the end of the period.
Compare both against the distinct jobs appearing in the period's execution records.
Investigate every job present in one of those lists and absent from the other.
Establish who disabled or amended a schedule entry, and under whose approval.
Report the count of unwatched or silently retired jobs beside the size of the schedule.

templates.title: Backups executed per schedule and verified
templates.description: The scheduled copying of the systems behind the accounting records, where each run is confirmed to have completed over the data it was meant to cover and the copy itself is checked as readable.
templates.objective: To ensure each system holding accounting data is copied at the frequency set for it, and that every completed copy is checked as readable and complete rather than assumed from a clean exit status.
templates.successCriteria:
Every system whose loss would delay or misstate a reported figure sits in the backup inventory with a frequency, a retention and an owner.
Each scheduled run resolves to a completed, partial or failed outcome, with no run missing from the record.
A completed run carries an integrity or checksum result read back from the copy itself, not merely the job's exit code.
A failed or unverifiable run is escalated the same working day, rerun where possible, and the coverage lost stated in hours.
What is verified here is the copy's own readability; that the data comes back is proven separately under restore testing.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the backup inventory as at period end, giving system, frequency, retention, destination and owner.
Export the backup run history for the period, giving run date, outcome, bytes written, duration and the data set each run covered.
Obtain the integrity or checksum output produced against each completed copy.
Obtain the escalation records raised for failed, partial or unverified runs, with the coverage gap each one left.
Obtain the storage listing showing which copies still exist, against the retention the inventory states.

Analysis:
Population is every system in the backup inventory at period end. Test all of them for a stated frequency, retention and owner, since a sample cannot show a system nobody copies.
Select 20 system-days across the period, weighted to the systems feeding the general ledger and to period-end dates, and trace each to a run record.
For each selected run read the integrity result over the copy rather than the exit code, and confirm the data set covered matches what the inventory entry requires.
Test every failed or partial run in the period rather than a sample, through to its rerun and the hours of coverage it left open.
Compare the copies present in storage against the retention period stated, in both directions, to find copies missing and copies kept too long.

Output:
A coverage result stating, per system-day tested, whether a run occurred, what it covered, and what the integrity check returned.
An exception list of inventoried systems with no run in the period, or with runs carrying no integrity result at all.
A statement of the longest coverage gap in the period, the system it fell on, and who accepted it.

title.en: Delimit which systems hold data a reported figure rests on

description.en: Set the backup population from the accounts backwards, so an interface staging store or a reporting database is not missed because nobody thought of it as a system of record.

text.en: Take the significant accounts and name the systems that originate or hold their data.
Add the staging, integration and reporting stores those systems depend on.
Agree for each the tolerable loss in hours the business is prepared to accept.
Derive the copy frequency and the retention period that tolerable loss implies.
Assign an owner to each entry who can confirm what a copy has to cover.

title.en: Set the retention, frequency and destination for each backup job

description.en: Turn the agreed tolerances into configured job settings, so the schedule enforces the recovery point rather than leaving it to whoever last edited the job by hand.

text.en: Configure each job to the frequency the tolerable loss for that system implies.
Point the copy at a destination separated from the system being copied.
Apply the retention period and confirm copies age out rather than accumulate.
Turn on the integrity step so every copy is read back after it is written.
Alert on a run that fails, completes partially, or does not start at all.

title.en: Verify each completed backup against its own integrity check

description.en: Read the verification result rather than the exit status, because a job can finish cleanly over a data set that quietly stopped including the database that actually matters.

evidenceHint.en: The run history for the day across every inventoried system, showing against each copy the checksum or verification result and the data set the run actually covered.

text.en: Open the previous day's run history across every system in the inventory.
Confirm the integrity step ran and returned a pass against each copy written.
Compare the data set the run covered with what the inventory entry requires.
Attach the day's verification output as Evidence against this control.
Sign the day off against the operator who performed the verification.

title.en: Escalate a missed or unverifiable backup the same working day

description.en: Treat a gap in coverage as a dated exposure with a named owner, since the cost of a missing copy is otherwise discovered only on the day somebody needs it.

evidenceHint.en: The escalation raised for each failed or partial run, naming the system, the hours of protection lost, the out-of-cycle copy taken, and who accepted any residual exposure.

text.en: Raise the failure to the system owner within the working day it occurred.
State the hours of data now unprotected and what would be lost today.
Take an out-of-cycle copy or rerun the job to close the gap where possible.
Obtain the system owner's acceptance where the gap cannot be closed at all.
Refer a system failing repeatedly into the incident and problem process.

title.en: Sample a month of backup records against the schedule that governs them

description.en: Test the pair the other way round, from the schedule into the records, because a system dropped from the job definition leaves no failed run behind for anyone to notice.

text.en: Choose a month and export the backup schedule as it stood inside it.
Pull the run records for that month across every inventoried system.
Identify systems carried in the inventory with no run record in the month.
Trace each schedule change made during the month to whoever approved it.
Report the systems actually covered beside the systems the inventory claims.

templates.title: Restore testing performed periodically
templates.description: The periodic exercise in which a copy from the live backup set is actually brought back into a working environment and the recovered data is reconciled, proving the copies are usable.
templates.objective: To ensure the organization proves at a set interval that a backup can be brought back into a usable and reconciled state inside the recovery time the business has agreed to accept.
templates.successCriteria:
A dated test plan names the systems to be tested, the scenario each is tested under, and the recovery time agreed for it.
Each test restores from a copy drawn out of the live backup set rather than one prepared in advance for the exercise.
The recovered data is reconciled to a known position, so the test concludes on completeness and not on the restore finishing.
Elapsed time is measured from a declared start to usable data and compared against the recovery time agreed.
A test that misses its target raises a dated remediation action and a scheduled retest, rather than a note that it was attempted.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the restore test plan approved for the period, naming systems, scenarios, participants and agreed recovery times.
Obtain the test record for each restore performed, with the copy identifier used, the declared start and the time usable data was reached.
Obtain the reconciliation worked between the recovered data and a control total held outside the copy.
Obtain the remediation actions raised where a test missed its target, with owners, due dates and status at period end.
Obtain the recovery time and recovery point the business has stated for each system in the backup inventory.

Analysis:
Population is every system the plan requires to be restore-tested in the period, taken from the backup inventory rather than from the tests that happened.
Test all of them for a completed test record, since a system quietly omitted from the exercise is precisely what a sample would miss.
For each test performed, confirm the copy used came from the routine backup set and establish who selected it and when.
Re-perform the reconciliation on one test from the recovered data and the retained control totals, without relying on the tester's own summary.
Compare each measured elapsed time against the recovery time agreed, and trace every miss to a remediation action and its status.

Output:
A coverage statement naming the systems the plan required, those actually tested, and those carried forward with a reason.
A result per test giving the copy used, the elapsed time, the recovery time agreed and the reconciliation outcome.
An open-action list of failed tests carrying the remediation owner and the date the retest is scheduled for.

title.en: Choose the restore scenarios the year's test has to prove

description.en: Pick the failure cases worth exercising, since recovering one deleted file proves something quite different from rebuilding a server whose underlying storage is gone.

text.en: Rank the systems by what a day of their loss would cost the reported figures.
Pair each ranked system with the failure mode it is most exposed to.
Agree the recovery time and recovery point the business will accept for each.
Fix the calendar dates on which the tests will actually be performed.
Name the people whose participation the test needs in order to mean anything.

title.en: Draft the restore runbook with the target time each scenario must meet

description.en: Write down the steps, the environment and the measurement rules before the day itself, so the exercise produces an elapsed time that can be compared from one year to the next.

text.en: Set out the restore steps in the order the operator will perform them.
Name the isolated environment the copy will be brought back into.
Define when the clock starts and what counts as data a user can work with.
State the reconciliation that will decide whether the recovered data is complete.
Version the runbook so the edition a given test was run against stays identifiable.

title.en: Restore the chosen backup into an isolated environment and reconcile it

description.en: Perform the exercise on a copy taken unprepared from the live backup set, and finish by proving the recovered data matches a known position rather than that the job completed.

evidenceHint.en: The completed test record: the copy identifier restored, the clock start and finish, the environment used, the reconciliation output and the tester's stated conclusion.

text.en: Select the copy from the routine backup set without preparing it in advance.
Start the clock at the declared point and follow the runbook exactly as written.
Bring the data back into the isolated environment rather than into production.
Reconcile the recovered records against control totals held outside the copy.
File the completed test record as Evidence and link it to this control through ControlEvidenceLink.

title.en: Grade the test against the recovery time the business agreed

description.en: Conclude on the exercise rather than filing it, because a restore that took three days against a one-day target is a finding and not a test that was successfully performed.

text.en: Compare the elapsed time measured against the recovery time agreed for that system.
Judge the reconciliation result, including any records that never came back.
Raise a dated remediation action for each target the test did not meet.
Schedule the retest and name the individual accountable for running it.
Report the systems tested beside the systems the backup inventory holds.

templates.title: IT incidents logged, prioritised and resolved
templates.description: The record kept of IT events that disrupt service or threaten data, each graded for severity against a published scale, given an owner and a response clock, and closed only when its cause is stated.
templates.objective: To ensure a disruptive IT event is logged as an incident, graded against a published severity scale, and closed only once its cause and its effect on the accounting records are stated.
templates.successCriteria:
Every incident carries a severity taken from the published scale, a named owner, a detection time and the systems it affected.
The response and update intervals actually achieved are visible against the ones the assigned severity demanded.
Artefacts gathered during the investigation are attached to the incident record itself, not left in a chat thread.
Closure states the cause, the correction applied, and whether any reported figure was affected or has to be restated.
Events surfacing through monitoring, the service desk or a failed job reach the register, and a control failure behind one is named.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export the Incident register for the period, giving reference, severity, detection time, owner, phase and the time of closure.
Obtain the published severity scale and the response, update and resolution intervals each grade carries.
Obtain the IncidentEvidence attached to each sampled incident, with the time each artefact was captured.
Obtain the monitoring alerts, service desk tickets and failed job runs raised over the same period.
Obtain the post-incident reviews and any correction or restatement they led to.

Analysis:
Population is every incident recorded in the period. Test all of them for a severity grade, a named owner and a detection time, since a blank field is the defect itself.
Sample 15 incidents stratified across the grades, taking every one graded at the top two levels rather than sampling those.
For each sampled incident compare the response and update times achieved against the intervals its grade demanded, measured from detection.
Test completeness the other way: trace a sample of 20 monitoring alerts, service desk tickets and failed job runs into the register, to find events worked but never logged.
Read each sampled closure for a stated cause and an explicit conclusion on whether a reported figure was affected.

Output:
A register exception list naming incidents without a severity grade, a named owner or a detection time.
A sample result stating, per incident, the grade assigned, the interval its grade required and the interval achieved.
A completeness result naming the alerts, tickets or job failures that never became an incident record at all.

title.en: Determine which operational events are raised as incidents

description.en: Draw the line between a routine service request and an incident before the pressure of an outage, so the register holds a comparable population rather than whatever felt serious at the time.

text.en: Name the event types that reach service availability, data integrity or confidentiality.
Separate an incident from a service request, a change and a known problem.
Fix the detection sources that must feed the register, monitoring and service desk included.
Agree which events oblige a report to a regulator, a customer or an auditor.
Publish the definition to everyone who could be first to see such an event.

title.en: Build the severity matrix that fixes each incident's response clock

description.en: Attach response, update and resolution intervals to each grade, so the severity assigned at detection decides what happens next rather than the handler's judgement on the day.

text.en: Define the grades by effect on users, on data and on reported figures.
Set the response, update and resolution intervals each grade carries.
Name the roles that must be told at each grade, and inside what time.
Configure the Incident record so severity and detection time cannot be left blank.
Test the matrix against the previous year's worst events to see whether it fits.

title.en: Open an incident record the moment detection is confirmed

description.en: Create the record at detection rather than after recovery, because the detection timestamp is the point from which every response interval is afterwards measured.

evidenceHint.en: The Incident row created at detection, carrying its reference, the grade assigned, the detection timestamp, the owner it went to and the notifications that followed.

text.en: Raise the record as soon as the event is confirmed, before recovery work begins.
Assign the grade from the published matrix and name the owner accountable.
Capture the detection timestamp and the source the detection came from.
Mark the incident reportable where it is, so the IncidentNotification deadlines run from detection.
Update the record as the incident moves through containment and recovery.

title.en: Attach the forensic artefacts to the incident before it is closed

description.en: Gather the logs and captures while they still exist and hang them on the record itself, since retention windows expire long before a later review asks what actually happened.

evidenceHint.en: The IncidentEvidence links on the closed record, covering the logs, captures and screenshots relied on, each carrying the time it was taken and the person who took it.

text.en: Collect the logs, captures and screenshots the investigation actually relied on.
Link each artefact to the incident as IncidentEvidence rather than to a chat thread.
State the cause reached and the correction that was applied to remove it.
Conclude whether a reported figure was affected and whether a restatement follows.
Close the record only once the owner and the affected system's owner agree.

title.en: Examine the quarter's incidents for controls that failed to detect them

description.en: Read the register as evidence about the control environment, because the events nobody detected say more about the monitoring in place than the ones that were caught within the hour.

text.en: Group the period's incidents by the system and the underlying cause behind them.
Identify which were found by monitoring and which by a user complaining.
Trace each repeating cause to the control that should have prevented it.
Raise a dated action where a control is shown to be absent or ineffective.
Report the count detected by monitoring beside the total the register holds.

templates.title: Inventory of ICFR-relevant systems and key reports
templates.description: The register of applications, interfaces and reports that financial reporting controls depend on, each carrying an owner, the controls that rely on it, and the basis on which it was judged in or out of scope.
templates.objective: To ensure every application, interface and report a financial reporting control depends on is registered with an owner, a scope decision and the controls that rely on it.
templates.successCriteria:
Every application and interface an in-scope control depends on is held as an Asset row, not in a side list.
Each report a control operator relies on is registered with its source system, its parameters and the control that consumes it.
Registered entries carry an owner, a criticality and a ControlAsset link to the controls depending on them, with the rationale stated.
A system run by a third party is cross-referenced to the service organization inventory rather than described twice.
Systems and reports withdrawn in the period are marked retired with a date, and the controls pointing at them re-pointed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the asset register export at period end, filtered to rows carrying financial reporting scope, with owner, type and criticality.
Obtain the risk-control matrix; its key controls are the population the register must account for.
Obtain the ControlAsset extract showing which controls link to which systems, with the rationale on each link.
Obtain the report register with source system, parameters and consuming control for each entry.
Obtain the period's implementation and decommission records, the identity directory's application list and the service organization inventory.

Analysis:
Population one is every key control on the matrix. Reconcile in full against the ControlAsset extract, listing controls that name a system or report but carry no link.
Population two is every registered system and report. Sample twenty-five weighted to those feeding material accounts and confirm owner, criticality and consumer.
Walk completeness from outside the register: take the application list from the identity directory and the hosting records, and find systems holding financial data on no register row.
Compare the period's implementations and decommissions against register additions and retirements, and measure the lag.
Confirm each third-party hosted system resolves to an entry in the service organization inventory.

Output:
Schedule of key controls whose system or report dependency is unrecorded, naming the account each affects.
Sample results for registered entries, stating how many were tested and which lacked an owner, a criticality or a consumer.
Completeness exception list from the directory walk, naming each unregistered system and the balances it touches.
Ageing of register additions against the implementation dates that should have triggered them.

title.en: Delimit which systems and reports carry financial reporting scope

description.en: Decide scope from what the controls actually consume rather than from the size of the system, so a small tool feeding a key reconciliation is in and a large system touching no reported figure is out.

text.en: Read each key control on the risk-control matrix for the system or report it consumes.
Trace every significant account to the application that originates its transactions.
State the scope test in one line: a control conclusion rests on the figures it produces.
Record a basis for each financial system judged to fall outside scope.
Settle who arbitrates the scope decision when finance and IT read it differently.

title.en: Register each in-scope system as an asset with its dependent controls

description.en: Put the inventory where the product already holds technology, so the dependency is a queryable link from a control to an asset instead of a document that ages the day it is written.

text.en: Create an Asset row for each in-scope system with its type, owner and criticality set.
Link every control to the systems it depends on through ControlAsset.
State on each link what the control takes from the system, in the rationale field.
Capture interfaces between systems as dependencies rather than leaving them implied.
Point a hosted system at its entry in the service organization inventory.

title.en: Refresh the register as systems and reports enter and leave service

description.en: Keep the inventory level with the estate by working the period's change records, because a register refreshed only at year end is wrong for eleven months of the year it covers.

evidenceHint.en: The register export at period end set beside the period's implementation and decommission records, showing the date each entry was added, retired or re-pointed.

text.en: Take the period's implementations, migrations and decommissions from the change records.
Add each new system or report before it first feeds a control's figures.
Mark withdrawn rows retired with a date instead of deleting the history.
Re-point controls whose dependency was retired onto the system that replaced it.
Name any change that reached production with no register entry raised for it.

title.en: Sweep the IT estate for systems the register never recorded

description.en: Test completeness from outside the register, since a list can only show what somebody remembered to put on it and the omission is exactly what an auditor is looking for.

text.en: Draw the application list from the identity directory and the hosting records.
Identify systems holding financial data that appear on no row of the register.
Test a sample of registered reports back to the catalogue of their source system.
Refer unregistered systems to the control owner with the balances they touch.

templates.title: Key report logic validated on creation and after change
templates.description: The validation that a key report returns what it claims: its logic agreed to the data underneath it before a control relies on it, and agreed again whenever the query, its parameters or the feeding system change.
templates.objective: To ensure a report relied upon by a financial reporting control is agreed to its source data before first use and agreed again whenever its logic or feeding system changes.
templates.successCriteria:
Each key report holds a validation record naming its query version, the data it was agreed to and who performed the agreement.
Validation agrees record counts to the source tables and sampled values to the transactions behind them.
The parameters, filters and date range used are captured with the result, so a later run can be shown to be the same report.
A change to the report logic, its parameters or the feeding system raises a fresh validation before reliance resumes.
The validator is not the author of the logic, and the result is attached as Evidence linked through ControlEvidenceLink.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the report register at period end; its key reports are the population every validation record must account for.
Obtain the validation records for the period, each naming the report version, the parameters used, the performer and the date.
Obtain the re-performance working papers and the source extracts or queries the report was agreed against.
Obtain the change records for reports altered in the period and for the systems feeding them.
Obtain the Evidence rows and their ControlEvidenceLink entries where validation results were attached to consuming controls.

Analysis:
Population one is every key report on the register. Reconcile in full to the validation records; a report relied on with no validation is an exception on its own.
Population two is every change in the period to a key report or its feeding system. Take all of them where fewer than twenty-five, otherwise sample twenty-five weighted to logic changes.
Re-perform ten sampled validations: run the report on the stated parameters, agree the record count to the source and agree five values back to their transactions.
Compare the validator named on each record against the report's own change history to find self-validation.
Set the validation date against the date the report was first relied upon, and measure any reliance that preceded it.

Output:
Schedule of key reports carrying no validation, or validated against a definition version since superseded.
Re-performance results per sampled report, stating the counts and values agreed and every difference found.
List of changed reports relied upon before re-validation, with the days between the change and the validation.
Exceptions where the validator and the author of the report logic are the same person.

title.en: Name the reports a control operator genuinely relies on

description.en: Separate the reports a control conclusion rests on from the ones read for context, because validating everything a system can print costs more than it proves and leaves the real dependencies unexamined.

text.en: Ask each key control's operator which report supplies the figures they check.
Distinguish a report read for background from one a control conclusion rests on.
Record the source system and the report identifier for every report named.
Mark reports whose figures are re-keyed into a workbook before they are used.

title.en: Frame the validation a report must pass before first use

description.en: Write down what agreeing a report to its source actually means here, so two validators reach the same standard and a record saying the report looked correct cannot pass as one.

text.en: State the completeness test: record counts agreed to the source tables.
State the accuracy test: sampled values agreed to the underlying transactions.
Require the parameters, filters and date range to be captured with the result.
Name who may validate, excluding whoever wrote the report logic.
Set what is attached as Evidence and which controls the result is linked to.

title.en: Re-perform the report against its source before reliance begins

description.en: Do the agreement itself: run the report, take the same figures out of the data underneath it, and settle every difference before a control operator uses the output as fact.

evidenceHint.en: The completed validation record for that definition version: parameters used, counts and values agreed to source, differences cleared, attached in the evidence library against the consuming control.

text.en: Run the report on the stated parameters and capture the definition version.
Agree the record count returned to the count held in the source tables.
Agree a sample of values back to the transactions that produced them.
Settle each difference found and record what was changed to clear it.
Attach the result as Evidence and link it to the controls consuming the report.

title.en: Re-test a report whenever its logic or feeding system changes

description.en: Treat a changed report as a new report until it has been agreed again, since the version a control was proved against is not the version it is now being given.

evidenceHint.en: The change record for the report or its feeding system set beside the re-validation performed on the new version, showing both dates and the validation it supersedes.

text.en: Watch change records for edits to a report definition or to its source tables.
Hold a changed report back from control use until it has been agreed again.
Re-run the completeness and accuracy tests against the changed version.
Note in the record what the change did to the figures the report returns.
Supersede the previous validation rather than leaving two current records.

title.en: Contest a validation performed by the report's own author

description.en: Look for the agreements that prove nothing: a builder checking their own query, a result nobody can reproduce, a reliance that began before the validation was signed.

text.en: Compare the validator named on each record with the report's change history.
Re-perform two validations independently and compare the figures reached.
Identify reports relied on between a change and the validation that followed it.
Refer validations that cannot be reproduced to the owner of the consuming control.

templates.title: End-user computing controls applied to ICFR-relevant files
templates.description: The controls around the spreadsheet beside the system: the user-built files whose output reaches a journal, a reconciliation or a disclosure, each with a named owner, restricted write access, a fixed retained version and a check of what it calculates.
templates.objective: To ensure each user-built file producing a figure relied upon in financial reporting is owned, restricted to named writers, retained as a fixed version and checked before its output is used.
templates.successCriteria:
A register names every user-built file whose output reaches a journal, a reconciliation or a disclosure, with its owner and consuming control.
Write access is held by named people and shown from the file store's own permission export rather than asserted.
The version used each period is retained as Evidence whose FileRecord sha256 fixes the bytes relied upon.
Formulas and cell ranges are checked when the file changes, and the check names what was compared.
Manual inputs cite the document they came from, and each is agreed to it before the file's output is used.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of user-built files at period end with owners and consuming controls; a completeness walk must account for it.
Obtain the permission exports for the folders or workbooks holding the registered files, drawn at the period end.
Obtain the Evidence rows retained for the period with their FileRecord hashes and version numbers.
Obtain the formula and cell-range checks performed on files changed in the period, stating what was compared.
Obtain the journals, reconciliations and disclosures of the sampled months with the support filed behind them.

Analysis:
For two sampled months reconcile in full the support behind posted journals and completed reconciliations against the register; a workbook behind a posted entry and on no register row is a completeness exception.
Sample fifteen registered files weighted to those feeding material accounts and to files carrying manual inputs.
For each sampled file compare the hash of the retained version against the file in use, re-perform one calculated column, and agree two manual inputs to the documents cited for them.
Test each file's permission export against the named writer set, and against the leavers recorded for the period.
Set the date of each formula check against the date the file was last changed.

Output:
Reconciliation of posted support to the register, naming files relied upon but never registered and the accounts they reached.
Sample results stating hash mismatches found, formula differences and the effect of each on the figure reported.
Permission exceptions listing writers outside the named set and leavers who kept access after their last day.
Statement of the population and sample sizes with the date each extract was drawn.

title.en: Enumerate the files whose output reaches a reported figure

description.en: Build the population by following support backwards from posted entries, because the files that matter are found in the working papers behind a number rather than in a survey of what people keep on a drive.

text.en: Follow each key control's support back to the file that produced its numbers.
Include files that only reformat system output if a figure is edited inside them.
Name the owner and the consuming control for each file the walk turns up.
Exclude files whose output is re-derived in the system before use, and say why.
Cross-reference files fed by a key report to that report's register entry.

title.en: Restrict write access on registered files to their named holders

description.en: Put the files somewhere the permissions can be exported and the calculation cells cannot be typed over, so the restriction becomes a testable fact rather than an understanding among colleagues.

text.en: Move registered files to a location whose permissions can be exported.
Grant write access to the owner and the named preparers, read access to the rest.
Protect the calculation cells so an input cannot overwrite a formula.
Include the file store's permission group in the periodic access review population.
Export the permission list as the artefact that shows the restriction is real.

title.en: Stamp the period's file as a retained version before its figures are used

description.en: Fix what was actually relied upon: the closed file goes into the evidence library where its hash and version number make a later substitution visible instead of arguable.

evidenceHint.en: The retained workbook in the evidence library with its sha256 and version number, alongside the agreed manual inputs and the column re-performed for that period.

text.en: Upload the closed file as Evidence against the control it supports.
Read back the FileRecord sha256 so the bytes relied upon are fixed.
Agree each manual input to the document that is cited as its source.
Re-perform one calculated column and compare it to the figure reported.
Replace a superseded file through the evidence version chain, not a second row.

title.en: Trace posted entries back to the register of user-built files

description.en: Test the register from the accounting records rather than from itself, and check that the file behind a posted entry is the version the evidence library holds for that period.

text.en: Sample journal entries and reconciliations whose support is a workbook.
Identify supporting files that appear on no row of the register.
Compare the file behind the entry against the version retained as Evidence.
Test the permission export against the leavers recorded for the period.
Report unregistered files with the accounts their figures reached.

templates.title: Policy framework approved with defined ownership
templates.description: The set of written policies through which control activities are carried into practice, each approved by someone with authority over its subject and held by one named owner.
templates.objective: To ensure every policy the control framework leans on is approved by someone with authority over its subject and carries one named owner accountable for keeping it current.
templates.successCriteria:
The register holds a row for every policy a key control relies on, naming its owner, its audience and the controls it deploys.
Each row resolves to a published version whose approval record names the approver and the date decided.
Every approver holds authority over that policy's subject under the delegation schedule, and decided before the version reached its audience.
A control stating it is deployed through a policy resolves to a register row, not to a document a team holds privately.
Policies whose owner has left or changed role surface as exceptions carrying a date.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export the policy register as at period end, giving owner, audience, status and current version for every policy.
Obtain the approval decision held against each current version, naming the requester, the approver and the date.
Obtain the delegation schedule showing who may approve a policy on each subject.
Export the policy-to-control links for the controls inside the reporting scope.
Obtain the staff roster and the leaver and mover lists covering the period.

Analysis:
Population is every policy in the register at period end. Test all of them for a named owner, a stated audience and a current version, since a sample cannot show an omission.
Sample 15 policies weighted towards those deploying key controls, and trace each to the decision held against the version now published.
Set each approver against the delegation schedule and judge whether that subject was theirs to approve.
Compare the decision date against the date the version was released to its audience.
Match every named owner to the roster, and to the leaver and mover lists.

Output:
A register exception list naming policies without an owner, an audience or an approved current version.
A sample result stating, per policy tested, the approver, the authority relied on and the days between decision and release.
A list of in-scope controls whose stated policy resolves to no register row.

title.en: Trace each key control to the policy that carries it

description.en: Walk from the control register into the policy library so the framework's boundary is drawn from the controls that depend on it, rather than from whichever documents happen to exist.

text.en: Pull the key controls in the reporting scope and note which of them name a policy behind them.
Open the policy library and match each named policy to a real record, marking those that resolve to nothing.
Add a row for any policy staff already follow that the library does not yet hold.
Mark the controls whose policy sits outside the library, such as a team wiki page or a shared drive.
Agree the resulting policy set with the control owners before ownership is assigned.

title.en: Assign each policy to a named owner and a defined audience

description.en: Give every policy record an accountable individual and the population it binds, using the fields the policy module already carries rather than a spreadsheet kept beside it.

text.en: Name one individual as owner on each policy record, not a team mailbox or a job family.
State the audience the policy binds, separating employees, contractors and third parties where they differ.
Link each policy to the controls it deploys so the dependency is navigable from either side.
Set the review frequency on the record so the next review date is computed rather than remembered.
Note the approval authority the subject demands, taken from the delegation schedule.

title.en: Put each new or changed policy through approval before it is issued

description.en: Publish the text as a version, obtain a recorded decision against that version, and release it to the audience only afterwards, so nobody is bound by a document nobody approved.

evidenceHint.en: The published version record and the decision held against it, naming who approved, on what date, and which version number was then released to the audience.

text.en: Publish the drafted text as a new policy version carrying a change summary against the version it replaces.
Raise the approval request against that version and route it to the authority the subject demands.
Capture the approver's decision, date and comment on the version itself, not in an email thread.
Release the version to its audience only once the decision is recorded as approved.
Retire the superseded version so the library returns only the text now in force.

title.en: Reconcile the register's named owners to the current roster

description.en: Test the ownership half of the framework by putting every named owner against the staff roster and the leaver list, since an owner who has left is the ordinary way a policy goes stale.

text.en: Export the register with the owner named against each policy as at the review date.
Match each owner to the roster, and to the leaver and mover lists for the period.
Raise an exception for every policy whose owner has left, moved on or cannot be identified.
Reassign each exception to a successor and record the date the handover took effect.
Report the count of unowned policies beside the size of the register that produced it.

templates.title: Policies distributed and attestation obtained
templates.description: The route by which a policy reaches the people it binds, with each person's attestation recorded against the specific version they were asked to follow.
templates.objective: To ensure each policy in force reaches everyone it binds and that their attestation is recorded against the exact version they were asked to follow, not the policy in general.
templates.successCriteria:
Every policy in force defines its audience by a rule the roster can be run against, rather than by a list typed once.
Each person the rule returns holds an assignment naming the version currently in force.
Attestations recorded in the period resolve to a person on the roster and to a version published on or before the date given.
Outstanding items are readable per policy with an age, and those past the deadline carry a dated referral.
A republished version that changes an obligation raises fresh assignments instead of inheriting the previous receipts.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export, per policy in force, the audience rule and the assignment list generated from it.
Export the attestation records for the period, each naming the person, the version and the timestamp.
Obtain the staff roster with joiner and mover dates covering the period.
Obtain the outstanding report and the referrals raised on items past their deadline.
Obtain the version history for the policies republished during the period.

Analysis:
Population is every person the audience rules return at period end. Reconcile the assignment lists against that population in full, because an omitted person appears in no sample of those who responded.
Sample 25 attestations spread across at least five policies and weighted to those deploying key controls, and confirm each names the version in force on the date attested.
Take the period's joiners and movers as a second population and test whether an assignment was raised within the stated window of their entering the audience.
Age each open item against its deadline and match it to a referral.
For each republished version, determine whether prior receipts were carried over or fresh assignments raised.

Output:
A per-policy completion rate stating the denominator used and the date it was drawn.
An exception list of people inside an audience holding no assignment, and of attestations naming a superseded version.
A findings note on joiners who performed a policy's duties before attesting to it.

title.en: Express each policy's audience as a rule over roles and units

description.en: Decide who a policy binds by a rule that can be run against the roster, so the audience re-derives itself as people join and move instead of ageing from the day it was typed.

text.en: State, per policy, the roles, units and contract types that fall inside its audience.
Run the rule against the current roster and read the population it returns.
Compare that population against who actually performs the controls the policy deploys.
Settle the treatment of contractors and secondees, who sit outside the employee roster.
Hold the rule against the policy record so the same rule produces the next campaign.

title.en: Bind the current version to everyone the audience rule returns

description.en: Create the acknowledgement assignments from the rule's output against the version in force, so the requirement is held per person and the outstanding list can be read off rather than reconstructed.

text.en: Raise an acknowledgement assignment for each person the rule returns, against the published version.
Set the deadline the assignment must be met by, and state where that deadline came from.
Check the assignment count against the population the rule returned and explain any difference.
Send the request through the policy module so the record and the notification cannot diverge.
Confirm each assignment names a version number rather than the policy alone.

title.en: Raise an assignment when a joiner or mover enters an audience

description.en: Catch the people who arrive between campaigns, since someone performing a control before attesting to the policy behind it is exactly the gap a period-end completion rate hides.

evidenceHint.en: The joiner and mover feed for the period set beside the assignment created for each one, showing the days between entering an audience and the requirement being raised.

text.en: Take the joiner and mover feed at the agreed interval and re-run each policy's audience rule.
Raise assignments for people who entered an audience since the rule last ran.
Withdraw assignments for people who left an audience, recording why they were withdrawn.
Hold a joiner to the onboarding deadline rather than waiting for the next campaign date.
Note any person who performed the policy's duties before their assignment existed.

title.en: Refer unanswered assignments to the manager once the deadline passes

description.en: Turn an outstanding list into a decision with a name against it, because an attestation campaign carrying no escalation arm closes every period at the same incomplete rate.

evidenceHint.en: The outstanding report per policy showing the age of each open item, with the referrals sent to line managers, the date each was raised and how it was resolved.

text.en: Read the outstanding list per policy and age each open item against its deadline.
Refer items past the deadline to the person's line manager, naming the policy and version.
Record the resolution of each referral, including a refusal and the reason given for it.
Escalate a refusal on a policy deploying a key control to that control's owner.
Close the campaign with a stated count of items never answered.

title.en: Recompute the completion rate on a freshly drawn audience

description.en: Re-derive the denominator at the review date and recompute the rate against it, since a figure quoted on the population captured when the campaign opened flatters itself.

text.en: Re-run each audience rule at the review date and take the population it returns now.
Recompute the rate against that population rather than the campaign's original list.
Test a sample of recorded attestations back to the version in force on the date given.
Identify attestations recorded against a version that had already been superseded.
Report both rates side by side with the date each denominator was drawn.

templates.title: Policies reviewed and reapproved on a defined cycle
templates.description: The periodic re-examination of each policy at an interval set for its subject, with the reviewer's conclusion recorded and a fresh approval obtained wherever the text moved.
templates.objective: To ensure every policy is re-examined at the interval its subject warrants, with the reviewer's conclusion recorded even where the text was left unchanged and re-approved where it moved.
templates.successCriteria:
Every policy carries a review interval and a next-review date computed from it, not an interval asserted in the text alone.
Each review in the period names its reviewer, the date decided and the conclusion, including a conclusion of no change.
A review that altered an obligation produced a new version with its own approval, not an edit to the version already in force.
Policies past their next-review date appear on a due list with the days elapsed and a dated owner action against each.
Intervals differ across the register in a way the subjects explain, rather than every policy sitting on twelve months.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export the register showing review interval, last-reviewed date and next-review date for every policy in force.
Obtain the review records completed in the period, each naming reviewer, date and conclusion.
Obtain the version history for the policies whose review concluded that a change was needed.
Obtain the approval decisions held against those new versions.
Obtain the overdue report as at period end and the actions recorded against each row.

Analysis:
Population is every policy in force at period end. Recompute last-reviewed plus interval across all of them and identify rows whose stored due date does not follow.
Sample 12 reviews from the period, weighted towards the policies deploying key controls, and confirm each carries a conclusion rather than only a date.
For every review concluding a change, trace through to the new version and confirm its approval post-dates the review.
Age each overdue row at period end and determine whether the recorded action pre-dates or follows the due date.
Set the intervals against the subjects they cover and challenge a uniform interval applied with no reasoning behind it.

Output:
A due-and-overdue schedule as at period end giving the days elapsed per policy.
A sample result stating reviewer, conclusion and, where the text moved, the version and approval that followed.
An exception list of stored due dates that do not follow from the interval and last review recorded.

title.en: Set the review interval each policy's subject warrants

description.en: Decide how often a policy has to be looked at from how fast its subject moves, instead of putting the whole register on one twelve-month cycle nobody chose deliberately.

text.en: Group the register by subject and note how often the rules under each subject move.
Give a shorter interval to policies whose process, system or regulation changes inside a year.
State the reasoning behind each interval so a reviewer can challenge it later.
Agree the intervals with the policy owners who will have to meet them.

title.en: Stamp the interval and next-review date onto every policy record

description.en: Put the agreed interval into the field that drives the due date, so the schedule computes itself from the last completed review rather than living in somebody's calendar.

text.en: Record the review frequency in days on each policy record, matching the agreed interval.
Set the last-reviewed date from evidence of the most recent completed review.
Confirm the due date the record computes matches the interval agreed for that policy.
Correct records whose stored due date does not follow from the interval and last review.
Draw the coming year's due schedule from the register itself, not from a separate tracker.

title.en: Conclude each policy falling due, including where nothing changed

description.en: Work the quarter's due list to a recorded judgement per policy, because a review nobody wrote down is indistinguishable afterwards from a review that never happened at all.

evidenceHint.en: The quarter's due list with the review held against each policy on it, giving the reviewer, the date decided, the conclusion reached and the version raised where one followed.

text.en: Draw the policies whose next-review date falls inside the quarter.
Read each against the process it now describes and the controls it deploys.
Record the conclusion, the reviewer and the date even where the text is left alone.
Stamp the reviewed date so the next due date recomputes from this review.
Refer a policy the owner cannot reach inside the quarter to the register's owner.

title.en: Publish and re-approve the text a review found must change

description.en: Carry a review that found a change through the same route a new policy takes, so the audience attests to the text they must now follow rather than to the one it replaced.

evidenceHint.en: The new version with its change summary, the approval decision recorded against that version, and the assignments raised for its audience after publication.

text.en: Publish the revised text as a new version whose change summary names what moved.
Obtain approval against the new version rather than amending the one already approved.
Raise fresh acknowledgement assignments wherever the change alters what someone must do.
Leave the prior version's receipts attached to the version they were given for.
Tell the owners of the controls the policy deploys that the text underneath them moved.

title.en: Challenge intervals that outlast the subjects they were set for

description.en: Look back across the year at whether the cycle is calibrated: a policy amended between two scheduled reviews was on too long an interval, and one concluding no change every time may be on too short one.

text.en: Compare each policy's interval against the number of times its text moved in the year.
Shorten the interval on policies amended between two scheduled reviews.
Question an interval that has not moved since the register was first built.
Age the overdue rows at year end and report the days elapsed against each policy.
Put the revised intervals to the approver who set the original cycle.

templates.title: Inventory of ICFR-relevant service organizations
templates.description: Providers whose processing reaches a financial statement account are identified, held on the vendor register with the process and accounts they touch, and kept complete as services are taken on and dropped.
templates.objective: To ensure every service organization whose processing reaches a financial statement account sits on the vendor register with the process it serves and the assurance relied on recorded on it.
templates.successCriteria:
Every provider that processes, hosts or reports transactions reaching a financial statement account holds a vendor record naming the process and accounts it touches.
Each in-scope vendor record carries a criticality tier, a named business owner and the assurance route relied on.
The register reconciles to the payables population and the application inventory, and additions arising are dated.
A provider taken out of ICFR scope carries a written basis on its record rather than an implied one.
Sub-service organizations behind a registered provider are carried on the register in their own right.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the vendor register exported at period end, filtered to the records flagged ICFR-relevant - the population this control is tested against.
Collect the accounts payable ledger for the period and the application inventory, the two sources an unregistered provider is found from.
Retrieve the criticality tier, business owner and assurance route recorded on each in-scope record.
Gather the scoping notes for providers assessed and left out of ICFR scope during the period.
Obtain the contracts and service descriptions naming sub-service organizations behind registered providers.

Analysis:
Reconcile the payables ledger in full against the register, isolating every supplier paid for a service that touches a ledger balance.
Sample twelve in-scope records across the criticality tiers and test whether the process and accounts named on each match the service actually received.
Re-perform the relevance judgement on every exclusion recorded in the period rather than on a sample, since each one removes a provider from oversight entirely.
Trace the sub-service organizations named in sampled contracts through to a register entry of their own.
Compare the register against the prior period to find providers that left it with no basis recorded.

Output:
Reconciliation of payables and the application inventory to the register, naming every provider found on neither.
Schedule of the sampled records showing process, accounts, tier, owner and assurance route, with the fields left blank.
Statement of whether each exclusion carries a basis, and which were re-performed to a different conclusion.
List of sub-service organizations relied on but absent from the register.

title.en: Delimit which outsourced services reach a reported balance

description.en: Decide process by process which providers can move a financial statement account and which merely supply the business, so the register is scoped by exposure rather than by spend.

text.en: Name every process outsourced in whole or in part, from payroll and billing to custody and hosting.
Trace each outsourced process through to the accounts and assertions it can move.
Set the test that separates an ICFR-relevant provider from one touching no reported balance.
Record the relevance decision and its basis on each vendor record, exclusions included.

title.en: Populate the register from payables, payroll and the application inventory

description.en: Build the first complete population from the sources that show money leaving and finance data moving, rather than from the list procurement happens to hold.

text.en: Pull the supplier population from the accounts payable ledger for the whole period.
Add the hosted applications through which finance data is processed, stored or reported.
Open a vendor record for each provider that has none, naming its business owner.
Tag each record with a criticality tier and the assurance route that tier demands.

title.en: Register a new provider before it processes its first transaction

description.en: Catch the provider at onboarding, while the contract and the service description are in hand, instead of at the year-end scoping exercise when nobody recalls what was agreed.

evidenceHint.en: The quarter's register additions, each showing the date its record was opened against the date the service went live.

text.en: Take the quarter's executed contracts and new suppliers as the arrival list.
Open the vendor record with process, accounts, owner and tier before go-live.
Attach the contract and service description to the record as vendor documents.
Escalate any provider already processing without a record to the control owner.

title.en: Reconcile the register to what the ledger actually paid for

description.en: Test completeness from outside the register: start from the payments made and the access granted, then see which providers the register never heard of.

text.en: Compare the payables population against the register and list what appears on neither.
Challenge exclusions where the service description contradicts the stated basis.
Check that sub-service organizations named in reports hold records of their own.
Refer unresolved gaps to the control owner with a date for closure.

templates.title: SOC 1 or equivalent reports obtained and reviewed
templates.description: An attestation report covering each relied-upon service is obtained for the whole reporting period, attached to the vendor record, and read against what the organization actually relies on.
templates.objective: To ensure an attestation report covering each provider's relied-upon services and the whole reporting period is obtained, read against that reliance, and concluded on in writing.
templates.successCriteria:
Each provider whose tier demands assurance has a current report on its vendor record, the period covered held in its validity dates.
The report's scope covers the services actually relied on, and any service outside that scope is named.
A dated review note per report records the opinion type, the deviations disclosed and the conclusion for reporting.
The gap between the report period end and the year end is covered by a bridge letter or by procedures performed here.
Sub-service organizations carved out of a report are identified, and assurance over each is obtained or its absence accepted.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of in-scope providers whose criticality tier demands an attestation report - the population, from which every critical provider and a sample of eight others are tested.
Collect the reports attached to those vendor records, with the validity dates recorded against each document.
Retrieve the dated review note behind each report and the bridge letter covering the gap period.
Gather the service descriptions or contracts stating what each provider actually performs.
Obtain the register of sub-service organizations carved out of the reports collected.

Analysis:
Compare each report's period against the organization's financial year and measure the uncovered days.
Set the scope section of each sampled report against the service description to find reliance the report never examined.
Read every disclosed testing deviation in the sampled reports and check it appears in the review note rather than only in the report.
Confirm the review note carries a date, an author and a conclusion expressed for financial reporting, not a filing stamp.
For carved-out sub-service organizations, trace through to a second report or to a recorded acceptance of the gap.

Output:
Schedule of the population showing report held, period covered, uncovered days and bridge letter status.
List of relied-upon services falling outside the scope of the report obtained for them.
Statement of which sampled reports carry a review note and which were filed unread.
List of carved-out sub-service organizations with no assurance and no recorded acceptance.

title.en: Determine which providers owe a report and what would satisfy it

description.en: Fix the assurance expectation per provider before the reporting season: which need a type 2 attestation, which are met by other evidence, and which the organization will test for itself.

text.en: Take the ICFR-relevant vendor records as the population that owes assurance.
State per criticality tier what report or alternative evidence will be accepted.
Name the services relied on that the report has to cover for each provider.
Record the accepted alternative where no attestation report exists at all.

title.en: Schedule each request against the provider's own reporting period

description.en: Turn that expectation into dates: when each report is published, when it is chased, and how the gap to the organization's year end will be covered.

text.en: Record each provider's report period end and its usual publication date.
Set the request and chase dates against the close calendar for the year.
Name the vendor contact the request will be sent to for each provider.
Decide per provider whether a bridge letter is needed for the gap period.

title.en: Attach the arriving report to its vendor record with the period it covers
