description.en: File the report where the oversight actually lives, so its coverage period is visible on the record instead of buried in somebody's mailbox.

evidenceHint.en: The report filed as a vendor document, its validity dates set to the coverage period, with the bridge letter beside it.

text.en: Load the report against its vendor record as an attestation document.
Set the document validity dates to the period the report covers.
Attach the bridge letter covering the gap to the organization's year end.
Chase a provider whose report has not arrived by its scheduled date.

title.en: Examine the report against the services actually relied on

description.en: Do the reading this control exists to force: a report on file proves only that somebody asked for it, and an unread qualification is the same as no report at all.

evidenceHint.en: The dated review note per report, recording opinion type, scope match, disclosed deviations and the conclusion for financial reporting.

text.en: Compare the services described in the report against those the process relies on.
Record the opinion type and read the auditor's testing deviations in full.
Identify sub-service organizations carved out and what assurance covers them.
Write the conclusion for financial reporting, naming what it does not cover.

title.en: Challenge reports filed with no reader and no conclusion

description.en: Look for the failure the control exists to catch - a report collected, filed and never read - and for conclusions that stop short of naming an effect on the accounts.

text.en: Select the period's reports and look for a dated review note behind each.
Test whether a report's coverage period leaves the year end uncovered.
Judge whether the conclusion addresses the services the process actually uses.
Raise unread reports with the control owner and set a date for reading them.

templates.title: Complementary user entity controls identified and tested
templates.description: The controls an attestation report assumes the organization performs are extracted from the report, matched to a named internal control and owner, and tested for operating effectiveness over the report's own period.
templates.objective: To ensure the controls a service auditor's report assumes the organization performs are owned internally and tested for operating effectiveness, not merely listed and filed.
templates.successCriteria:
Every complementary user entity control stated in a relied-upon report is extracted into a list, cited to the section it came from.
Each extracted item is matched to a named internal control, its owner and its frequency, or recorded as having nothing behind it.
Operating effectiveness is tested over a sample drawn from the report's coverage period, with the sample size and basis recorded.
An item that fails its test or has nothing behind it is opened as a deficiency with an owner and a due date.
The extracted list is redrawn when a new report is issued or the way the service is consumed changes.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the extracted list of complementary user entity controls for every report relied on in the period - the population this control is tested against.
Collect the reports themselves, so the extraction can be checked back to the section it claims to come from.
Retrieve the mapping of each extracted item to an internal control, with owner and frequency.
Gather the test sheets: population, sample selected, items tested, exceptions and conclusion.
Obtain the deficiency entries opened for unowned items and failed tests, with their due dates.

Analysis:
Re-extract the user entity control section of three reports in full and compare against the list, since an omission here is invisible downstream.
Trace every extracted item to a mapped control and treat an unmapped item as a gap rather than as pending.
For eight mapped controls spanning at least three providers, re-perform two sample items each and compare the conclusion reached.
Check each sample was drawn from the report's coverage period rather than from the weeks before testing.
Compare the deficiency log against the failed and unowned items to find failures that never became deficiencies.

Output:
Schedule of extracted items per report showing mapped control, owner, frequency and test conclusion.
List of assumed controls with nothing behind them, and how long each has stood unowned.
Re-performance results for the eight controls tested, naming any conclusion not supported by the evidence.
Statement of whether the sample periods align to the reports, with the exceptions listed.

title.en: Extract the user entity controls each report assumes of us

description.en: Pull the assumptions out of the report and into a list that can be owned, citing each back to the section it came from so a reader can check rather than trust it.

text.en: Work through each report's user entity control section and list every assumption stated.
Cite each extracted item to the report, its version and the section it sits in.
Discard assumptions covering services this organization does not rely on.
Carry the surviving list onto the vendor record of the provider concerned.

title.en: Match each assumed control to an owner and a control that operates here

description.en: Turn an assumption into something testable: a named internal control, the individual who operates it and how often it runs, or an explicit statement that nothing behind it exists.

text.en: Map each assumption to a control in the register that already performs it.
Name the individual who operates that control and the frequency it runs at.
Mark assumptions with nothing behind them as gaps rather than as covered.
Agree the test approach and the sample basis for each matched control.

title.en: Test a sample drawn from the report's own coverage period

description.en: Do the part most often skipped: obtain evidence that the assumed control operated, across the period the service auditor relied on it operating.

evidenceHint.en: The test sheet per assumed control: population, sample selected, dates tested, exceptions found and the effectiveness conclusion.

text.en: Draw the population for each matched control over the period the report covers.
Select the sample on a stated basis and record why that size is sufficient.
Examine each item and record the exceptions rather than a pass rate alone.
Conclude in writing on whether the assumed control operated effectively.

title.en: Raise every unowned or failed assumption as a deficiency

description.en: Close the loop that identification leaves open, so an assumption nobody performs becomes a tracked deficiency with a date instead of another line in a list.

evidenceHint.en: The deficiency entries opened this cycle, each naming the assumption behind it, a remediation owner and a due date.

text.en: Open a deficiency for each assumption with no control or a failed test.
Assess the accounts and assertions that failure leaves exposed to misstatement.
Assign a remediation owner and a due date proportionate to that exposure.
Report the open items in the period's control reporting to the committee.

title.en: Judge whether the assumption list still fits the service taken

description.en: Re-read the list against how the service is consumed now, since a changed configuration can retire an assumption or introduce one nobody has extracted yet.

text.en: Compare this year's report section against the list drawn from last year's.
Identify changes in how the service is consumed since the list was drawn.
Retire assumptions that no longer apply, recording why each was dropped.
Add assumptions the current report states that the list never carried.

templates.title: Service organization report exceptions remediated
templates.description: Deviations, qualifications and failed user entity controls disclosed by a service organization's report are graded for their effect on the accounts, taken back to the provider with a date, and covered here until they close.
templates.objective: To ensure a deviation disclosed by a service organization's report is graded for its effect on the accounts, pursued to a dated fix, and covered by a procedure here while it stands.
templates.successCriteria:
Every deviation, qualification and exception disclosed by a report relied on is recorded and graded against the accounts it can misstate.
A graded deviation is put to the provider in writing and carries a remediation owner and a completion date.
Where reliance continues, a compensating procedure is performed here for each period the deviation remains open, and its output is kept.
Exceptions still open at the year-end conclusion are taken to management and the audit committee with their exposure stated.
Closure is evidenced by the following period's report rather than by the provider's own confirmation.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the exception schedule for the period - every deviation, qualification and failed user entity control disclosed by the reports relied on, which is the population tested.
Collect the reports themselves, so the schedule can be checked for omissions against what was disclosed.
Retrieve the correspondence putting each graded deviation to the provider, with the remediation plan returned.
Gather the compensating procedures performed while exceptions stood open, with their dated output.
Obtain the papers taken to management and the audit committee, and the following period's reports.

Analysis:
Re-read the deviations section of every report in full against the schedule, as an omitted exception is the failure with no downstream trace.
Sample six graded deviations across providers and test whether the grading follows the materiality thresholds set for the period.
For each sampled item still open, confirm the compensating procedure was performed in every period it was required, not only the first.
Compare the closure dates claimed with the results in the following period's report and note deviations that repeat.
Trace items open at year end into the committee papers and into the conclusion reached on internal control.

Output:
Reconciliation of report disclosures to the exception schedule, naming what never reached it.
Grading results for the six sampled deviations, with those graded below the threshold the accounts suggest.
Schedule of compensating procedures due and performed per open exception, with the periods missed.
List of deviations repeating in the following report despite a recorded closure.

title.en: Grade each disclosed deviation by the account it can misstate

description.en: Separate the deviations that reach the financial statements from those that do not, so effort follows exposure rather than the order in which the report happened to list them.

text.en: Collect every exception, qualification and deviation the period's reports disclosed.
Trace each one through to the service relied on and the accounts behind it.
Rate the exposure against the materiality thresholds already set for the period.
Discard deviations touching services this organization does not consume.

title.en: Agree a dated fix with the provider through its contract owner

description.en: Take the exception back to the provider through the relationship that can actually move it, and come away with a date rather than an assurance that it is being looked at.

text.en: Put the graded exceptions to the provider's named contact in writing.
Obtain a remediation plan carrying an owner and a completion date.
Record the plan against the vendor record as a document, not in an inbox.
Escalate to the contract owner where no date is offered at all.

title.en: Run the compensating procedure for as long as the exception stands

description.en: Cover the exposure here while the provider's fix is outstanding, because reliance on the service carries on whether or not the deviation has been closed.

evidenceHint.en: The completed procedure for every period it was required, showing the items checked, the differences found and who performed it.

text.en: Design a procedure that detects what the failed provider control would have caught.
Perform it in each period the exception remains open and keep the output.
Record the differences found and follow every one to a resolution.
Stop the procedure only once the provider's fix has been evidenced.

title.en: Table unresolved exceptions before the year-end conclusion

description.en: Put the open items in front of the people who sign the assessment while there is still time to do something other than disclose them.

evidenceHint.en: The schedule taken to management and the audit committee, showing status, exposure and the procedure standing behind each open item.

text.en: Compile the open exceptions with exposure, owner and expected closure date.
State for each what compensating procedure is standing in the meantime.
Take the schedule to management and to the audit committee in session.
Minute the decisions reached on items that will not close before sign-off.

title.en: Verify the next report shows the deviation closed

description.en: Test the provider's claim against the only independent evidence there is, the following period's attestation, instead of against its own confirmation email.

text.en: Take the prior period's exception list into the new report's testing results.
Confirm each closed item is absent from the current period's deviations.
Reopen any exception the new report repeats, with the history attached.
Report repeat deviations as a provider performance matter, not a new finding.

templates.title: Code of conduct approved by the board and published
templates.description: The standards of conduct the organization holds itself to, approved at board level and made available to everyone bound by them.
templates.objective: To ensure the conduct standards the organization expects are fixed by a board-level decision and published to everyone bound by them, rather than asserted informally.
templates.successCriteria:
A current code of conduct exists with a recorded board or equivalent approval naming the version and the date it was agreed.
The published version matches the approved version exactly, with no undated or draft copy reachable to a reader.
Every population bound by the code has a route to the current version, including contractors, agency staff and directors.
A review cycle is defined, the last review fell within it, and the reviewer and outcome are recorded even where nothing changed.
Superseded versions are withdrawn from every location a reader could still reach them from.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current code of conduct and the minute or resolution recording its approval.
Obtain the publication location and the date the approved version was posted there.
Collect the distribution list or access route for each population bound by the code, including contractors.
Obtain the defined review cycle and the record of the most recent review.
Request any superseded versions still reachable to staff.

Analysis:
Compare the published document against the approved version to confirm they are the same text.
Set the approval date against the publication date to confirm publication followed approval.
Test whether each bound population has a route to the current version, not only permanent employees.
Compare the last review date against the stated cycle and judge whether the cycle has lapsed.
Inspect the publication location for superseded copies that a reader could mistake for current.

Output:
Record whether a current, approved and published code exists, naming its approval date and reviewer.
List any population bound by the code without a route to it.
State whether the review cycle is being met, and by how far it has lapsed if not.

title.en: Establish the conduct standards the organization will hold

description.en: Draft or confirm the code's content, covering the conduct areas the organization's activities actually expose it to rather than a generic template.

text.en: List the conduct areas the organization's operations expose it to, such as conflicts of interest, gifts, confidentiality and fair dealing.
Identify every population the code will bind, separating employees, contractors, temporary workers and directors.
Draft the code text against those areas, stating expected behaviour rather than aspirations.
Record which existing policies the code defers to, so an obligation is stated once rather than in several places.

title.en: Obtain board approval and record the decision

description.en: Take the code to the board or equivalent body and capture the approval as a dated record, since an unapproved code carries no authority.

text.en: Table the drafted code at the board or committee holding the approval authority.
Capture the approval in the minute, naming the version approved and the date it was agreed.
Record any changes the board required and confirm they are carried into the approved version.
File the approved version so the minute and the document can be tied together later.

title.en: Publish the approved code to every bound population

description.en: Put the approved version where each bound population can reach it, and remove earlier copies that could be mistaken for current.

evidenceHint.en: The publication location showing the approved version and its posting date, with the distribution route recorded for each bound population.

text.en: Publish the approved version to the intranet or handbook location staff are directed to.
Provide a route for contractors and temporary workers who do not have intranet access.
Withdraw superseded versions from every location where a reader could still reach them.
Record the posting date so publication can be shown to have followed approval.

title.en: Review the code against the defined cycle

description.en: Re-examine the code on its stated cycle and record the outcome, so a code nobody has revisited becomes visible as such.

text.en: Compare the last review date against the stated cycle and open the review when it falls due.
Assess whether the conduct areas covered still match the organization's activities and exposures.
Record the review outcome, including a decision that no change was needed, with the reviewer named.
Return the code for re-approval where the review changed its substance.

templates.title: Annual code of conduct acknowledgement obtained
templates.description: A yearly confirmation from every person bound by the code that they have read the version in force and accept the obligations it places on them.
templates.objective: To ensure every person bound by the code confirms each year that they have read the version in force and accept the obligations it places on them.
templates.successCriteria:
The population bound for the cycle is drawn from named source systems at a stated as-of date, with contractors and directors included.
Every receipt is attributable to a named individual, carries a date, and cites the version of the code in force.
Names still outstanding at the close of the cycle are listed with the escalation taken against each.
People joining after the cycle closed acknowledged the code inside the onboarding window set for them.
Refusals and qualified responses are held separately and routed to a named owner rather than counted as complete.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the acknowledgement register for the cycle as exported at the date of test.
Obtain the HR master list, the contractor and agency rosters and the director list as at the cycle's as-of date.
Collect the acknowledgement wording issued and the code version it referred to.
Obtain the reminder and escalation correspondence covering the outstanding population.
Collect the list of people who started after the cycle closed, with each start date.

Analysis:
Reconcile the register against the combined population sources and quantify people bound but never issued a request.
Sample 25 receipts spread across employees, contractors and directors, and test each for attribution, date and the code version cited.
Trace every name outstanding at close to the escalation taken, and judge whether it ended in a receipt, a refusal or nothing.
Test the whole joiner population against the onboarding window, measuring days from start date to receipt.
Inspect refusals and qualified responses for routing to a named owner rather than closure as complete.

Output:
Completion figure for the cycle expressed as receipts over the bound population, with the denominator named.
Schedule of people bound by the code holding no receipt, split by employee, contractor and director.
Exception list of receipts that are undated, unattributable or cite a superseded version of the code.
Statement of joiner timeliness naming those outside the window and by how many days.

title.en: Draw the population bound by the code for this cycle

description.en: Fix who must acknowledge this year from named source systems, and set the as-of date the population is measured at, so a completeness figure later has a denominator that can be defended.

text.en: Export the employee list from the HR system as at the cycle's as-of date, including people on leave.
Add contractors, agency and temporary workers from the procurement and agency rosters, which HR master data does not carry.
Add directors and officers, who are bound by the code but sit outside payroll reporting.
State the cut-off date after which a new starter is handled by the joiner route instead of this cycle.
Note any exclusion from the population with the reason for it and the person who approved it.

title.en: Prepare the acknowledgement statement and its issue route

description.en: Settle the words a person is agreeing to, tie them to the version of the code in force, and decide how the request reaches populations without a corporate mailbox.

text.en: Draft the statement so it covers reading the code, accepting its obligations and the duty to report a breach.
Bind the statement to the code version and date in force, so a later receipt shows what was accepted.
Configure the capture so each response carries the person's identity and a timestamp that cannot be edited.
Agree a paper or supervised route for contractors and site staff who hold no corporate mailbox.
Set the response window, the reminder dates and the point at which a name is escalated.

title.en: Collect receipts across the cycle and clear what is outstanding

description.en: Issue the request to the drawn population, work the reminder and escalation schedule, and bring every name to a receipt, a refusal or a recorded escalation.

evidenceHint.en: The acknowledgement register for the cycle showing each person, the date received and the code version accepted, alongside the closing list of names still unresolved.

text.en: Issue the request to every name in the drawn population and log the issue date against each.
Send reminders on the agreed dates and refresh the outstanding list after each pass.
Escalate names still outstanding at the end of the window to their line manager and capture the response.
Separate refusals and qualified responses, and route each to the named owner for handling.
Close the cycle with a dated completion figure stated over the population drawn at the start.

title.en: Capture joiner acknowledgements inside the onboarding window

description.en: Take the acknowledgement from people who join after the cycle has closed, as part of onboarding, rather than leaving them unbound until the next annual pass.

evidenceHint.en: The onboarding or induction record for each starter in the period, carrying the date the code was acknowledged set against that person's start date.

text.en: Place the acknowledgement step in the onboarding checklist so it falls in the joiner's first week.
Take the receipt against the code version in force on the joiner's start date.
Compare new starters against receipts each month to find joiners the onboarding route missed.
Escalate any joiner past the onboarding window to the hiring manager and note the outcome.
Feed joiner receipts into the register the annual cycle writes to, so one population view exists.

title.en: Reconcile receipts to the bound population and report the gap

description.en: Set the receipts collected against the population that was bound, quantify the shortfall by category, and put the result in front of the owner accountable for the code.

text.en: Match the register to the population source used at the start of the cycle, name by name.
Quantify people bound but never issued a request, apart from those issued and not responding.
Split the shortfall by employee, contractor and director, since each has a different route and owner.
Test a sample of receipts for attribution, date and the code version they cite.
Report the completion figure and the unresolved names to the code owner with a date for clearance.

templates.title: Code of conduct waivers and exceptions reviewed
templates.description: The record of departures from the code, showing who was permitted what, on whose authority and for how long, and the periodic examination of that record as a whole.
templates.objective: To ensure a departure from the code happens only with a stated reason, an approver holding the level set for that provision, and a fixed expiry, rather than by quiet practice.
templates.successCriteria:
Every departure granted in the period sits in one register, with the code provision it departs from named.
Each entry carries the requester, the business reason, the conditions attached and a firm expiry date.
The approver of each grant held the level set for that provision, and no grant was approved by the person it benefits.
Grants benefiting directors or executive officers were escalated to the audit committee or board, with the disclosure decision recorded.
Expired grants are closed or re-argued on their own record instead of running on unexamined.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the waiver register for the period, with the provision, approver, conditions and expiry on each entry.
Obtain the document setting which provisions admit a departure and the approval level reserved for each.
Collect the request and approval correspondence behind a sample of entries.
Obtain the audit committee or board papers covering grants to directors and executive officers.
Collect the gift, hospitality, outside-interest and related-party declarations logged in the period, as an independent source.

Analysis:
Trace declarations logged outside the register into it, to surface exceptions granted informally.
Sample 15 entries weighted towards senior grantees and test each approver against the level set for that provision.
Test whether any grant was approved by the person it benefits or by someone reporting to them.
Group the period's grants by provision, business unit and grantee, and judge whether a repeat signals a provision out of step with practice.
Compare expiry dates against current status to find grants still operating past their term.
Check each director and executive officer case against the escalation record and the disclosure decision taken.

Output:
Schedule of the period's grants by provision, naming the approver and their level against each.
List of exceptions found in the declarations but absent from the register.
Findings on self-approval, expired grants still running, and concentration by grantee or unit.
Statement of whether every senior case reached the audit committee, naming any that did not.

title.en: Define which code provisions admit a departure, and at what level

description.en: Separate the provisions where a documented exception is possible from those that admit none, and fix the approval level each requires before any request arrives.

text.en: Identify the code provisions where practice creates genuine exceptions, such as gifts, hospitality and outside interests.
Name the provisions that admit no exception at all, so a request against them is refused rather than negotiated.
Set the approval level per provision, reserving director and executive officer cases for the board or its committee.
Fix the fields every entry must carry, including the conditions attached and a firm expiry date.
State how long a grant may run before it has to be re-argued rather than rolled forward.

title.en: Open one register and pull informal approvals into it

description.en: Stand up a single record of departures from the code, and move approvals currently sitting in mailboxes and local files into it, so the period's population is complete.

text.en: Create the register with the agreed fields: requester, provision, reason, conditions, approver and expiry.
Search mailboxes and shared drives for approvals already given, and enter those still in force.
Publish the request route so a person seeking an exception lands in the register rather than an inbox.
Restrict who may edit a granted entry, and keep a trail of changes to its conditions or expiry.
Agree retention for closed entries, so a lapsed grant can still be examined after the fact.

title.en: Grant or refuse each request at the level set for it

description.en: Decide each request on the record, at the approval level its provision requires, with conditions and an expiry attached rather than an open-ended permission.

evidenceHint.en: The register entry behind each decision, carrying the provision departed from, the business reason, the approver and their level, the conditions imposed and the expiry date.

text.en: Check the request names the code provision it departs from and the business reason behind it.
Route it to the approval level set for that provision, and refuse where no exception is admitted.
Attach conditions and a firm expiry date to every grant rather than permitting it indefinitely.
Reject any decision taken by the person it benefits or by someone reporting to them.
Notify the requester of the decision in writing and file that notification against the entry.

title.en: Escalate departures held by directors and executive officers

description.en: Carry the small population of senior cases to the body that must approve and disclose them, because an exception for an officer is a governance matter rather than a management one.

evidenceHint.en: The audit committee or board paper for the period listing each grant to a director or executive officer, with the disclosure decision minuted against it.

text.en: Identify grants whose beneficiary is a director, an executive officer or a person close to one.
Prepare the paper naming the provision departed from, the reason given and the conditions imposed.
Take each case to the audit committee or board at its next meeting rather than at year end.
Minute the decision reached and any external disclosure obligation it triggers.
Feed the conditions the committee imposed back onto the entry, so the grant and its terms agree.

title.en: Examine the period's grants for pattern, concentration and drift

description.en: Read the register as a whole rather than case by case, since a provision departed from repeatedly is evidence about the code itself rather than about the person asking.

text.en: Group the period's entries by provision, business unit and beneficiary, and count the repeats.
Judge whether a provision departed from repeatedly should be redrafted instead of exempted each time.
Compare expiry dates against current status to find grants still operating past their term.
Test whether refusals appear at all, since a register holding none suggests a rubber stamp.
Put the findings to the code owner with the changes proposed and a date against each.

templates.title: Confidential reporting channel available and publicised
templates.description: A route for raising a concern that does not pass through the person the concern may be about, reachable by everyone the organization deals with and known to them.
templates.objective: To ensure a person who does not trust their own manager still has a confidential route for raising a concern, and can find that route without asking anyone for it.
templates.successCriteria:
At least one route reaches a recipient outside the reporter's management line and can be used without giving a name.
Every population the channel is meant to serve, including contractors, agency staff and suppliers, has a route stated in terms it can use.
The published contact details resolve to a live recipient, shown by a test submission made during the period.
A statement that retaliation is prohibited sits with the route and names who enforces it.
Awareness is measured rather than assumed, with a dated record of the last publicity cycle.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current description of every intake route, naming the recipient each one reaches and whether it accepts an anonymous report.
Obtain the publicity artefacts used in the period - intranet pages, posters, induction material, supplier terms and contractor packs.
Collect the test submissions made during the period, with the date each was raised and the date a recipient responded.
Request the retaliation statement as published and the name of the person accountable for enforcing it.
Obtain the vendor contract or standing instruction that keeps the channel available, including the hours and languages covered.

Analysis:
Trace each route from its published contact detail through to the recipient, and confirm at least one bypasses line management entirely.
Take every population the channel claims to serve as the population under test, and judge whether each has a route in a language and format it can use.
Re-perform a submission through the anonymous route and follow it to the point of receipt, checking that no identifying field is mandatory.
Compare the response times on the period's test submissions against the stated intake window.
Inspect publicity material against the current contact details to find any published route that no longer resolves.

Output:
Schedule of intake routes, the recipient of each, and whether anonymity survives as far as receipt.
List of populations with no usable route, with the reason recorded against each.
Statement of whether test submissions were answered inside the stated window, naming any that were not.
Record of publicity material still carrying stale or unreachable contact details.

title.en: Map the routes a concern can travel when the manager is its subject

description.en: Work out which existing escalation paths still run through the person a concern could name, and where a genuinely independent route has to sit.

text.en: Draw the current escalation paths from first report through to a decision maker.
Mark each path that passes through a line manager who could be the subject of the concern.
Name the populations the channel must serve, separating employees, contractors, agency staff and suppliers.
Decide which routes must accept an anonymous report and which may require a name.
Fix the intake window within which any route must reach a recipient.

title.en: Commission the intake channel and its independent recipient

description.en: Stand up the route itself: the mechanism a report arrives by, the person outside management who receives it, and the hours and languages it covers.

text.en: Select the intake mechanism, whether an external hotline, a web portal or a named postbox.
Appoint a recipient outside the management line, with a deputy for when they are conflicted.
Configure the intake form so that no field identifying the reporter is mandatory.
Agree the hours, languages and response window in the contract or standing instruction.
Restrict sight of arriving reports to the named recipient and the deputy.

title.en: Publicise the route to every population it is meant to serve

description.en: Put the contact details where each population will actually meet them, including people who never see the intranet, and keep the retaliation statement beside them.

evidenceHint.en: The publicity artefacts as displayed in the period - intranet page, induction pack, supplier terms and contractor notice - each showing the current contact details and its posting date.

text.en: Publish the contact details on the route staff are already directed to for policy.
Carry the same details into induction material and the annual code refresh.
Place the route in supplier terms and contractor packs for people outside the intranet.
Display the retaliation statement wherever the contact details appear.
Withdraw superseded contact details that would send a reporter to a dead recipient.
Measure whether staff and contractors can name the route when asked, and date the result.

title.en: Time an anonymous submission from sending to acknowledgement

description.en: Raise a controlled report through each live route, anonymously where the route allows it, and follow it to the point a recipient acknowledges receipt.

text.en: Raise a test report through each published route, including the anonymous one.
Time the interval from submission to a recipient's acknowledgement.
Check whether the anonymous submission stayed anonymous once it reached the case log.
Confirm the report reached a recipient outside the subject's management line.
Report any route that failed to resolve, with the date it was found broken.

templates.title: Reported concerns triaged, logged and assigned
templates.description: Every concern that arrives is captured on receipt, graded for seriousness, and handed to a handler who has no stake in how it ends.
templates.objective: To ensure every concern that arrives is captured on receipt, graded for seriousness and conflict, and handed to a handler who has no stake in how it ends.
templates.successCriteria:
Each concern received appears on the case log inside the stated intake window, whatever route carried it.
Every logged case holds a severity grade and the reason it was set, decided by someone not named in the report.
The assigned handler sits outside the subject's reporting line and outside the function involved, with that check on the case file.
The reporter is acknowledged, and an anonymous reporter is given a way to follow the case without identifying themselves.
Sight of case records is confined to the assigned handlers, evidenced by a system-produced access list.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the case log for the period, carrying the receipt date, route, grade and assigned handler on each entry.
Collect the raw intake records behind it - hotline transcripts, mailbox exports, portal submissions and notes of concerns raised in person.
Obtain the grading scheme in force and the conflict test applied before a handler is assigned.
Request the acknowledgement issued to reporters and the mechanism offered to an anonymous reporter to follow a case.
Obtain the system access list for case records as at the date of test.

Analysis:
Take every raw intake record in the period as the population and trace each into the case log, treating anything untraced as a concern that never reached triage.
Sample all cases graded high or naming a manager, plus a random sample of the remainder, and test each grade against the scheme.
For each sampled case, judge whether the handler sits outside the subject's reporting line and outside the function the concern touches.
Compare receipt dates against log dates to measure intake delay across the period.
Inspect the access list for anyone holding sight of a case they were never assigned, and for access left over from a closed one.

Output:
Reconciliation of raw intake records to logged cases, naming every concern that opened no case.
Schedule of sampled cases showing the grade set, the reason given, and whether it matched the scheme.
List of assignments where the handler was not independent, naming the relationship that compromised it.
Statement of intake delay for the period, naming the cases that exceeded the window.

title.en: Set the severity grades and the conflict test intake will apply

description.en: Decide in advance how a concern is graded and what disqualifies a proposed handler, so neither judgement is made for the first time while a live report waits.

text.en: Define the severity grades, with an example of a concern belonging in each.
State which grades demand a handler from outside the function involved.
Set out the conflict test a proposed handler must pass before assignment.
Fix the intake window within which a received concern must reach the log.
Name the deputy who grades a concern involving the usual grader.

title.en: Build the case log that holds a concern from receipt to closure

description.en: Create the record itself, with the fields triage depends on and visibility narrow enough that a concern about a manager does not reach that manager.

text.en: Create case fields for receipt date, route, grade, handler and closure.
Restrict record visibility to the assigned handler and the named deputy.
Add the independence check as a field completed before assignment is possible.
Generate a case reference an anonymous reporter can quote without giving a name.
Retain a history of grade changes so a later downgrade remains visible.

title.en: Triage each arriving concern and assign a handler clear of it

description.en: On the day a concern lands, open its case, grade it against the scheme, test the proposed handler for conflict, and close the loop with whoever raised it.

evidenceHint.en: The case log entry opened on receipt, showing the grade, the reason it was set, the completed independence check and the handler it was given to.

text.en: Open a case record on the day the concern arrives, whatever route brought it.
Grade the concern against the scheme and state the reason for that grade.
Apply the conflict test to the proposed handler and capture its result.
Acknowledge the reporter, using the case reference where no name was given.
Escalate a concern naming senior management outside the normal assignment path.

title.en: Sweep the intake records for concerns that never became cases

description.en: Test the intake seam from the other side: start from what arrived rather than from what was logged, because a concern suppressed at triage leaves no case behind.

text.en: Pull the period's hotline, mailbox and portal records as the intake population.
Trace each one into the case log and mark any concern that opened no case.
Re-grade a sample of closed cases against the scheme to find quiet downgrades.
Test assignments against the subject's reporting line for independence failures.
Report untraced concerns and failed independence checks with an owner against each.

templates.title: Investigation outcomes reported to the audit committee
templates.description: What the investigations concluded, carried to the body that can act when the subject sits above the people who would otherwise decide what gets reported.
templates.objective: To ensure the audit committee sees how reported concerns were concluded, including the matters touching the management who would otherwise decide what the committee hears.
templates.successCriteria:
Each committee cycle receives the period's case count by category and the disposition of every case closed since the last cycle.
A matter implicating senior management or the override of a control is presented on its own, not folded into a total.
The pack reaches the committee unedited by anyone named in a case it carries, shown by the preparer and approver names.
Cases open past the agreed target age are shown with their age and reason rather than held back until closure.
Actions the committee directs are carried forward, with their status appearing at the following cycle.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the committee pack and the minutes for every cycle falling in the period.
Obtain the case log as it stood at each cycle cutoff date, not as it stands today.
Collect the preparer, reviewer and approver record for each pack, with the date of each step.
Request the follow-up tracker holding the actions the committee directed and the status carried forward.
Obtain any matter escalated to the committee chair between cycles, with the date it was raised.

Analysis:
Take the case log at each cutoff as the population and reconcile its counts and dispositions to the figures the committee received.
Read the minutes for matters implicating senior management or control override, and test whether each was presented individually.
Check whether anyone named in a reported case appears in the preparation or approval chain of the pack that carries it.
Compare open cases against the agreed target age and judge whether ageing cases were shown or withheld until closure.
Trace every directed action into the following cycle's papers and confirm a status was reported against it.

Output:
Reconciliation of the case log to the reported figures at each cutoff, naming every difference.
Schedule of matters that met the individual-presentation rule, showing how each was actually presented.
Statement of whether any pack was prepared or approved by a person named in a case it carried.
List of directed actions with no status at the following cycle, and of aged cases never shown.

title.en: Settle with the committee what each cycle's paper must carry

description.en: Agree the content the committee needs in order to act: the counts it wants, the matters it insists on seeing individually, and the point at which it must be told between meetings.

text.en: Agree the case categories and counts the committee wants at each cycle.
Define which matters must be presented individually rather than inside a total.
Set the target age past which an open case must be shown to the committee.
Fix the threshold at which a matter goes to the chair between meetings.
Name who prepares, who approves, and who stands aside when named in a case.

title.en: Compile the cycle paper from the case log at its cutoff date

description.en: Draw the figures from the log as it stood at the cutoff rather than from recollection, and separate out the matters the committee agreed to see on their own.

text.en: Extract the case log as it stands at the agreed cutoff date.
Summarise closures by category, with the disposition reached on each.
Separate matters naming senior management or a control override for individual presentation.
Attach the ageing of cases still open past the agreed target.
Check the preparation chain against the names appearing in the cases carried.

title.en: Table the period's outcomes with the committee in session

description.en: Take the committee through what the investigations concluded, answer what it asks, and capture what it directs so the direction survives the meeting.

evidenceHint.en: The minutes of the cycle recording the papers tabled, the questions put and any action directed, together with the issued version of the pack they refer to.

text.en: Take the committee through the individually presented matters before the totals.
Answer questions on cases the committee asks to see in more detail.
Capture every action the committee directs, with an owner and a due date.
Offer a private session without executive management present.
Confirm the minutes reflect what was tabled and what was directed.

title.en: Escalate a matter naming senior management before the next cycle

description.en: Where a concern reaches the agreed threshold, the committee chair hears it when it is graded rather than at the next scheduled meeting, and not through the person it names.

evidenceHint.en: The dated escalation note to the committee chair, with the acknowledgement received and the case reference it relates to.

text.en: Judge the matter against the agreed escalation threshold on the day it is graded.
Notify the committee chair directly, without routing through the person named.
Capture the date, the recipient and what was disclosed at escalation.
Carry the matter into the next cycle's paper whether or not it has closed.

title.en: Reconcile what the committee was shown against the case log

description.en: Go back to the log at each cutoff and test the pack against it, because a report that quietly omits a case is indistinguishable from one with nothing to omit.

text.en: Re-extract the case log as at each cutoff used during the period.
Compare its counts and dispositions with the figures the committee received.
Identify matters that met the individual-presentation rule but appeared in a total.
Trace directed actions into the following cycle and note any carrying no status.
Report each difference to the committee chair with the reason it arose.

templates.title: Audit committee charter defines control oversight duties
templates.description: The written mandate under which the audit committee oversees financial reporting and internal control, setting out the duties it holds, the authority it may exercise and the access it is owed.
templates.objective: To ensure the committee's oversight of financial reporting and internal control rests on a written mandate that names its duties, authority and access, rather than on custom.
templates.successCriteria:
A board-approved charter is in force, carrying the adopting body and the date of adoption.
Its duties over financial reporting, internal control, internal audit and the external auditor are named, and distinct from duties held elsewhere on the board.
Authority to obtain records, to commission work at the company's cost and to sit without management is stated rather than implied.
Meeting frequency, quorum and the reporting line back to the board are fixed, and the period's meetings met them.
The charter was reviewed within its stated cycle, and each amendment carries a board approval predating its use.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the charter in force at the date of test and the board minute recording its adoption.
Obtain the population of committee meetings held in the period, with the agenda, papers and minutes of each.
Obtain the schedule of charter amendments made in the period and the approval recorded for each.
Obtain the terms of reference of the board's other committees, to test where duties overlap or fall between them.
Request the record of sessions held with the external auditor, internal audit and finance without management present.

Analysis:
Trace every duty the charter claims to an agenda item in the period, and identify the duties that were never reached.
For a sample of four meetings spanning the period, compare recorded attendance against the charter's quorum.
Compare the charter against the other committees' terms of reference and isolate any duty claimed twice or by nobody.
Test whether the stated authority to commission work and to sit without management was exercised at least once, or exists only on paper.
Check that each amendment was approved before the amended version was relied on.

Output:
Statement of whether a current board-approved charter is in force, naming its adoption date and version.
Schedule of charter duties against the meeting that discharged each, and those with no occurrence in the period.
List of duties overlapping another committee or held by none, with the body that should carry each.
Finding on whether meeting frequency and quorum were met, with each exception named by date.

title.en: Draft the oversight duties the committee will hold

description.en: Set out, before adoption, which financial reporting and internal control duties belong to this committee, what authority it needs to discharge them, and how often it must sit.

text.en: Enumerate the duties over financial reporting, internal control, internal audit and the external auditor that the committee is to hold.
Read the board's and other committees' terms of reference and mark every duty that would otherwise be claimed twice or by nobody.
State the authority the committee needs: access to records, the right to commission advisers, and sessions without management present.
Fix meeting frequency, quorum, the notice period for papers and the route by which the committee reports back to the board.
Circulate the draft to the external auditor and internal audit for comment on anything their work depends on.

title.en: Adopt the charter at board level and version the text

description.en: Put the drafted mandate to the board, capture the resolution that adopts it, and leave only one dated version in circulation afterwards.

text.en: Table the draft charter at a board meeting and have the adopting resolution recorded in the minute.
Stamp the adopted text with a version number and the date of the resolution that carried it.
Withdraw superseded versions from the board portal and from any handbook that reproduces the terms of reference.
Issue the adopted charter to committee members, the secretariat, internal audit and the external auditor.
Open an amendment log so a later change is approved on its own terms rather than absorbed into practice.

title.en: Plan the year's agenda against each charter duty

description.en: Turn the charter into a dated agenda plan, so every duty it claims has a meeting at which it is actually taken and can be shown to have been discharged.

evidenceHint.en: The annual agenda plan alongside the minutes of each meeting, showing which charter duty every item discharged and on what date.

text.en: Map each duty in the charter to the meeting in the year at which it will be taken.
Add standing items for the private sessions with the external auditor and with internal audit.
Issue papers no later than the notice period the charter sets, and capture the issue date.
Note against each minuted item which charter duty it discharged, so coverage can be read from the minutes.
Carry any duty not reached into the next meeting rather than letting it lapse for the year.

title.en: Re-read the charter against the year the committee had

description.en: Compare the mandate as written with the meetings actually held, and take any amendment the comparison justifies back to the board rather than letting practice drift from the text.

text.en: Set the period's agendas and minutes against the charter's list of duties and mark those never exercised.
Test attendance at each meeting against the quorum the charter requires and note every shortfall.
Identify duties the committee took on in practice that the charter does not give it.
Draft the amendments the comparison justifies, with the reason for each stated.
Take the amendments to the board for approval and date the version they adopt.

templates.title: Committee independence and financial expertise evaluated
templates.description: A determination, made against written criteria and corroborated against records the member does not control, of whether each committee member is independent and where the committee's financial reporting expertise sits.
templates.objective: To ensure each member's independence and the committee's financial reporting expertise are determined against stated criteria and evidence, rather than inferred from job titles.
templates.successCriteria:
Written independence criteria are adopted before they are applied, naming the relationships that disqualify a member.
Every person who served on the committee in the period has a signed declaration covering the whole of their service.
The determination for each member records the facts relied on, including for members judged not independent.
Financial reporting expertise is evidenced by qualification or role history against a named member, not asserted for the committee at large.
A relationship arising mid-period was declared and re-assessed within the stated window, not held over to the next annual cycle.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the written independence criteria in force and the date the board adopted them.
Obtain the population of members who served at any point in the period, with their appointment and resignation dates.
Collect each member's signed declaration and the determination recorded against it.
Obtain the related-party register, supplier master and payroll extract covering the period, as sources the member does not control.
Obtain the expertise assessment for the member relied on, with the qualification or role history behind it.

Analysis:
Test the whole member population rather than a sample - it is small enough that sampling would only weaken the conclusion - for a declaration spanning the full service period.
Compare declared interests against names appearing in the related-party register, supplier master and payroll extract, and raise anything present there but absent from the declaration.
Re-perform each determination against the written criteria and confirm the facts relied on are recorded, not just the conclusion.
Check that a member appointed during the period was assessed before their first meeting, and that any change in circumstance was re-assessed within the stated window.
Judge whether the financial expertise relied on is evidenced, and whether it rests on a single member with no successor.

Output:
Determination schedule for every member who served, naming the criteria applied and the outcome reached.
List of relationships found in corroborating records but missing from a declaration, with the member and the source.
Finding on whether financial reporting expertise is evidenced and how far it is concentrated.
Exceptions: members without a current declaration, and determinations carrying a conclusion but no supporting facts.

title.en: Determine which relationships disqualify a member from independence

description.en: Put in writing the relationships that cost a member their independent status, who rules on them and how quickly a change in circumstance must be re-assessed, so the test exists before anyone is measured by it.

text.en: Name the disqualifying relationships: recent employment, fees beyond director remuneration, cross-directorships, close family and material supplier or customer ties.
State any threshold in figures, so a borderline relationship is decided by the criterion rather than by judgement on the day.
Appoint the body that makes the determination and the person who assembles the facts it rules on.
Set the window within which a newly arising relationship must be declared and re-assessed.
Take the criteria to the board for adoption and date the version applied this cycle.

title.en: Build the declaration form and its corroborating sources

description.en: Turn the criteria into a form a member can answer, and secure access to the records that will be used to test each answer independently of the member.

text.en: Draft a declaration field for each criterion, so no criterion depends on the member volunteering it unprompted.
Identify the corroborating extracts to be used: related-party register, supplier master, payroll and share register.
Agree with the owner of each extract how and when it will be provided for the annual cycle.
Add fields capturing the service dates the declaration covers, so a part-year member is not tested for the wrong window.
Set the annual timetable, placing issue and return before the meeting at which determinations are made.

title.en: Obtain a signed declaration from everyone who served

description.en: Collect a dated declaration from each member covering their whole period of service, chasing the returns that do not come back rather than treating silence as a nil return.

evidenceHint.en: Signed and dated declarations for every person who sat on the committee in the period, each stating the service dates it covers.

text.en: Issue the form to each serving member ahead of the first meeting of the cycle.
Issue it separately to anyone appointed or retiring mid-period, covering only the months they served.
Chase outstanding returns and escalate a non-return to the committee chair before the determination meeting.
File each declaration with its signature date and the service window it covers.
Flag any answer that differs from last cycle's so the change is examined rather than filed.

title.en: Determine each member's status and where expertise sits

description.en: Rule on independence member by member against the criteria, test the answers against the corroborating extracts, and name the member whose background supplies the committee's financial reporting expertise.

text.en: Apply the criteria to each member in turn and write the facts the conclusion rests on, not the conclusion alone.
Run declared interests against the related-party register, supplier master and payroll extract and investigate every unexplained match.
Name the member whose qualification or role history supplies the financial reporting expertise, and attach the evidence.
Judge whether that expertise is concentrated in one person and say what happens if they leave.
Report the determinations to the board, identifying any member judged not independent and the relationship that decided it.

templates.title: Management reports control effectiveness to the committee
templates.description: Management's own periodic account to the committee of how the financial reporting controls are performing: testing completed against plan, the deficiencies found, their severity, and how far remediation has moved since the last account.
templates.objective: To ensure the committee is told, on a fixed cadence, how the financial reporting controls are performing and which deficiencies management already knows about.
templates.successCriteria:
A report reaches the committee for every scheduled meeting in the period, with any omission recorded and reasoned.
Each report states testing completed against plan, the deficiencies identified and the severity assigned to each.
Open deficiencies carry an owner, a due date and their age, so movement since the previous report can be read without recalculation.
The deficiencies in management's own log at the cut-off reconcile to those presented, and an item held back is explained on the face of the report.
Questions and requests minuted by the committee are answered in a later report, and those still open are aged.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the committee's meeting calendar for the period and the reporting pack issued for each meeting.
Obtain management's deficiency log as it stood at each reporting cut-off, which is the population the pack's completeness is measured against.
Obtain the control testing plan for the period and the record of testing actually completed.
Collect the minutes recording the committee's questions, challenges and requests.
Obtain the remediation tracker showing owner, due date and closure evidence for each open item.

Analysis:
Compare packs issued against the meeting calendar and identify any meeting that received no report.
Reconcile the deficiency log at each cut-off to the deficiencies presented, testing every item above the lowest severity and a sample of ten below it; an item in the log but not the pack is a reporting failure, not a formatting one.
Re-perform the severity assignment for a sample of ten deficiencies against the stated severity definitions.
Trace testing completed against the plan and confirm the pack reports coverage as well as outcome.
Trace each minuted committee request through to the report that answered it, and age those never answered.

Output:
Schedule of meetings against the pack issued, with the days between issue and meeting.
Reconciliation of the deficiency log to the deficiencies reported, naming every item that did not reach the committee.
Re-performed severity assessments, naming any deficiency presented below the severity its definition requires.
Ageing of open deficiencies and of unanswered committee requests, with the owner of each.

title.en: Settle the reporting cadence and the standing content it carries

description.en: Settle with the committee the contents of the periodic account - coverage against plan, deficiencies by severity, remediation ageing and management's conclusion - and the cut-off and cadence it arrives on.

text.en: Agree the sections the report must carry, including testing coverage against plan and management's own conclusion.
Adopt severity definitions, so a deficiency is graded by a written rule rather than by the preparer's tone.
Fix the reporting cut-off and the cadence against the committee's meeting calendar.
Set the lead time by which papers reach members, and what triggers an out-of-cycle report.
State that the deficiency log at the cut-off is the population the report must reconcile to.

title.en: Connect the deficiency log to the reporting pack

description.en: Make the pack a derived extract of the log rather than a separately written narrative, so completeness can be tested mechanically instead of taken on trust.

text.en: Designate one deficiency log as the source the pack is extracted from, and close any rival list.
Add owner, due date and date-identified fields to the log so ageing is computed, not typed.
Build the extract that produces the pack's deficiency schedule directly from the log at the cut-off.
Insert a reconciliation step between extract and issue, with a named reviewer signing it off.
Define how an item management proposes to hold back is marked, so it appears rather than disappears.

title.en: Compile and issue the pack ahead of each meeting

description.en: Produce the account for each scheduled meeting from the log at the cut-off, reconcile it before issue, and get it to members within the agreed lead time.

evidenceHint.en: The issued pack for each meeting with its issue date, the deficiency log extract it was drawn from, and the signed reconciliation between the two.

text.en: Extract the deficiency population from the log at the agreed cut-off date.
Reconcile the pack's schedule to that extract and resolve every difference before issue.
State testing completed against plan for the period, including tests not yet performed.
Age each open deficiency against its due date and show the movement since the previous pack.
Issue the pack to members within the lead time and record the date it went out.

title.en: Test whether what management knew reached the committee

description.en: Independently compare the deficiencies management held at each cut-off with those actually presented, and age the committee's own requests that have gone unanswered.

text.en: Take the deficiency log as it stood at each cut-off, from the system rather than from the pack.
Compare it against the deficiencies presented and list every item that did not reach the committee.
Re-grade a sample of deficiencies against the severity definitions and report any understatement.
Trace each minuted committee request to the report that answered it and age those still open.
Present the comparison to the committee directly, so the test of escalation is not reported by the party being tested.

templates.title: Organizational structure and reporting lines documented
templates.description: The units, roles and reporting lines through which management runs financial reporting, written down and carried forward as the organization reorganizes.
templates.objective: To ensure the units, roles and reporting lines carrying financial reporting work are written down and current, so every activity traces to a person answerable for it.
templates.successCriteria:
A current structure shows every unit inside the financial reporting boundary, including shared service centres and activity run by an outside provider.
Each in-scope unit names the individual accountable for its financial reporting activity and the manager that individual answers to.
The documented lines agree with the HR system of record, and any position appearing in one and not the other is explained.
Reorganizations, acquisitions and departures during the period reached the structure inside the stated update window.
A position held vacant carries a named interim holder and the date the vacancy arose.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the organizational structure in force at the test date and the version in force at the start of the period.
Obtain the HR extract of active positions, holders and reporting managers for units inside the financial reporting boundary.
Collect the period's reorganizations, acquisitions, disposals and senior departures from HR and legal records.
Obtain the service scope statements for shared service centres and outsourced finance activity.
Select a sample of 15 positions carrying a financial reporting duty, weighted toward units that changed in the period.

Analysis:
Reconcile the structure against the HR extract in both directions and treat any position on one side only as an exception.
Trace each sampled position to a named holder, a named reporting manager, and the officer accountable for that unit.
Compare the opening and closing structures against the change list to measure how long each change took to arrive.
Test whether outsourced and shared service activity shows a retained owner employed inside the organization.
Examine vacant positions for an interim holder and judge how long the gap has been open.

Output:
Reconciliation of structure to HR records, naming each unmatched position and the side found to be wrong.
Schedule of sampled positions lacking a holder, a manager or an accountable officer.
Statement of whether period changes arrived inside the update window, giving the longest lag observed.
List of units whose work is performed outside the organization with no retained owner named.

title.en: Delimit the units that carry financial reporting duties

description.en: Fix which legal entities, sites and business units sit inside the financial reporting boundary, so the structure that follows has a population to be complete against.

text.en: Name every legal entity, site and business unit whose activity reaches the consolidated financial statements.
Separate work performed in-house from work run by a shared service centre or an outside provider.
State the criterion that puts a unit inside the boundary, and who settles a disputed case.
Fix the window inside which a reorganization must arrive in the documented structure.

title.en: Draw each unit through to a named accountable officer

description.en: Chart the positions that authorise, record and review transactions in each in-scope unit, and attach a person and a manager to every one of them.

text.en: Chart the positions that authorise, record and review transactions in each in-scope unit.
Attach a named holder to every position and name the manager that holder answers to.
Show the retained owner inside the organization for activity performed by an outside provider.
Mark positions held on an interim basis with the date the vacancy arose.
Have each unit head confirm in writing the lines drawn for their own unit.

title.en: Reflect the period's reorganizations in the published structure

description.en: Carry each reorganization, acquisition and senior departure into the structure and publish it, so what staff can reach is what management decided.

evidenceHint.en: The dated versions issued during the period alongside the change log, showing each reorganization and the day it arrived in what staff can reach.

text.en: Collect the period's reorganizations, acquisitions, disposals and senior departures from HR records.
Amend the units and lines affected by each change and date the amendment.
Publish the amended structure to the intranet location staff are directed to.
Withdraw the superseded version wherever a reader could still reach it.
Note the lag between each change taking effect and its arrival in the published version.

title.en: Reconcile the charted positions to the HR system of record

description.en: Run the documented structure against the HR system in both directions each quarter and settle every position that appears on only one side.

text.en: Extract active positions, holders and reporting managers from the HR system of record.
Match that extract to the charted positions in both directions and list every unmatched entry.
Investigate each unmatched position and note which of the two sources was wrong.
Escalate any in-scope unit left without an accountable officer to the responsible executive.
Close the reconciliation with a date, the preparer named and the exceptions carried forward.

templates.title: Delegation of authority matrix approved and maintained
templates.description: The matrix stating what each role may commit the organization to, approved at a level competent to confer that power and revised as roles, entities and thresholds change.
templates.objective: To ensure authority to commit the organization is conferred in writing at stated value limits by an approver competent to grant it, rather than inferred from a job title.
templates.successCriteria:
A current matrix states, for every transaction type the organization enters into, the role that may approve it and the value limit attached to that role.
The version in force carries a dated approval by the board or a delegate holding power to confer the authority it grants.
Each delegation names a deputy and the route a value above the limit must take, so absence does not force a workaround.
Role changes, new entities and threshold changes since the last approval appear in the version in force.
Temporary delegations carry an expiry date and no expired grant is still presented as live.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the authority matrix in force and the record of its approval, naming the approver and the date.
Obtain the version in force at the start of the period and the change log between the two.
Compile the population of transaction types from the chart of accounts, contract register and payment runs.
Collect the delegation letters and role grants held by individual delegates, permanent and temporary.
Select a sample of 20 delegations spanning every transaction type and both grant kinds.

Analysis:
Test each transaction type in the population against the matrix and treat a type with no stated approver as an exception.
Confirm the approver of the version in force holds power to confer what it grants, and that the approval predates the effective date.
Trace each sampled delegation to a holder, a deputy, a stated limit and a route above that limit.
Compare the year's role changes, new entities and threshold changes against the matrix to find rows overtaken by events.
Check temporary delegations for an expiry date and test whether any lapsed grant is still recorded as current.

Output:
Coverage table of transaction types against matrix rows, naming every type with no approver stated.
Schedule of sampled delegations missing a limit, a deputy or an escalation route.
Statement of the approver and date behind the version in force, and any lapse against the review cycle.
List of expired temporary grants still shown as current, with an owner named against each.

title.en: Enumerate the transaction types an authority must cover

description.en: Draw up the population of commitments the organization can enter into, so the matrix is built against a stated denominator instead of the types someone remembered.

text.en: Draw the transaction types from the chart of accounts, contract register and payment runs.
Group the types by the exposure each carries to the financial statements, not by department.
Note for each type the legal entities it can be entered into within.
Single out types approved today by custom alone, with no written delegation behind them.

title.en: Set the value limits and approver roles against each type

description.en: Attach an approver role and a value limit to every transaction type in the population, together with a deputy and the route a larger value must take.

text.en: Assign an approver role, never a named individual, to every transaction type listed.
Attach a value limit to each role and state the route a value above it must take.
Give each approver role a deputy, so an absence does not force a workaround.
Date-stamp any grant made temporarily with the day it expires.
Draft the matrix as one document, so a reader finds a single answer per transaction type.

title.en: Put the matrix into force under a dated board approval

description.en: Take the drafted matrix to the body competent to confer the authority it grants, capture the decision, and issue the approved version to the people who rely on it.

evidenceHint.en: The minute recording the approval decision, filed with the exact version it approved and the date that version took effect.

text.en: Submit the draft to the board or committee holding power to confer the authority.
Capture the decision, the approver and the date the version takes effect.
Issue the approved version to budget holders, finance and the systems team.
Withdraw the previous version from every location a reader can still reach.
File the approval record beside the version it approved, so the pair can be produced together.

title.en: Re-approve the matrix against the year's role changes

description.en: Test the matrix in force against the roles, entities and thresholds that actually changed during the year, and record the re-approval decision that follows.

text.en: Collect the role changes, new entities and threshold changes recorded during the year.
Run each change against the matrix to find rows that no longer name a live role.
Challenge limits no transaction has approached and limits exceeded as a matter of routine.
Amend the affected rows and take the amendments back for re-approval.
Record the re-approval date and the rows changed since the previous version.

templates.title: Authority limits enforced in transactional systems
templates.description: The approved limits configured in the systems that post transactions, so a commitment beyond a delegate's authority is refused, and the postings that got round it are found.
templates.objective: To ensure the approved authority limits are configured in the systems that post transactions, so a commitment beyond a delegate's limit is refused rather than merely disallowed on paper.
templates.successCriteria:
Approval workflows in each transactional system carry limits traceable row for row to the approved authority matrix.
A value above a delegate's limit cannot be posted without the higher approval the matrix calls for, demonstrated by re-performance.
The account raising a transaction cannot approve that same transaction in any system inside the boundary.
Overrides and emergency approvals are logged with a reason and examined by somebody other than the user who invoked them.
Over-limit, self-approved and split postings in the period are identified, explained and dispositioned.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved authority matrix in force during the period, as the standard the configuration is tested against.
Export the workflow configuration and limit tables from each transactional system: purchasing, payments, journals and master data.
Obtain the full population of postings for the period with requester, approver, value and vendor.
Collect the override, emergency-access and workflow-bypass logs covering the period.
Obtain the change records for every limit altered in a system during the period.

Analysis:
Compare each configured limit against the matrix row behind it, treating a system value with no matrix row as an exception.
Re-perform the control with test postings either side of a limit and confirm the one above is refused without the higher approval.
Interrogate the whole posting population for requester equal to approver and for approvals above the approver's limit.
Sum same-vendor, same-day postings and compare the total against the threshold, to find values split beneath a limit.
Trace each logged override to a stated reason and to a reviewer other than the user who invoked it.
Confirm each limit changed in a system is supported by a matrix change approved beforehand.

Output:
