Configuration comparison naming every limit that differs from the matrix and the direction of the difference.
Re-performance result stating the system, the limit tested and whether the posting was refused.
Exception listing of over-limit, self-approved and split postings with an owner named against each.
Disposition of every override in the period, naming those with no reason or no independent reviewer.

title.en: Scope the systems in which a commitment can be posted

description.en: Establish which systems can create an obligation or move money, including any route that reaches the ledger without meeting an approval workflow at all.

text.en: Catalogue the systems that post purchase orders, payments, journals and contract commitments.
Note for each system whether its approval workflow is native or handled outside it.
Single out routes that reach the ledger without meeting an approval workflow at all.
Name the person able to change a limit in each of those systems.

title.en: Configure the approved thresholds into each workflow

description.en: Carry every matrix row into the workflow rule that implements it, and close the self-approval path, so the limit is refused by the system rather than by a reader.

text.en: Map each row of the approved matrix onto the workflow rule that will implement it.
Enter the value limits into purchasing, payments, journal and master data workflows.
Stop the account raising a transaction from approving that same transaction.
Route a value above a limit to the higher approver instead of offering an override.
Attach the change ticket that carried each limit into the system to the row it implements.

title.en: Investigate postings that cleared outside a configured limit

description.en: Interrogate the month's postings for approvals above the approver's limit, self-approvals and values split beneath a threshold, and settle each one with the unit that raised it.

evidenceHint.en: The month's exception listing from each transactional system, showing every over-limit, self-approved and split posting with its explanation and disposition.

text.en: Query the month's postings for approvals above the approver's stated limit.
Query the same population for an account that approved a transaction it raised.
Sum same-vendor, same-day values to surface commitments split beneath a threshold.
Obtain an explanation and a disposition from the unit owner for each exception raised.
Refer exceptions left unexplained to the controller for correction or reversal.

title.en: Re-perform the threshold test either side of a limit

description.en: Prove the configuration by trying to post beyond it: a value under the limit, a value over it, and an approval by the account that raised the transaction.

text.en: Choose one limit to test in each transactional system inside the boundary.
Post a test transaction below the chosen limit and confirm it clears as expected.
Post a test transaction above the chosen limit and confirm the system refuses it.
Attempt an approval from the account that raised it and record the system's response.
Reverse the test transactions and retain the screen evidence of each attempt.

templates.title: Competency requirements defined for control-relevant roles
templates.description: The knowledge, experience and delegated authority each control-performing seat demands, written down per role so fitness for it is judged against a stated standard.
templates.objective: To ensure every role that performs, reviews or supervises a financial reporting control carries a written competence requirement, so fitness for the seat is judged against a stated standard.
templates.successCriteria:
Each role that performs or supervises an in-scope control has a written competence statement naming the knowledge, experience and authority it demands.
The requirement set for a reviewer or approver is deeper than the one set for the preparer of the same control, not a copy of it.
Every in-scope seat traces to a current statement, with none covered only by a recruitment advertisement or by custom.
The statements were reviewed within the stated cycle and reflect the process and system changes of the period.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the population of in-scope roles, drawn from the control matrix rather than from the organisation chart alone.
Obtain the competence statement held for each sampled role, with its version, approver and approval date.
Collect the process, system and reporting changes of the period that could alter what a seat must know.
Obtain the record of the last review of the statements, naming who performed it and when.
Request the job descriptions and recruitment postings used when these seats were last filled.

Analysis:
Reconcile the role population against the control matrix to expose control-performing seats with no statement at all.
Sample roles across preparer, reviewer and approver seats and test whether each statement sets knowledge, experience and authority separately.
Compare the preparer and reviewer statements for the same control to confirm the reviewer's requirement is not the preparer's reworded.
Test the period's changes against the statements for the seats they touched, and judge whether any requirement is now out of date.
Compare the recruitment postings against the statement to confirm the standard used to hire matches the standard written down.

Output:
Schedule of in-scope seats with the statement held for each, naming those with none.
List of statements omitting knowledge, experience or authority, with the missing element against each.
Statement of whether the review cycle was met, and which changes of the period have not reached a statement.

title.en: Identify the roles that perform or supervise in-scope controls

description.en: Draw the role population from the control matrix rather than the organisation chart, so a seat performing a control under a generic job title is still counted.

text.en: Extract from the control matrix every in-scope control and the seat that performs it.
Separate preparer, reviewer and approver seats, because each carries a different depth of requirement.
Add the seats that supervise or can override a control, including those held by contractors and interim staff.
Reconcile the resulting role list against the HR establishment and resolve every seat appearing on only one side.

title.en: Draft the competence standard each in-scope role must meet

description.en: State per role the knowledge, experience and delegated authority the seat demands, scaled to what its holder can approve or override rather than written once for everyone.

text.en: State the accounting, system and process knowledge the seat needs to perform its control unaided.
Set the experience or qualification floor separately for preparer, reviewer and approver seats.
Name the delegated authority the seat carries and the limit above which it must escalate.
Note what is accepted as proof of each requirement, such as a qualification certificate or a documented assessment.
Route the draft to the control owner and to HR, and file the approved version with its date.

title.en: Match each appointment to the standard the seat carries

description.en: Before a person takes up a control-relevant seat, assess them against the written standard for it and record where they fall short and what covers the shortfall until it closes.

evidenceHint.en: The appointment file for each in-scope seat filled during the period, holding the assessment against the written standard and the approver's decision on any shortfall.

text.en: Obtain the current competence standard for the seat before the appointment is confirmed.
Assess the candidate or internal mover against each element of that standard and note the gaps.
Agree the supervision, training or withheld duties that cover a gap until it is closed.
File the assessment and the approver's decision with the appointment record.

title.en: Re-test the standards against the period's process and system changes

description.en: Where a process, system or reporting requirement changed in the period, judge whether the competence stated for the seats it touched is still the competence the work now demands.

text.en: Compile the process, system and reporting changes of the period that touched an in-scope control.
Map each change to the seats whose control it altered, using the control matrix as the link.
Compare the stated requirement for those seats against what the changed control now demands.
Revise the affected standards, or record why the existing wording still holds.
Report the seats left with an out-of-date standard to the control owner with a date to fix.

templates.title: Pre-hire screening performed for control-relevant roles
templates.description: Background checking completed before a person takes up a control-relevant post, with the depth of check set by the authority and access that post carries.
templates.objective: To ensure a person appointed to a control-relevant post has been screened to a depth matched to the authority the post carries, and cleared before they can act on it.
templates.successCriteria:
Every control-relevant post is graded into a screening tier from the approval limit, system privilege and data access it holds.
Each appointment into such a post in the period holds a completed screening result dated before the start date.
The checks reach contractors, agency staff and internal movers into these posts, not only external permanent hires.
An adverse or incomplete result was decided by the person entitled to decide it, with the outcome recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the tiering schedule showing each control-relevant post, its graded tier and the attributes the grade was drawn from.
Obtain the screening procedure, including the checks each tier attracts and the consent and retention rules they run under.
Draw the appointment population for the period from payroll joiners, contractor and agency records, and internal transfer lists.
Obtain the screening file for each sampled appointment and the start date recorded for the same person.
Obtain the log of adverse or incomplete results and the decision recorded against each.

Analysis:
Test every appointment into the highest tier and a sample of the lower tiers, so depth is judged where the authority sits.
Compare the checks actually performed against the checks the post's tier required, and note any performed at a lower tier.
Set each clearance date against the start date to find people who began work before the checks returned.
Trace internal movers into a higher-tier post to a re-screening, rather than reliance on the clearance held for their previous seat.
Test the adverse results for a recorded decision by the named decider, and check any restriction imposed was applied in the systems.

Output:
Schedule of the period's appointments with the tier, the checks held and the clearance date for each.
List of people who started before clearance, or who hold checks below their post's tier, with the authority each was granted meanwhile.
Statement of whether adverse results were decided by the entitled decider and whether restrictions were enforced.

title.en: Grade each control-relevant post by the authority it carries

description.en: Place every post that performs, reviews or can override a control into a screening tier, using the money, data and system authority it holds rather than its position in the hierarchy.

text.en: Take the posts that perform or approve an in-scope control from the control matrix.
Note for each post its approval limit, its system privileges and the data it can reach.
Assign a tier from those attributes, so a junior post that releases payments sits above a senior post that cannot.
Agree the tiering with Legal/Compliance so each check is lawful where the post is hired.

title.en: Define the check set each tier of post attracts

description.en: Fix which checks a tier requires, from identity and right to work through to qualification verification, references, credit and criminal record, and the consent and retention rules that govern them.

text.en: Specify the checks applying at every tier, such as identity and right to work.
Add the checks only the higher tiers attract, naming the authority that triggers them.
State the consent, disclosure and retention rules each check runs under, per jurisdiction.
Name the provider or internal team performing each check and the turnaround it commits to.
Appoint who decides when a result is adverse or incomplete, and what they are entitled to decide.

title.en: Complete the tier's checks before the appointee takes the seat

description.en: Run the checks the post's tier requires and clear them ahead of the start date, holding the start or the authority rather than letting a person begin on trust.

evidenceHint.en: The screening file for every appointment in the period, showing each check the tier required, its result, and the clearance date set against the recorded start date.

text.en: Begin the checks when the offer is made, so turnaround does not force a start on trust.
Note each check returned, its result and its date, against the tier the post was graded at.
Hold the start date, or withhold the post's authority, where a required check has not returned.
File the screening result so its clearance date can later be compared with the start date.

title.en: Escalate an adverse or incomplete result to the named decider

description.en: Where a check returns something adverse or cannot be completed, route it to the person entitled to decide and capture what they decided and why, rather than letting the appointment proceed by default.

evidenceHint.en: The adverse-result log for the period, each entry carrying the decision to proceed, restrict or withdraw, the decider's name and the date it was taken.

text.en: Route the result to the decider named for that tier within the time the procedure states.
Assemble what the decider needs: the check returned, the post's authority and any explanation offered.
Capture the decision to proceed, to restrict the post's authority, or to withdraw the offer.
Apply any restriction in the systems that grant the post its authority, not on paper alone.
Dispose of the adverse result at the end of the retention period set for it.

title.en: Sweep the period's appointments for a missing or under-tiered check

description.en: Take every person who took up a control-relevant post in the period, whether external hire, contractor, agency worker or internal mover, and test each against the file their tier should have produced.

text.en: Draw the appointment population from payroll joiners, contractor records and transfer lists.
Match each appointment to a screening file and set out those with none.
Check the checks performed match the tier the post carries rather than a lower tier.
Test whether an internal mover into a higher tier was re-screened for the seat moved into.
Refer the exceptions to an owner with a date, and escalate anyone still in post uncleared.

templates.title: Onboarding covers the role's control responsibilities
templates.description: What a new or moved post-holder is walked through before performing a control: the controls the seat owns, the evidence each must leave, and where its authority stops.
templates.objective: To ensure a person taking up a control-relevant seat is walked through the controls it owns and the evidence they must leave, before they first perform one of them.
templates.successCriteria:
Each control-relevant seat has an onboarding brief naming the controls it performs, the evidence each leaves and the authority limit that binds it.
Every joiner and internal mover into such a seat in the quarter completed the brief, with a dated record of who delivered it.
The brief was delivered before the holder first performed the control, not at the close of a probation period.
Where a seat's controls changed since the brief was written, the version delivered reflects the change.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the onboarding brief held for each control-relevant seat, with its version date and the control set it was written from.
Draw the quarter's population of joiners and internal movers into those seats from HR records, transfer lists and contractor onboarding records.
Obtain the completed brief for each sampled person, showing the deliverer, the holder's acknowledgement and the date.
Obtain the date each sampled person first performed one of the seat's controls, taken from the control evidence itself.
Collect the changes made to the seats' control sets during the quarter.

Analysis:
Reconcile the seat population against the briefs held to expose control-relevant seats with no brief written at all.
Test every sampled person for a completed brief, and compare its delivery date with the date of their first performance.
Sample briefs and trace their content back to the current control matrix, checking the controls, evidence and limits named are the seat's own.
Compare the version delivered against the version current at the delivery date, to catch a superseded brief still in use.
Test whether contractors and internal movers were briefed on the same basis as permanent joiners.

Output:
Schedule of the quarter's entrants to control-relevant seats, with the brief date and first performance date for each.
List of people who performed a control before being briefed, naming the control performed.
List of seats with no brief, or with a brief predating the last change to the seat's controls.

title.en: Determine what each control-relevant seat must brief its holder on

description.en: Decide per seat which controls its holder performs, what evidence each must leave and the limit beyond which they escalate, so the brief is built from the seat rather than a generic induction pack.

text.en: Pull from the control matrix the controls each in-scope seat performs or reviews.
State the evidence each of those controls must leave and where it is filed.
Name the authority limit the seat holds and who it escalates to beyond that point.
Note the system access the seat needs and the segregation rule constraining it.

title.en: Build the onboarding brief for each seat from its control set

description.en: Turn the per-seat content into something a line manager can deliver, with a checklist showing what was covered and a record that the seat's holder received it.

text.en: Draft one brief per seat, covering its controls, the evidence they leave and its limits.
Include the date by which the holder is expected to perform each control unaided.
Add a sign-off for the deliverer and the holder, with the date of delivery.
Attach the underlying procedure or work instruction rather than restating it in the brief.
Agree with HR where the completed brief is filed so it can be produced on request.

title.en: Deliver the brief before the holder first performs the control

description.en: Walk the new or moved holder through the seat's brief ahead of their first performance, and capture the delivery rather than relying on a manager's recollection of it.

evidenceHint.en: The completed onboarding brief for each joiner and internal mover in the quarter, signed by the deliverer and the holder and dated ahead of the first performance.

text.en: Schedule the briefing inside the seat's stated window, ahead of the first performance date.
Walk the holder through each control, the evidence it leaves and the limit that binds it.
Capture the questions raised that show the brief is unclear, and send them to its author.
File the signed brief with the joiner record and note the date it was delivered.

title.en: Trace the quarter's joiners and movers to a completed brief

description.en: Take the quarter's population of people who entered a control-relevant seat and test whether each holds a delivered brief dated before they first performed one of the seat's controls.

text.en: Draw the quarter's joiner and internal-mover population from HR and contractor records.
Filter it to those entering a seat that performs or reviews an in-scope control.
Match each to a completed brief and compare its date with the first performance of the control.
Sample the briefs against the current control set to confirm the version delivered was current.
Report the seats briefed late or not at all, naming the control performed meanwhile.

templates.title: Annual role-specific training completion tracked
templates.description: The yearly training each control-relevant role is required to complete, tracked against a named population so a non-completion is visible rather than assumed away.
templates.objective: To ensure the training each control-relevant role must complete in the year is tracked against a named population, so a person who has not completed it is visible before the year closes.
templates.successCriteria:
A module set is assigned per control-relevant role rather than one course issued to everyone, and each role maps to the modules it requires.
The tracked population is drawn from the establishment and includes contractors and internal movers, not only the permanent staff in post at the year's start.
Completion is held per person and per module with a date, and the register separates not started from overdue.
Every non-completion reached a conclusion in the year: completed, waived by a named approver, or escalated to the role's owner.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the curriculum map showing each control-relevant role and the modules assigned to it.
Obtain the completion register as at the year end, holding a status and date per person and per module.
Obtain the establishment of control-relevant roles at the year end, with the joiners, leavers and internal movers of the year identified.
Collect the chase correspondence and the approved waivers or deferrals recorded against non-completions.
Obtain the completion rate as reported to management for the year.

Analysis:
Reconcile the enrolled population against the year-end establishment in both directions, and explain every name appearing on only one side.
Sample people across preparer, reviewer and approver roles and confirm each was assigned the module set their role requires.
Recompute the completion rate from the register and compare it with the rate reported, noting whether waived entries were counted as complete.
Test the joiners and internal movers of the year for enrolment from the date they entered the role, not from the following cycle.
Trace each non-completion to its conclusion, and check a waiver was approved by someone entitled to grant it.

Output:
Schedule of control-relevant roles with the module set assigned to each, naming those with none.
Reconciliation of the enrolled population against the establishment, with the unexplained names on each side.
Recomputed completion rate against the reported figure, and the list of non-completions still open at the year end.

title.en: Assign the module set each control-relevant role must complete

description.en: Decide what each role is required to learn in the year, distinguishing the role that performs a control from the one that approves it, instead of routing everyone to a single course.

text.en: Group the in-scope roles by the control work they do, not by department or grade.
Select the modules each group must complete, naming the control risk each addresses.
Add the modules a change in the year makes necessary, such as a new system or reporting requirement.
Set the completion deadline for each module and the year it runs to.

title.en: Load the curriculum and its deadlines into the training record

description.en: Put the per-role assignment into the system that holds completion, so a person's outstanding modules can be read off a register rather than assembled by hand at the year end.

text.en: Enrol each role's population against its assigned modules in the learning record.
Configure the deadline and the reminder schedule for every enrolment.
Link the enrolment to the HR establishment feed so a joiner or mover is picked up automatically.
Sample people against the modules their role requires, to prove the register was built correctly.

title.en: Chase the outstanding completions to a dated conclusion

description.en: Work the list of people who have not completed, during the year rather than after it, until each is completed, formally waived, or escalated to the role's accountable owner.

evidenceHint.en: The year-end completion register showing each person's status per module, with the chase correspondence and any waiver approved by a named manager.

text.en: Run the outstanding list at each reminder point and send it to the line manager.
Capture the reason given for each non-completion, such as leave, transfer or workload.
Route a request to waive or defer to the manager entitled to approve it, and note the decision.
Escalate the people still outstanding at the deadline to the role's accountable owner.
Close each entry as completed, waived or escalated, with the date it reached that state.

title.en: Test the completion register against the establishment at year end

description.en: Reconcile the population the register tracked against the people actually holding control-relevant roles at the year end, so a role never enrolled does not read as fully compliant.

text.en: Draw the establishment of control-relevant roles at the year end from HR records.
Compare it with the enrolled population and explain every name on only one side.
Recompute the completion rate from the register and compare it with the rate reported.
Check contractors and internal movers were enrolled from the date they entered the role.
Report the roles with no module set assigned and the people holding none at all.

templates.title: Control responsibilities included in performance objectives
templates.description: The duty to operate a control is written into the objectives of the individual who performs it, so the responsibility rests on a person and not on a function.
templates.objective: To ensure each person who operates a control carries that duty in their agreed objectives for the period, so accountability sits on a named individual rather than on a team.
templates.successCriteria:
Every control in the register resolves to a named individual whose objectives for the period state the duty.
The objective wording names the control and when it falls due, rather than committing generally to compliance.
People who joined or changed role during the period had objectives amended within the window the cycle sets.
Where a control changed hands, the duty was closed out of the outgoing holder's objectives and added to the incoming holder's.
No objective names a control that has since been retired from the register.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the control register for the period showing the owner recorded against each control.
Obtain the objective records agreed at cycle start for every person named as an owner.
Obtain the joiner and internal-move report for the period from the HR system.
Obtain the stated window for setting objectives after a hire or a change of role.
Request the ownership change log for controls that moved between holders.

Analysis:
Reconcile the register's owner column against the objective population and isolate controls whose holder has no objective naming the duty.
Read a sample of at least 25 objectives, or all of them where fewer, for a stated act and a due date rather than a general undertaking.
Compare each internal move against the date the objectives were amended and measure the gap against the stated window.
For each control that changed hands, check the outgoing holder's duty was removed and the incoming holder's added in the same cycle.
Search the objective set for duties naming controls no longer in the register.

Output:
An exception list of controls whose named holder carries no objective covering them.
The gap in days for every joiner or mover whose objectives were amended late.
A statement of the sample size, the population drawn from, and the exceptions found.

title.en: Resolve every control in the register to one named individual

description.en: Take each control down to a single person rather than a department, because an objective can only be written for an individual and a duty shared between several is the one nobody performs.

text.en: Export the control register with its owner column as it stood at the opening of the objective cycle.
Resolve each owning team or function to a single named person who actually performs the work.
Flag controls sitting against a vacant post or a shared mailbox and escalate them for assignment.
Record the person-to-control mapping with the date it was taken, as the population for the cycle.

title.en: Draft objective wording that states the duty and when it falls due

description.en: Agree a form of words specific enough to be assessed at the end of the period, so that an evaluator can decide whether the duty was discharged or not.

text.en: Write wording that names the control, the act required of the holder, and the date it is due.
Separate that duty from a general commitment to compliance, which cannot be judged at year end.
Agree the wording with the process owners whose objectives will carry the duty this cycle.
Load the agreed wording into the objective-setting template used across the organization.

title.en: Amend objectives when a control changes hands mid-cycle

description.en: Move the duty with the control whenever somebody joins, leaves or transfers, so the register and the objective records do not drift apart between cycles.

evidenceHint.en: The amended objective records for the outgoing and incoming holders, each dated, alongside the ownership change log entry they answer.

text.en: Watch the joiner, leaver and internal-move feed for people entering or leaving a control role.
Amend the incoming holder's objectives to name the control within the window the cycle sets.
Close the duty out of the outgoing holder's objectives so it is not counted against two people.
Note the effective date of each amendment against the entry in the ownership change log.

title.en: Sweep the register mid-cycle for controls with no matching objective

description.en: Check the two records against each other partway through the period, while an unassigned control can still be given to somebody before the cycle closes.

evidenceHint.en: The dated comparison showing register holders without an objective covering the duty, and objectives naming controls no longer in force.

text.en: Pull the objective records in force at the sweep date for everyone named as a holder.
Identify controls whose holder carries no objective naming the responsibility at all.
Identify objectives naming a control that has since been retired from the register.
Refer each unmatched control to the executive owning that function for reassignment.
Report the count of unmatched controls and the days taken to clear each one.

templates.title: Performance evaluations assess control responsibilities
templates.description: At the close of the cycle, the evaluation of each control holder carries a judgement on how the control was actually operated, supported by what the period's records show.
templates.objective: To ensure the control duties agreed at the start of the cycle are judged in the completed evaluation against the period's recorded results, rather than passed over or rated on impression.
templates.successCriteria:
Each completed evaluation for a control holder carries an explicit judgement on the control duty, not only on functional targets.
The judgement cites what the period recorded: completions, exceptions, overdue remediation or test results.
Holders whose controls failed repeatedly are rated differently from holders whose controls operated as designed.
Where the duty was judged unmet, a consequence or development action is recorded against the holder.
Evaluations are signed within the window the cycle sets, and any outstanding one is named.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the completed evaluation records for everyone who held a control duty during the period.
Obtain the control test results, exception logs and overdue remediation items covering the same period.
Obtain the evaluation calendar stating when ratings were due and signed.
Collect the consequences or development actions recorded where a duty was judged unmet.
Request the calibration notes for ratings adjusted after moderation.

Analysis:
Read a sample of at least 25 evaluations, or all where fewer, for a judgement that addresses the control duty by name.
Set each holder's rating against the failures recorded on their own controls, and isolate holders rated as meeting the duty whose controls failed more than once.
Trace a rating comment back to the exception log or test result it cites, to confirm the cited evidence exists.
Compare signature dates against the evaluation window to find ratings completed late or not at all.
Check each unmet judgement carried an action, and whether that action was afterwards performed.

Output:
A list of control holders whose evaluation contains no judgement on the control duty.
The set of holders rated favourably despite recorded control failures, naming the failures.
A statement of evaluations outstanding at the cut-off and how many days they are overdue.

title.en: Set the criteria a control duty judgement has to meet

description.en: Decide in advance what an evaluator must cite and what separates a duty discharged from one only partly discharged, so ratings across evaluators mean the same thing.

text.en: State the evidence an evaluator must cite, such as test results, exception counts or overdue items.
Define what separates a discharged duty from a partly discharged one in terms an evaluator can apply.
Agree how a control failure outside the holder's influence is treated, so the rating stays fair.
Publish the criteria to evaluators before the rating window opens for the cycle.

title.en: Build the control duty section into the evaluation form

description.en: Put the judgement where the evaluator cannot skip it, and place the holder's objectives and period evidence in front of them at the moment they write it.

text.en: Add a field to the evaluation template requiring a judgement on the control duty in words.
Make that field mandatory so a form cannot be submitted while it is left blank.
Show the holder's agreed objectives and the period evidence inside the same form.
Pilot the form with a small group of evaluators and correct the wording they misread.

title.en: Rate each holder's control duty on the period's recorded results

description.en: Write the rating from what the evidence pack shows rather than from recollection, and raise an action where the duty was not discharged.

evidenceHint.en: Completed evaluation forms carrying the duty judgement, each citing the test result, exception log entry or overdue item it rests on.

text.en: Read the period evidence attributed to the holder before drafting any rating text.
State the judgement in the evaluation, citing the specific result or exception it rests on.
Distinguish holders whose controls operated from those whose controls failed repeatedly.
Raise a development action or a consequence where the duty was not discharged.
Sign and date the evaluation inside the window the cycle calendar sets.

title.en: Challenge favourable ratings given to holders of failed controls

description.en: Take the ratings that contradict the period's record to moderation before they are finalised, since an unchallenged one teaches everybody that the duty is decorative.

evidenceHint.en: The moderation record listing each rating challenged, the control failures behind the challenge, and the outcome after the evaluator responded.

text.en: Join the rating table to the control failures recorded against each holder for the period.
Select every holder rated as meeting the duty whose controls failed more than once.
Ask the evaluator what evidence supported that rating, and record the answer given.
Refer unexplained cases to the moderation forum before ratings are finalised.
Summarise the challenges raised and their outcome for the cycle's record.

templates.title: Incentive structures reviewed for override pressure
templates.description: The pressure a reward scheme places on the people it pays: targets, thresholds and payout curves examined for what they would reward somebody for doing to figures that person helps prepare.
templates.objective: To ensure the payout terms of every scheme in force are examined each cycle for the pressure they place on participants able to influence the figures their reward is measured on.
templates.successCriteria:
Every scheme in force is listed with its metric, threshold, payout curve, cap and participant population.
Each metric is traced to the account, estimate or judgement a participant is positioned to influence.
Schemes carrying a cliff edge, uncapped upside or a single period-end measure are identified and the reason recorded.
Participants settling within a narrow band of a threshold are examined against their period-end activity.
Conclusions are passed to the owner of the fraud risk assessment rather than held within the reward function.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scheme documents in force for the period, with targets, thresholds, payout curves and any discretion held.
Obtain the participant population for each scheme and the measure each person is paid against.
Obtain the actual results by participant at the measurement date, showing where each landed relative to threshold.
Collect the malus, clawback or conduct gate terms and every occasion they were applied.
Obtain the minutes recording who reviewed the schemes and what was concluded.

Analysis:
Map each metric to the accounts and estimates a participant can influence, separating figures they prepare from figures set elsewhere.
Identify cliff structures where a small movement in the measure changes the payout sharply.
Select participants landing within a narrow band of a threshold and examine the transactions booked on their metric near the cut-off.
Test whether a conduct gate or clawback could be applied in practice, not merely stated in the terms.
Compare the conclusions reached against the fraud scenarios on record, to confirm the pressure identified reached that assessment.

Output:
A schedule of schemes ranked by the pressure their terms create, with the reason recorded against each.
The participants who settled close to a threshold and what examination of their period-end activity showed.
A statement of which conclusions were passed to the fraud risk assessment and which changes to scheme terms were proposed.

title.en: Assemble a schedule of every reward scheme and who is paid under it

description.en: Bring each bonus, commission and long-term award operating in the period onto one schedule, since a scheme nobody has written down is a scheme nobody examines.

text.en: Gather the terms of every bonus, commission and long-term award in force during the period.
Record the metric, threshold, payout curve and any cap that applies to each of them.
List the participants under each scheme and the measure their payout depends upon.
Note where discretion can change a payout, and which person or body holds it.

title.en: Trace each scheme metric to the figures its participants prepare

description.en: Establish where the person being paid also influences the number deciding the payment, which is the condition that turns a reward into pressure on a control.

evidenceHint.en: The metric-to-account mapping for the cycle, marking every measure whose inputs are prepared or approved by the participant being paid on it.

text.en: Take each metric from the scheme schedule and name the ledger account or estimate behind it.
Mark the metrics whose inputs are prepared or approved by the participant being paid.
Flag measures resting on a judgement, such as a reserve, an accrual or a cut-off date.
Rank the schemes by how far a participant is able to move their own measure.
Hand the ranking to the reviewing body as the basis for this cycle's discussion.

title.en: Examine payouts that settled within a narrow band of a threshold

description.en: Look at the population where the pressure would have shown itself, comparing what was booked near the cut-off for those who just cleared a threshold and those who just missed one.

evidenceHint.en: The near-threshold schedule for the cycle, showing each selected participant, the period-end transactions examined and the conclusion reached.

text.en: Compute each participant's distance from the nearest threshold at the measurement date.
Select those landing just above a threshold and those falling just short of one.
Examine the transactions booked on their metric in the closing days of the period.
Ask the process owner to explain anything timed unusually close to the cut-off.
Record the conclusion for every case selected, including those where nothing was found.

title.en: Attach a conduct gate to schemes whose terms allow none

description.en: Give the organization a route to withhold or recover a payout won in a way it would not defend, because a scheme paying on the number alone rewards the override as readily as the result.

text.en: Identify schemes whose terms offer no route to withhold or recover a payment.
Draft gate wording tying payment to how the result was reached, not to the number alone.
Agree that wording with the body approving reward terms before the next cycle opens.
Amend the scheme documents and tell participants what changed and when it takes effect.

title.en: Refer the pressure findings into the fraud risk assessment

description.en: Pass what the examination found to the people who build fraud scenarios, so the pressure this control identifies becomes an input there instead of being assessed twice or not at all.

evidenceHint.en: The dated transfer note listing each scheme concern handed over, with the fraud register entry or scenario it was logged against.

text.en: Summarise each scheme concern as what its terms would reward somebody for doing.
Send that summary and the supporting schedule to the owner of the fraud risk assessment.
Confirm each concern was logged as a scenario input, or record why it was not taken.
Keep the transfer note so the two assessments can be reconciled at the year end.

templates.title: Data sources supporting financial reporting identified
templates.description: The register of origins behind the figures in the financial statements - the team, file, feed or outside party each figure comes from, how it arrives, and how heavily the statements lean on it.
templates.objective: To ensure every figure reaching the financial statements traces to a named origin, inside or outside the organization, whose supplier, arrival route and reliance are recorded.
templates.successCriteria:
Every significant account and disclosure names at least one source, and no scoped figure comes from an origin the register omits.
Each entry states who supplies the data, whether it originates inside or outside the organization, and the route it arrives by.
A source that is not a system - a spreadsheet, an external valuation, a bank file - carries the same fields as one that is.
Each entry grades the reliance placed on it, so a source behind a material estimate is separable from one behind a footnote.
A supplier, route or format that changed in the period shows in the entry with the date it took effect.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved list of significant accounts and disclosures - that list is the population every coverage claim below is measured against.
Export the data-source register as at period end, giving supplier, origin, arrival route, form and graded reliance per entry.
Obtain the inventory of ICFR-relevant systems and key reports, which this register cross-refers to rather than reproduces.
Collect one month's close file showing the inputs each material balance was assembled from.
Obtain the period's record of supplier changes, migrations and retired feeds.

Analysis:
Population is every significant account and disclosure. Test all of them for at least one named source, because an omission cannot be sampled into view.
Sample ten sources weighted to material balances and confirm the party named still supplies the data in the form recorded.
Take the month's close file and name every input that reached a balance without appearing in the register.
Read each entry and judge whether it names where a figure came from rather than restating the system that held it or the report that printed it.
Test the non-system entries specifically - spreadsheets, valuations, vendor files - since those are the rows left thin.
Match the change record against entry dates to find a supplier that moved with no amendment.

Output:
Coverage table of significant accounts against named sources, listing the accounts with none.
Exception list of close-file inputs absent from the register, separating omissions from sources known but unrecorded.
Schedule of in-period supplier or route changes whose entry predates them.
Count of non-system sources stated beside the register total that produced it.

title.en: Trace each significant account back to the figures that feed it

description.en: Build the register from the accounts that must be reported rather than from the data that happens to be catalogued, so its boundary is a consequence of scope.

text.en: Begin from the approved list of significant accounts and disclosures for the period.
Name the figures each account is built from, down to what a preparer keys or imports.
Follow each figure back to the point it entered the organization, not the system that last held it.
Stop at the party that produced it, whether a business team, a bank, a broker or a provider.
Mark the accounts whose figures cannot be followed back to any identifiable origin.

title.en: Capture the supplier, arrival route and form of every source

description.en: Give each source an entry carrying the facts a tester needs to confirm it - who sends it, how it arrives and in what shape - so the register answers the question without a conversation.

text.en: Open one entry per source and name the party that supplies the data.
State whether the source sits inside the organization or outside it.
Describe how the data arrives: an interface, a file drop, a portal download or a manual entry.
Give the format and the cadence, so a monthly file is not mistaken for a live feed.
Cross-refer the entry to the receiving system instead of repeating that inventory here.

title.en: Grade each source by the reliance the statements place on it

description.en: A register treating a price feed behind a material valuation the same as an origin behind a rounding-level disclosure cannot direct testing effort, so reliance is recorded as a graded fact.

text.en: Name the account or disclosure each source ultimately feeds.
State the largest balance that source influenced during the period.
Grade the reliance against the materiality thresholds already approved.
Flag sources feeding an estimate or a judgement, which carry reliance beyond their size.
Agree the grading with the controller before it is used to direct testing.

title.en: Refresh an entry when its supplier or feed changes

description.en: A source register decays through supplier changes nobody told it about, so the in-period amendment is what keeps it describing the data actually arriving.

evidenceHint.en: The amended entry for each in-period change, showing the previous and new supplier or route, the date it took effect, and who confirmed it.

text.en: Watch for supplier changes, system migrations and renegotiated service arrangements.
Amend the affected entry with the new supplier, route or format and the effective date.
Retire an origin that has stopped feeding the statements rather than deleting its history.
Tell the owners of any reconciliation built on the old route that the route has moved.

title.en: Sample postings and confirm the register names their origin

description.en: What separates a register describing the data from one describing an intention is picking postings independently and asking the register where each figure came from.

text.en: Select postings from the ledger rather than from a list the register's owner offers.
Follow each posting back to the figure behind it and the party that produced that figure.
Confirm the origin appears in the register with the same supplier and arrival route.
List the origins found in practice that the register does not hold at all.
Report the unregistered count beside the number of postings examined.

templates.title: Completeness and accuracy controls over ICFR data flows
templates.description: The reconciliation performed over each transfer carrying financial data between systems: what the sending side despatched set against what the receiving side holds, with rejected records worked off and the result held as evidence on the control.
templates.objective: To ensure every transfer carrying financial data is reconciled on arrival, so what the receiving system holds is proven against what was sent rather than assumed complete.
templates.successCriteria:
Every transfer on the inventory is reconciled each time it runs, comparing record counts and control totals despatched against those received.
A difference is chased to the transaction and cleared before the period closes, with the explanation held against the transfer.
Records the receiving system rejected are worked to zero, or carried forward with an owner and a date.
The completed reconciliation is held as an evidence record linked to the control, so a tester retrieves it without asking the performer.
A run that did not happen, or happened twice, surfaces as an exception rather than passing unnoticed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of transfers carrying ICFR data, naming the sending system, the receiving system and the cadence of each.
Export the completed reconciliations for three consecutive months, each showing the counts and totals held on both sides.
Obtain the rejection and error queues for those months with their opening and closing positions.
Export the evidence records linked to this control for the period, with the date each was attached.
Obtain the job or scheduler history showing when each transfer actually ran.

Analysis:
Population is every transfer on the inventory across the three months. Check all of them for a reconciliation per run, since a transfer nobody reconciles never enters a sample.
Sample twelve reconciliations across the highest-volume transfers and recompute the arithmetic from the counts and totals recorded on each side.
Confirm every difference carries an explanation reaching a transaction, and a clearing date earlier than the close it fed.
Roll the rejection queue from opening to closing position and name the records still outstanding at period end.
Compare the job history against the reconciliations, in both directions: a run with no reconciliation, and a reconciliation citing a run that did not occur.
Test whether the evidence attached to the control is the reconciliation itself rather than a summary written for the file.

Output:
Coverage table of transfers against reconciliations per month, naming the gaps by transfer.
Recomputation results, separating an arithmetic failure from a difference left unexplained.
Ageing of rejected records, each with the owner and date carried against it.
List of unreconciled runs and of reconciliations naming a run the job history does not show.

title.en: Enumerate the transfers carrying financial data between systems

description.en: The population has to be drawn from the flows themselves, including the informal ones, because a transfer left off the inventory is a transfer nobody reconciles and nobody misses.

text.en: Walk each in-scope process and note every point where data leaves one system for another.
Include file drops, portal downloads and spreadsheets re-keyed into the ledger.
Name the sending system, the receiving system and the cadence of each transfer.
State the accounts each transfer ultimately affects, so materiality can direct effort.
Agree the inventory with the owner of each receiving system before controls are set.

title.en: Pair each transfer with the totals its two sides must agree

description.en: Completeness and accuracy over a flow is arithmetic rather than assertion: the sender has to publish a figure and the receiver has to produce the same figure independently from what it loaded.

text.en: Choose the total that means most for the transfer: record count, sum of amounts, or both.
Make the sending system publish that total with the batch rather than on request.
Make the receiving system compute the same total from the records it actually loaded.
Set the tolerance, if any, and state what a difference inside it may consist of.
Route rejected records into a queue with an owner rather than into a log file.

title.en: Re-perform the arrival reconciliation on every run

description.en: The operating half of the control: two totals compared while the period is still open, and a difference chased to the record that caused it rather than to a plausible reason.

evidenceHint.en: The completed reconciliation per run, showing both totals, the difference, the transaction-level explanation and the clearing date, attached to the control as an evidence record.

text.en: Compare the despatched count and total against what the receiving system now holds.
Investigate any difference down to the transaction rather than to a plausible cause.
Work the rejection queue to zero, or carry an item forward with an owner and a date.
Sign the reconciliation as preparer and obtain an independent reviewer's approval.
Attach the signed reconciliation to the control as evidence rather than filing it locally.

title.en: Escalate a transfer that failed to run or ran twice

description.en: A reconciliation only proves the run it covers; the run that never started and the batch loaded a second time are caught by watching the schedule, not by comparing totals.

evidenceHint.en: The exception record for each missed or duplicated run, naming the batch, what was reloaded or reversed, and the date the ledger position was corrected.

text.en: Monitor the schedule for a run that did not start or that finished with errors.
Check for a duplicate load by matching batch identifiers against those already received.
Reverse a duplicated load before the ledger closes and record exactly what was reversed.
Raise the missed or duplicated run with the receiving process owner the same day.

title.en: Re-trace a sampled batch from despatch to posted journal

description.en: Agreeing totals proves two numbers match; only following a real batch through proves the numbers describe the records that reached the ledger.

text.en: Select a batch from the sending system's own despatch log, not from the reconciliation file.
Confirm the count and total on that batch against the reconciliation held for the run.
Follow the batch into the receiving system and on to the journal it produced.
Look for records dropped, duplicated, or posted into a later period than they belong.
Return an unexplained difference to the transfer owner with a date to resolve it.

templates.title: Data definitions and ownership documented
templates.description: The dictionary of data elements the financial statements depend on: what each element means, how it is calculated, the values it may take, and the one individual accountable for keeping that definition true.
templates.objective: To ensure every data element the financial statements depend on carries a written meaning, a stated calculation and one named individual accountable for keeping both current.
templates.successCriteria:
The dictionary holds a row for every element a significant account, disclosure or key report depends on.
Each row states what the element means, the calculation applied to produce it, and the values it may legitimately take.
One named individual owns each element, and a team name or job title is not accepted in that field.
A changed definition is approved before the first figure computed under it is published, and the reports it moves are named.
Two reports quoting the same element for one period return the same value, or the divergence is registered with a date to settle it.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export the data dictionary as at period end, giving meaning, calculation, permitted values and owner for each element.
Obtain the list of significant accounts, disclosures and key reports, which establishes which elements are in scope.
Obtain the approval record for every definition change made in the period, with the date each took effect.
Collect two in-scope reports quoting a common element for the same period end.
Obtain the staff roster and the leaver and mover lists covering the period.

Analysis:
Population is every element an in-scope account, disclosure or key report depends on. Test all of them for a meaning, a calculation and an owner, since an absent row cannot be sampled.
Sample ten elements weighted to those feeding material balances and read each calculation for whether a second preparer could apply it unaided.
Recompute one sampled element from the underlying records and compare the result against the value its report returned.
Compare each change approval date against the publication date of the first figure computed under the new definition.
Match every named owner to the roster and to the leaver and mover lists.
Set the two reports side by side on the common element and require an explanation for any divergence.

Output:
Coverage table of in-scope elements against dictionary rows, listing the elements holding no row.
Sample results stating, per element, whether the calculation was followable and whether recomputation agreed.
Schedule of definition changes whose figures were published before the approval was recorded.
List of elements whose owner has left or moved, and of divergences found between the two reports.

title.en: Select the data elements the statements actually depend on

description.en: A dictionary covering everything the databases hold is never finished and never used, so the boundary is drawn at the elements an in-scope account, disclosure or key report consumes.

text.en: Start from the significant accounts, disclosures and key reports inside the scope.
Name the elements each of them consumes, down to the field a report actually reads.
Include elements produced by a calculation as well as those keyed or imported.
Leave out elements no in-scope output depends on, and say where the line was drawn.
Agree the resulting element list with the report owners who consume them.

title.en: Draft the meaning, calculation and permitted values of each element

description.en: Write each row so a preparer who has never met the element computes it the same way twice, which is the test a definition passes before it is worth holding at all.

text.en: State what the element means in business terms before any formula is given.
Write the calculation as an operation on named source fields, not as a description of one.
Give the values the element may take, including how an unknown or a nil is represented.
Name the origin the value arrives from, cross-referring to the data-source register.
Note the reports and balances consuming the element, so a later change can be aimed.

title.en: Name one accountable individual against every element

description.en: An element owned by a team has nobody who can approve its definition, so ownership sits with a person and is handed over explicitly when that person moves on.

text.en: Put one individual in the owner field rather than a team or a job family.
Confirm the named owner accepts the element and can explain its calculation.
Set the review date on the row so the next check is computed rather than remembered.
Reassign ownership explicitly when the holder changes role, recording the handover date.

title.en: Approve a changed definition before figures computed under it are published

description.en: A definition that moves without a decision republishes history quietly: one account is computed two ways across two periods and the comparative stops meaning anything.

evidenceHint.en: The approval record for each definition change, naming the previous and new calculation, the approver, the effective date, and the reports reissued under it.

text.en: Raise the proposed wording and calculation against the dictionary row it replaces.
Quantify which reports and balances the change moves, and by how much on the last period.
Obtain the element owner's and the controller's decision before the effective date.
Publish the new row with its effective date and keep the superseded text readable.
Tell the consumers named on the row which reports change, and from which period.

title.en: Compare a common element across two reports for divergent values

description.en: The cheapest evidence that a definition is missing, ambiguous or ignored is two reports quoting one element for one period and disagreeing about it.

text.en: Choose an element that at least two in-scope reports quote for the same period.
Pull both values and express the difference in amount and in percentage terms.
Trace each report back to the calculation it actually applied to produce its figure.
Judge whether the dictionary row is silent, ambiguous, or simply being ignored.
Register each divergence with the element owner and a date to settle the definition.

templates.title: Control responsibilities communicated to performers
templates.description: The standing account each performer is given of the control they operate - the act, its timing, the evidence to retain and the route to use when it cannot be run - reaching everyone in post rather than only those who joined this period.
templates.objective: To ensure every person performing a control holds a current statement of what that control asks of them, and can say it back when asked rather than merely having been sent it.
templates.successCriteria:
Every performer in the control register holds a current statement of the control, its timing and the evidence it must leave.
Delivery is recorded against the individual, so a posting to a shared site or a distribution list counts as undelivered.
The version a performer holds matches the register entry in force, and anyone holding a superseded one is named.
Sampled performers describe their own duty unprompted, which is what separates communication from distribution.
Coverage is reported over the register population as denominator, with performers holding nothing named.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export the control register as at the cycle date, which gives the performer population every figure below is measured against.
Obtain the statement issued for each control, carrying its version and the date it was released.
Obtain the per-person delivery and acknowledgement record, showing who received which version and when.
Obtain the register's change history for the cycle, so a held version can be compared with the entry in force.
Collect the responses from the comprehension exercise run in the period, each with the date it was taken.

Analysis:
Reconcile the register's performer population against the delivery record and isolate performers with no statement at all.
Sample 25 performers, or all of them where fewer, and compare the version each holds against the register entry in force on that date.
Put the question to the sampled performers first and set their answer beside the register entry, not beside the statement text.
Test whether each delivery resolves to an individual, treating an intranet posting or a distribution list as undelivered.
Compare acknowledgement dates against the cycle window and count those recorded after it closed.

Output:
Coverage stated as performers reached over the register population, naming every performer holding no statement.
List of performers holding a superseded version, with the control and the days since that version changed.
The sampled performers' own accounts of their duty set against the register, naming each mismatch.
A statement of the sample size, the population it was drawn from and the exceptions found.

title.en: Scope the performer population the statement must reach

description.en: Settle who the communication is owed to before anything is written, taking the register down to individuals and adding the reviewers whose act the control also depends on.

text.en: Export the control register at the cycle date with the performer recorded against each entry.
Resolve entries sitting against a team or a shared mailbox to the individual who does the work.
Add the reviewers and approvers the control depends on, not only the person who runs it.
Fix that population as the denominator this cycle's coverage will be reported against.

title.en: Frame the statement a performer receives for their own control

description.en: Compose what one performer is handed for one control, in operational terms rather than register shorthand, and stop at what they must do rather than how they will be judged on it.

text.en: State the act the control requires, in the words the performer would use for it.
Name the date or trigger it falls due on, and the evidence the performer must retain.
Name the route to use when the control cannot be performed as stated.
Version the statement and bind it to the register entry it was written from.
Hold it to what the performer must do, leaving how they are graded to the objective cycle.

title.en: Send each performer the statement for the controls recorded against them

description.en: Get the current version into the hands of every named holder and record receipt individually, so coverage can be counted rather than assumed from the fact that something was published.

evidenceHint.en: The cycle's delivery log showing each performer, the version they were sent, and the date they acknowledged receiving it.

text.en: Work through the register and give each holder what it records against them.
Record the acknowledgement against the individual, not against the team they sit in.
Chase the performers who have not acknowledged before the cycle window closes.
Withdraw superseded versions so nobody acts on a statement no longer in force.
Report the performers still holding nothing at the close of the window.

title.en: Poll a sample of performers on the duty they believe they hold

description.en: Test what actually landed by asking performers to describe their own duty cold, because a signed acknowledgement proves receipt and nothing more.

text.en: Draw a sample of performers across cycles, locations and lengths of service.
Ask each what they perform and when it falls due, before showing them anything.
Set the answer beside the register entry rather than beside the statement text.
Treat a mismatch as a communication failure and name the control it concerns.
Report the sample size, the population it came from and every mismatch found.

templates.title: Escalation channels for control failures communicated
templates.description: The route a performer uses to report that a control did not operate, was skipped, or threw an exception they cannot clear: a named recipient in the reporting function, a published response window, and a rule that keeps it apart from the confidential channel for conduct concerns.
templates.objective: To ensure a person who finds that a control has not operated knows which route carries that report, and that it reaches a recipient able to act on it inside a published window.
templates.successCriteria:
The route is published to every performer, naming its recipient, the contents a report needs and the answering window.
It is held apart from the confidential conduct channel, and a report on the wrong route is moved rather than answered there.
Each logged report names the control, the occurrence that failed and the date found, so it matches the control register.
Reports are acknowledged inside the published window, and those that are not are aged and chased against a named recipient.
A report naming a control the recipient owns passes to the deputy rather than being triaged by the person answerable.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the published description of the route, naming its recipient, deputy, response window and the contents a report must carry.
Export the failure report log for the period, the population across which acknowledgement and closure timing are measured.
Draw the performer list from the control register, which is the population publicity coverage is measured against.
Collect the test submissions raised in the period, with the date each was sent and the date a recipient answered.
Obtain the confidential conduct channel's case log for the period, to find control failures that arrived on the wrong route.

Analysis:
Match every logged report to a control register entry and isolate those naming no control or an occurrence with no date.
Measure acknowledgement against the published window across the whole log, not a sample, since the log is small enough to take entire.
Sample 25 reports, or all where fewer, and trace each to the owner it was passed to and the answer that closed it.
Read the conduct channel's log for control failures raised there, and time how long each took to be redirected.
Test the deputy arm by isolating reports naming a control the recipient owns, and check who triaged them.

Output:
Schedule of reports against the published window, naming every one acknowledged late with the days taken.
List of reports that could not be tied to a control register entry, with the wording each carried instead.
Count of control failures that arrived on the conduct channel, and the interval before each was redirected.
Names of reports triaged by the recipient whose own area the failed control sits in.

title.en: Separate a failed control report from a conduct concern at intake

description.en: Draw the line between the two routes before either is publicised, so a performer knows which one their situation belongs on and a misrouted item has a stated way back.

text.en: Set out what belongs on this route: a control that did not operate, as against an allegation about a person.
Agree the redirection rule and the window inside which a misrouted report is moved.
Name what a failure report must contain - the control, the occurrence and the date found.
Decide which failures must be reported at once and which can wait for the next cycle.

title.en: Attach a named recipient, a deputy and a response window to the route

description.en: Stand the route up as something a report can actually arrive at: a person who receives it, a substitute for when they are conflicted, and a stated time by which the reporter hears back.

text.en: Name the recipient who takes failure reports and can act on the control named.
Name a deputy to take the reports that concern the recipient's own area.
Set the acknowledgement window, and what the reporter is told once it passes.
Build log fields that tie each report to the control register entry it names.
Configure the intake so a report cannot be filed without naming a control.

title.en: Publish the route beside the control instructions each performer holds

description.en: Put the route where a failure is actually discovered rather than on a policy page nobody opens mid-close, and say plainly what belongs on the confidential channel instead.

evidenceHint.en: The route as published in the period, carrying the recipient, the response window and the required contents, with the date it was posted.

text.en: Carry the route into the statement each performer holds for their control.
Repeat it where exceptions already surface, such as reconciliation and close checklists.
State beside it which concerns belong on the confidential channel instead.
Withdraw stale contact details that would send a report to a recipient who has moved.

title.en: Triage each reported failure to the owner who must answer it

description.en: Work the arriving reports: acknowledge inside the window, hand each to the owner of the control it names, and move anything that turns out to be a conduct allegation.

evidenceHint.en: The period's report log showing, per entry, the control named, the acknowledgement date, and the owner it was passed to.

text.en: Acknowledge each arriving report inside the published window and record the date.
Pass reports touching the recipient's own controls to the named deputy instead.
Assign each report to the owner of the control it names, with a date to answer by.
Age the reports still unanswered and chase them against a named recipient.
Move a conduct allegation to the confidential channel and record that it went.

title.en: Re-perform a failure report and follow it to the recipient

description.en: Raise a controlled report through the live route and watch where it lands, including one naming a control the recipient owns, which is the case the deputy exists for.

text.en: Raise a controlled report naming a real control and a dated occurrence.
Time the interval from submission to the acknowledgement the reporter receives.
Check it reached the published recipient rather than a general mailbox.
Repeat for a control the recipient owns, and check the deputy took it.
Record any published detail that no longer reaches a live recipient.

templates.title: Control changes communicated to affected personnel
templates.description: What the people a control change lands on are told before it takes effect - the act that alters, from which date, and what they must now retain - as distinct from the amended documentation being versioned and filed.
templates.objective: To ensure the performers and reviewers a control change lands on are told what alters for them, and from which date, before the amended control first falls due.
templates.successCriteria:
Every amendment, retirement and addition in the change log has a named audience identified before its effective date.
The notice says what alters for the reader - the act, its timing, the evidence or the recipient - not a version number.
The notice is dated on or before the effective date, and one issued later is reported as late with the days counted.
The first occurrence under the new design is performed by somebody recorded as having received the notice for it.
A retirement is notified as plainly as an amendment, so nobody goes on performing a control that has been withdrawn.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export the control change log for the period - every amendment, retirement and addition with its effective date - as the population each test below runs over.
Obtain the audience recorded for each change, naming performers, reviewers and the functions that feed the control.
Collect the notices issued, with the date each went out and the distribution it went to.
Obtain the first execution record under each amended design, showing who performed it.
Obtain the register entry before and after each change, to establish what actually altered for the reader.

Analysis:
Reconcile the change log against the notices issued and isolate changes that took effect with nothing sent.
Sample 25 changes, or all where fewer, and compare issue date with effective date, counting the days where the notice came late.
Read the sampled notices for the act that altered, and separate those that cite only a version or a library location.
Match the performer of each first occurrence against the distribution list for that change.
Take the retirements as their own population, since a withdrawn control produces no evidence to expose a missing notice.

Output:
List of changes effective in the period with no notice issued, naming the control and its effective date.
The days late for every notice that went out after its change had taken effect.
Names of first performers absent from the distribution for the change they operated under.
A statement of the sample drawn, the population it came from and the exceptions found.

title.en: Enumerate who a pending control change actually lands on

description.en: Work out the audience from the change itself rather than from a standing mailing list, including the functions upstream whose input or timing the change quietly alters.

text.en: Read the approved change and list the controls it amends, retires or adds.
Name the performers and reviewers recorded against each affected control.
Add the upstream functions whose input or timing the change alters.
Record that audience against the change before its effective date arrives.

title.en: Draft a notice form that states what alters for the reader

description.en: Settle the shape of the message so it carries the operational difference rather than a version reference, and fix the lead time by which it must reach the audience.

text.en: Set the fields it must carry: the control, what alters, and from when.
Require the act to be described, not referred to by version number alone.
Keep the notice distinct from the document library, which records rather than tells.
Agree who signs a notice off before it goes to the affected audience.
Fix the lead time by which it must reach the audience ahead of the effective date.

title.en: Issue the notice to the recorded audience inside the lead time

description.en: Get the message out before the amended control first falls due, and treat a withdrawal as needing saying just as plainly as an amendment does.

evidenceHint.en: Each notice as issued, with its date and distribution, set against the effective date the change log records for that change.

text.en: Check the audience recorded against the change before anything goes out.
Say what the reader must now do differently, and from which date.
Confirm the first performer under the new design was on the distribution.
Notify a retirement as plainly as an amendment, naming the control withdrawn.
Record the issue date against the change log entry it answers.

title.en: Match the change log against the notices actually issued

description.en: Compare the two records independently of the people who issued the notices, and count lateness in days rather than reporting it as sent or not sent.

text.en: Take the change log for the period from the system rather than from a pack.
Identify changes that took effect with no notice issued to anybody.
Count the days between effective date and issue date for every late notice.
Trace the first occurrence under each change to the distribution it was on.
Report the exceptions with the control and the effective date named.

title.en: Sweep for retired controls that are still being performed

description.en: Look for work still being done on controls that were withdrawn, which is the failure a missing retirement notice leaves behind and the one no evidence expectation will surface.

text.en: List the controls retired in the period, taken from the change log.
Look for evidence produced against them after the retirement date.
Ask the last recorded performer whether they were told it had been withdrawn.
Report each retirement whose notice never reached the people performing it.

templates.title: External reporting channels and spokespersons defined
templates.description: Who may speak for the organization to an outside party on a matter affecting financial reporting or internal control, the channel each audience is answered on, and what anyone else does when approached instead of answering.
