templates.objective: To ensure a statement reaching an outside party on a matter affecting financial reporting comes from a person authorised to make it, on a channel the organization can later produce.
templates.successCriteria:
A current schedule names, for every external audience, the person authorised to speak to it and the deputy who acts in their absence.
The channel each audience is answered on is stated, so a release on any other channel can be identified as one.
Anyone approached who is not on the schedule refers it instead of answering, and the referral is recorded the day it arrives.
A statement bearing on financial reporting is approved before release by the function owning its subject, and that version is issued.
Authority is withdrawn when a spokesperson leaves or changes role, and the schedule carries the withdrawal date.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the spokesperson schedule in force during the period, with its approval date and the audiences it covers.
Obtain the register of external approaches and referrals for the period, which is the population the referral tests are drawn from.
Collect the statements issued to outside parties in the period - investor and analyst material, media comment, customer and supplier assurances - with the pre-release review record for each.
Obtain the leaver and internal-mover report from HR covering the same period.
Obtain the published channel list showing the address, portal or account each audience is answered on.

Analysis:
Sample twenty issued statements, stratified so every audience contributing more than one statement is represented, and compare each author against the schedule as it stood on that date.
Check the channel each sampled statement left on against the channel named for its audience.
Re-perform the pre-release review on ten statements bearing on financial reporting, comparing the approved draft with the version actually issued.
Reconcile the schedule against the leaver and mover report and measure the days between a departure and the withdrawal of authority.
Take every referral in the register and test whether it reached an authorised spokesperson, and how long that took.

Output:
Schedule of audiences against the spokesperson and deputy named for each, naming any audience covered by neither.
List of statements traced to an unauthorised author or released on an unlisted channel, with the date of each.
Differences between approved drafts and issued versions, naming the statement and its reviewer.
Ageing of referrals that never reached an authorised spokesperson, and of authority left standing after a departure.

title.en: Delimit who may speak for the organization to each outside audience

description.en: Work out which outside parties receive statements bearing on financial reporting or internal control, and settle how much authority answering each of them requires.

text.en: Enumerate the outside parties that ask about financial reporting or control matters.
Separate the audiences where a wrong answer creates a disclosure or reporting exposure.
Decide the seniority an answer to each audience requires before it may be given.
Settle what a person not on the schedule does when approached, and who they hand it to.
Fix the channel each audience is answered on, and rule the remaining routes out.

title.en: Publish the spokesperson schedule beside the channels it authorises

description.en: Turn those decisions into a named schedule people can consult before answering, and put it where an approached employee will actually meet it.

text.en: Appoint a spokesperson and a deputy for every audience on the schedule.
State the address, portal or account each audience is answered on.
Obtain approval from the executive carrying the disclosure exposure.
Place the schedule in induction material, the policy site and the reception script.
Open the referral route an unauthorised person uses, naming its recipient.

title.en: Route each external approach to the person authorised to answer it

description.en: Take approaches as they arrive, hand each to the spokesperson named for that audience or the deputy, and keep the record showing who answered and where the answer went out.

evidenceHint.en: The approach and referral register for the period, each entry carrying the date received, the audience it came from, who it was handed to and the channel the answer left on.

text.en: Log every external approach on the day it arrives, with the audience behind it.
Hand the approach to the spokesperson named for that audience, or the deputy.
Refer rather than answer when the approach reaches someone without authority.
Review a statement bearing on financial reporting before release, keeping the approved draft.
Capture the channel the answer went out on, so an off-channel release is visible.

title.en: Trace issued statements back to the authority that permitted them

description.en: Independently assemble what actually went out during the period and test each statement against the schedule in force on its date and against the channel list.

text.en: Assemble the period's statements from the audiences themselves, not from the register.
Compare each statement's author with the schedule as it stood on that date.
Check the channel used against the one named for that audience.
Reconcile the schedule to leavers and movers, naming authority never withdrawn.
Report unauthorised statements to the executive that approved the schedule.

templates.title: Communication protocol for regulators and auditors
templates.description: The route a request from a regulator, the external auditor or another oversight body travels: one point of receipt, a logged request, a response approved before it leaves, and a record of what was released and what was promised.
templates.objective: To ensure a request from a regulator or an external auditor is received at one point, answered from reviewed material, and closed with a record of what was released and when.
templates.successCriteria:
Every request from an external oversight body - regulator, external auditor, tax authority or exchange - enters one log carrying its date and deadline.
A response leaves only after the named reviewer for its subject matter approves it, and the approved version is the one released.
What was released is retained as released, so a later question about consistency is answered from the record rather than from memory.
A commitment given to an external body carries an owner and a due date, and its closure is evidenced.
A request answered after its deadline is recorded with the days it ran over and the reason.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the external request log for the period, the population the sampling below is drawn from, with the date received and deadline of each entry.
Obtain the correspondence held for each external body dealt with in the period, taken from the mailbox or portal rather than from the log.
Collect the approved response and the material as released for the sampled requests, together with the reviewer's approval.
Obtain the register of commitments given to external bodies, with owner, due date and closure evidence.
Obtain the release records - the time-limited shares issued to an external body, their expiry and revocation dates, and any request returned through them.

Analysis:
Reconcile the correspondence against the request log and name every request that never reached the log.
Sample twenty requests, taking all those above the materiality the protocol sets and ten at random below it, and trace each to the response actually sent.
Compare the material released with the version approved, and report any figure or statement released without approval.
Re-perform the elapsed-days calculation on every request answered late and read the reason recorded against it.
Test each commitment in the register against its due date and agree those marked closed to their evidence.
Check whether a share issued to an external body was revoked or expired once its request closed.

Output:
Reconciliation of correspondence to the request log, naming requests handled outside it.
Schedule of sampled requests against their responses, with days taken and the deadline each carried.
List of releases made without the named reviewer's approval or differing from the approved version.
Ageing of open commitments with the owner of each, and of shares still live after their request closed.

title.en: Settle the point of receipt and the approval a response must carry

description.en: Decide where a request from an external body lands, who owns the log it enters, and what approval any material must carry before it leaves the organization.

text.en: Name the external bodies the protocol covers, and those it deliberately does not.
Appoint a single point of receipt, with a deputy for absence and for conflicts.
Set the approval a response needs, by subject matter and by materiality.
Decide what is retained of each release, in what form and for how long.
State how a request arriving elsewhere is redirected into the log.

title.en: Build the request log and the release record beside it

description.en: Create the log the protocol depends on, with the fields that make a deadline computable and every release traceable to the approval that permitted it.

text.en: Open one log for external requests, carrying body, subject, date received and deadline.
Add the approval field naming the reviewer and the version they approved.
Attach the released material to its entry in the form it was released in.
Bind the commitment register to the log so a promise keeps its request.
Configure a time-limited, revocable share for material leaving the organization.

title.en: Issue each response from reviewed material inside its deadline

description.en: Work the live queue: log the request on arrival, have the response reviewed by the function that owns the subject, release it on a recorded channel and close the entry against its deadline.

evidenceHint.en: The external request log for the period, each entry showing the body, the date received, the reviewer who approved the response, the material released and the date it was issued.

text.en: Log the request on arrival with the body, the subject and the deadline it sets.
Route it for drafting to the function that owns the subject matter.
Obtain the named reviewer's approval before any material leaves.
Release on a time-limited share and capture the date it was issued.
Close the entry against its deadline, recording the reason for any overrun.
Raise any commitment given into the register with an owner and a due date.

title.en: Contrast the correspondence file with the request log

description.en: Test the log for completeness from outside it, reading the mailboxes and portals the external bodies actually used, and find the requests handled off the record.

text.en: Pull the period's correspondence from each external body's mailbox or portal.
Match every item to a log entry and name the requests that never reached it.
Re-perform the elapsed-days calculation on twenty answered requests.
Compare released material against the approved version and report any difference.
Check that shares issued to external bodies were revoked once their request closed.

templates.title: External feedback and complaints routed and actioned
templates.description: What arrives from customers, suppliers, banks and service providers about invoices, balances and statements: routed to a named owner, actioned to a correction, and read for the control failure it may be reporting. A conduct concern raised in confidence travels the confidential channel instead.
templates.objective: To ensure feedback arriving from a customer, supplier or bank reaches a named owner, is actioned to a correction, and is read for what it says about a control that failed.
templates.successCriteria:
Every intake point an outside party can reach - billing disputes, supplier claims, bank differences and provider notices - delivers into one queue.
Each arriving item is assigned to a named owner inside the stated routing window, so nothing sits unowned.
An item whose recorded cause is a control that did not operate is raised as a deficiency, not closed as a one-off correction.
Closure is evidenced by the correction made, and the outside party is told the outcome where one was asked for.
The period's items are read for pattern, and a recurring cause is put to the process owner who can remove it.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the period's items from each intake system directly - billing, accounts payable, treasury and the provider notice mailbox - which is the completeness population.
Obtain the routing queue itself, showing arrival date, assigned owner and the date of assignment for each item.
Collect the closure evidence for the sampled items - credit note, adjusting entry, reconciliation or correspondence - and the reply sent to the outside party.
Obtain the deficiency log for the period, against which items with a control cause are tested.
Obtain the period's cause analysis and the notes issued to process owners.

Analysis:
Reconcile the intake population to the routing queue and name every item that never entered it.
Measure arrival-to-assignment for every queued item and compare the distribution against the stated routing window.
Sample twenty-five closed items, stratified so each intake point contributes at least one, and agree every closure to its evidence.
Take the items whose recorded cause is a control failure and trace each into the deficiency log; one corrected without a deficiency raised is a routing failure, not an accounting one.
Age every open item against its arrival date and read the reason recorded for any beyond the window.
Re-perform the cause analysis on the period's population and compare the recurring causes it yields with those reported.

Output:
Reconciliation of intake systems to the routing queue, naming items handled outside it.
Distribution of arrival-to-assignment intervals against the routing window, naming the items outside it.
Sampled closures agreed to evidence, naming any closed with no correction made.
List of control-caused items that never reached the deficiency log, with the ageing of items still open.

title.en: Enumerate the intake points an outside party can reach

description.en: Find every route by which a customer, supplier, bank or provider raises something, including the inboxes and phone lines that appear on no process map.

text.en: Trace how a customer billing dispute reaches the organization today, end to end.
Add the supplier, bank and service-provider routes to the same inventory.
Name an owner for each route and the queue it must deliver into.
Set the window inside which an arriving item must be assigned.
Separate conduct concerns, which travel the confidential channel instead.

title.en: Connect every intake point to one routing queue

description.en: Make the queue the single place an external item lives, with the fields that let routing time be measured and a control cause be escalated rather than absorbed.

text.en: Feed each intake point into the queue, retiring the private inbox it used.
Add arrival date, owner and routing date so the interval is computed, not typed.
Add a cause field separating a one-off error from a control that did not operate.
Link the queue to the deficiency log so a control cause is raised in one step.
Set the reply the outside party receives when their item is closed.

title.en: Assign each arriving item and drive it to a closed correction

description.en: Work the queue day to day: give every arriving item an owner inside the window, action it to a correction, and decide in each case whether a failed control sits behind it.

evidenceHint.en: The routing queue export for the period showing each item's arrival date, assigned owner, date of assignment, recorded cause and the closure evidence attached to it.

text.en: Assign each arriving item to an owner inside the routing window.
Capture the cause, separating a one-off error from a failed control.
Raise a deficiency where the cause is a control that did not operate.
Attach the correction - credit note, adjusting entry or reconciliation - to the item.
Tell the outside party the outcome where they asked to be told.

title.en: Summarise the period's items by cause and put recurring ones to their owner

description.en: Read the closed population as a whole rather than item by item, and place each recurring cause in front of the process owner who can remove it.

evidenceHint.en: The period's cause analysis showing the item count and value behind each recurring cause, with the note issued to each process owner named in it.

text.en: Group the period's items by recorded cause and by intake point.
Rank the causes by item count and by the value corrected.
Name the process owner each recurring cause belongs to.
Issue the analysis to those owners with the items behind each cause.
Carry an unresolved recurring cause into the next period's analysis.

title.en: Sweep the source systems for items the queue never saw

description.en: Test completeness from outside the queue by reading the intake systems themselves, then judge whether recurring causes were reported or quietly absorbed.

text.en: Extract the period's items from each intake system, not from the queue.
Match them to queue entries and name every item handled off the record.
Agree a sample of twenty-five closures to the correction evidence held.
Check that items caused by a control failure reached the deficiency log.
Compare the recurring causes in the population with those reported to owners.

templates.title: Annual monitoring plan covering key controls defined
templates.description: A dated plan, settled before the period opens, that says which controls will be evaluated during it, by whom, how often, and by which method - monitoring built into the process itself, or an evaluation conducted separately from it.
templates.objective: To ensure every control the organization relies on for financial reporting appears in an approved plan that fixes its evaluator, method and frequency before the period opens.
templates.successCriteria:
Every control the register marks as key carries a line, and each omission is reasoned in writing and approved.
Each line names an evaluator, a method, a frequency and the quarter the evaluation falls in.
Each line is marked as monitoring inside the process or as a separate evaluation, and the separate ones say whether the evaluator is independent of the control.
Approval predates the period, and the plan is attached to the audit cycle the period's evidence is assembled under.
Versions issued after approval carry a date and a reason, so coverage withdrawn mid-period stays visible.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved monitoring plan for the period, its approval record, and every version issued afterwards.
Obtain the control register as it stood at approval with the attribute marking a control as key; this register is the population the plan's coverage is measured against.
Obtain the audit cycle opened for the period, with the framework key and period dates recorded on it.
Request the written reason held for each key control the plan does not cover.
Collect the evaluator assignment behind each line, including whether that evaluator sits outside the process being evaluated.

Analysis:
Reconcile key controls in the register against plan lines and isolate every key control with no line and every line with no control.
For twenty-five lines, or all of them where fewer, confirm the evaluator, method, frequency and period are all stated rather than implied.
Split the lines by method and compare the proportion evaluated independently against the controls management says it relies upon most heavily.
Compare the approval date with the first day of the period, and read each later version for coverage removed rather than added.
Trace the plan to the audit cycle it hangs from and confirm the framework and period on that cycle agree with the plan.

Output:
A coverage reconciliation naming each key control absent from the plan, with the reason held for it or the absence of one.
The count of lines incomplete in any of the four required fields, with those lines named.
A version history showing what each post-approval change did to coverage and who approved it.
A statement of the sample size, the population drawn from, and the exceptions found.

title.en: Delimit the population of controls the plan has to cover

description.en: Settle which controls are relied upon for financial reporting before anything is scheduled, because a plan built on an unstated population cannot be shown to have covered it.

text.en: Export the control register with the attribute that marks a control as key, dated at export.
Confirm each key marking against the account or assertion the control is relied upon for.
Refer contested markings to the process owner and record the outcome against the control.
Freeze the resulting list as the coverage population the plan will be measured against.

title.en: Timetable each evaluation against an evaluator and a method

description.en: Turn the population into scheduled lines, each naming who performs the evaluation, by what method and in which part of the period, so the plan can be tested line by line.

text.en: Assign every control in the population to a named evaluator rather than to a function.
Mark each line as monitoring inside the process or as an evaluation conducted apart from it.
State, for each evaluation of the second kind, whether its evaluator is independent of the control.
Place each line in a quarter, so the period's workload is visible before it starts.
Obtain approval of the completed plan and record the date it was given.

title.en: Open the audit cycle the period's evidence will hang from

description.en: Attach the approved plan to the audit cycle for the framework and period, so evaluations, evidence and readiness snapshots accumulate against one engagement instead of being gathered again at year end.

evidenceHint.en: The approved plan with its approval date, and the audit cycle record showing the framework key, the period dates and the plan attached to it.

text.en: Create the audit cycle for the framework, naming the period start and end dates.
Attach the approved plan version to that cycle as the scope it will be worked to.
Point each planned evaluation at the control it covers, so completion can be read per control.
Record the readiness position at the opening of the period as the baseline for the year.
Publish the cycle to the evaluators named in the plan and confirm each can see their lines.

title.en: Amend the plan where the control population has moved since approval

description.en: Check partway through the period whether controls have become key since approval or fallen out of scope, while the schedule can still be changed rather than explained after the fact.

evidenceHint.en: The dated mid-period comparison, naming every newly key control that has no scheduled line and every scheduled line whose control has since been retired or merged.

text.en: Pull the control register again at the mid-period date and compare it to the frozen population.
Name each newly key control that the plan has no line for and the quarter it can still fit.
Name each plan line whose control has been retired or merged since approval.
Put the additions and removals to the plan's owner for a versioned amendment.
Report how much of the period's schedule has been completed to date against what it scheduled.

templates.title: Control self-assessments executed per plan
templates.description: The evaluations the plan assigns to the people who run the control: performed on the schedule set, answered from named evidence rather than recollection, and recorded as what they are - an assessment by the control's own owner.
templates.objective: To ensure each control the plan schedules for self-assessment is assessed within its quarter, from evidence the assessor names, and recorded as an assessment made by the control's own owner.
templates.successCriteria:
Every self-assessment scheduled for the quarter is completed inside it, and a late one carries the date finished and the reason it slipped.
Each answer cites the documents, the sample and the period examined, not the assessor's confidence.
The record names the assessor and their relationship to the control, so one performed by the control's own owner is identifiable as such.
No line the plan scheduled for independent evaluation is closed by a self-assessment instead.
A conclusion that the control did not operate raises a finding inside the quarter rather than resting in the assessment record.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the plan's self-assessment lines for the period; these lines, not the assessments returned, are the population completeness is measured against.
Obtain the completed self-assessment records with their submission dates and the identity of each assessor.
Obtain the control register's owner field, which is what makes an assessor's relationship to the control testable rather than self-declared.
Collect the evidence cited by each assessment, through the evidence links attached to the control.
Obtain the findings raised in the period and the self-assessment each was raised from.

Analysis:
Compare scheduled lines against completed records and measure, for each completion, the days between the quarter end and submission.
Re-perform ten self-assessments, or all where fewer, by examining the cited evidence and reaching an independent conclusion on the same material.
Match each assessor against the control's owner and count the assessments performed by the person accountable for the control being assessed.
Isolate plan lines requiring an independent evaluation that were closed by a self-assessment instead.
Trace every negative conclusion to a finding and measure the days between the conclusion and the finding being raised.

Output:
A completeness schedule of scheduled against completed assessments, with the lateness of each in days.
Re-performance results naming every assessment whose cited evidence does not support the conclusion recorded.
The count and the proportion of assessments performed by the control's own owner, stated as a limitation on the weight the evaluation carries.
A list of independent-evaluation lines closed by self-assessment, and of negative conclusions never raised as findings.

title.en: Draw the quarter's assessment population from the approved plan

description.en: Take the quarter's work from the plan rather than from whoever responds, so an assessment that was never returned is an exception instead of an absence nobody notices.

text.en: Extract the plan lines whose scheduled quarter is the one now opening.
Resolve each line to the person who runs the control, by name and not by team.
Separate the lines the plan reserved for an independent evaluator and exclude them here.
Issue the resulting list as the quarter's population, dated and held for comparison at close.

title.en: Draft questions an assessor can only answer from evidence

description.en: Word the assessment so each response has to name the documents, the sample and the period examined, which is what separates an evaluation from a statement of confidence.

text.en: Write each question to ask what was examined, over what period, and with what result.
Require a sample size and a source system on any question about a recurring activity.
Add a field capturing the assessor's relationship to the control being assessed.
Reject free-text confidence ratings as an acceptable answer to any question asked.
Pilot the wording on two controls and redraft the questions that produced unusable answers.

title.en: Assess each scheduled control and attach what was relied on

description.en: Work the quarter's population, answering from the material actually examined and linking that material to the control so a later reviewer reaches it without asking the assessor.

evidenceHint.en: The completed assessment record for each scheduled control, with its submission date, the assessor named, and the evidence items linked to the control that the answers cite.

text.en: Examine the documents and samples the questions call for, over the stated period.
Answer each question from that material and cite the items it rests on.
Attach the cited items to the control as evidence rather than holding them locally.
State the assessor's relationship to the control on the face of the record.
Submit inside the quarter, or record the date completed and why it moved.

title.en: Re-perform a sample from outside the process assessed

description.en: Have someone with no responsibility for the control examine the same evidence and reach their own conclusion, because an evaluation by those who own the control is weaker evidence than one that is not, and the difference is only visible when both exist.

evidenceHint.en: The re-performance working papers for the sampled assessments, showing the evidence examined, the independent conclusion reached, and each difference from the conclusion recorded by the owner.

text.en: Select the sample from the completed population, weighted to the controls relied upon most.
Examine the cited evidence directly, without the assessor's summary of it.
Reach a conclusion on the same material and record where it differs from the owner's.
Report the proportion of the quarter assessed only by the people who run the control.
Refer differences to the plan's owner for a separate evaluation of the control concerned.

templates.title: Automated exception and KPI monitoring operating
templates.description: Monitoring built into the processing itself: scheduled jobs that test a stated condition against a stated threshold, raise what breaches it into a queue, and are worked to a disposition each business day.
templates.objective: To ensure the automated monitors run as scheduled each day, that what they raise reaches a queue with an owner, and that every item there is dispositioned within the time the organization has set.
templates.successCriteria:
Every monitor records a completed run for each scheduled day, and a day with no run is investigated rather than read as a quiet one.
Each item raised carries the condition breached, the source system and the record involved.
Items are dispositioned inside the stated time, and the disposition names what was examined and what was done.
A monitor that has raised nothing over the stated interval is proved alive by a deliberately seeded item.
An item whose disposition shows a control failed is raised as a finding rather than closed in the queue alone.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the monitor inventory: each monitor's condition, threshold, source system, schedule and the queue its output lands in.
Obtain the scheduler's run history for the period, which is the population run completeness is measured against; the queue is not, because a monitor that did not run raises nothing.
Obtain the exception queue for the period with the raised and dispositioned timestamps on every item.
Obtain the stated disposition time and the escalation route for an item that passes it.
Collect the seeded test items used to prove the quiet monitors, with the dates they were raised and cleared.

Analysis:
Compare scheduled runs against completed runs per monitor and list every missed day, monitor by monitor.
Age the queue: measure raised-to-dispositioned for every item and compare each against the stated time.
Read the disposition text on twenty-five items, or all where fewer, for a statement of what was examined rather than a closing code alone.
Rank monitors by items raised and examine every monitor that raised none, tying each to a seeded item that it detected.
Trace items whose disposition shows a control failure through to the finding raised from them.

Output:
A run-completeness table by monitor and day, naming every missed run and the days it went unnoticed.
An ageing of the queue against the stated disposition time, with the oldest open items and their owners.
A list of monitors that raised nothing in the period, each marked as proved alive by a seeded item or not proved at all.
The count of dispositions carrying no statement of what was examined, out of the number read.

title.en: Enumerate the conditions the monitors are meant to catch

description.en: Write down what each automated check is for before configuring anything, so the inventory records a tested condition and a threshold rather than the name of a job.

text.en: List the errors and breaches the process needs caught between its manual controls.
State the condition and the threshold that identifies each one in the data.
Name the source system and the field the condition is evaluated against.
Agree who disposes of items from each monitor and how quickly they must do it.

title.en: Configure the schedules, thresholds and the queue items land in

description.en: Build the monitors to the inventory, routing what they raise to a queue with a named owner rather than to a mailbox, so an unworked item is visible to someone other than its recipient.

text.en: Implement each condition against the source system named in the inventory.
Schedule the run and record what a completed run writes to the run history.
Route raised items to the queue with the condition and the record identifier attached.
Configure an alert for a scheduled run that does not complete, sent to the monitor's owner.
Test each monitor against a record known to breach its threshold before it goes live.

title.en: Triage the day's items and record what each disposition rests on

description.en: Work the queue every business day, examining the underlying record for each item and writing down what was found rather than closing it with a reason code.

evidenceHint.en: The run history showing each monitor completed for the day, alongside the queue entries raised that day with their dispositions, the examiner named and the time taken.

text.en: Confirm every scheduled monitor completed its run before working the queue.
Examine the underlying record for each raised item in the source system.
Record what was examined and what was done, not only that the item was closed.
Raise a finding where the disposition shows a control failed rather than a false positive.
Escalate anything still open past the stated time, naming the item and its age.

title.en: Seed a known breach to prove a silent monitor is alive

description.en: Put a record that must breach the threshold through each monitor that has raised nothing for a while, because a quiet monitor and a broken one look identical from the queue.

evidenceHint.en: The seeded record for each quiet monitor, the queue entry it produced with its timestamp, and the removal of the test record from the source system afterwards.

text.en: Identify every monitor that has raised nothing over the stated interval.
Construct a record that breaches its threshold and introduce it in a controlled way.
Confirm the item reached the queue, with the condition and record shown correctly.
Withdraw the seeded record and note the withdrawal against the monitor tested.
Report any monitor that failed to raise the seeded item as an unmonitored process.

templates.title: Monitoring results reported to management
templates.description: The periodic account to the executive forum that runs the business: how much of the monitoring plan has been performed, what the evaluations and the automated queues found, and which of those results management is being asked to act on.
templates.objective: To ensure management receives, on a fixed cadence, what the period's monitoring has performed and found, together with the decisions it is being asked to take on results already known.
templates.successCriteria:
A report reaches the named management forum for every month, and a month without one records the reason.
Each report states plan completion against what was scheduled to that date, including work not yet performed.
Self-assessment and queue results are carried with their owner and their age, not as a count of items.
A readiness score quoted is labelled as a measure of coverage, evidence and task state, and the conclusion on whether controls operated rests on evaluation results instead.
Every matter put for decision carries a decision-maker and a date, and anything undecided reappears next month.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the terms of reference naming the management forum, its cadence and the cut-off each report is prepared to.
Obtain the report issued for each month of the period, with the date it went out.
Obtain the monitoring plan and the record of evaluations completed at each cut-off; the plan is the population completion is measured against, not the evaluations returned.
Obtain the exception queue and the self-assessment results as they stood at each cut-off.
Obtain the readiness snapshots for the period, with the score and gap count recorded on each, and the minutes of the forum's meetings.

Analysis:
Compare reports issued against months in the period and identify every month that received none.
Recompute plan completion at three cut-offs from the underlying records and compare each with the figure the report carried.
Reconcile the results presented to the queue and the assessment population at the same cut-off, and name anything omitted.
Read how each readiness figure is described, and judge whether the report draws a conclusion on operating effectiveness from a coverage measure.
Trace each matter put for decision to the minute recording the decision, and age those never decided.

Output:
A schedule of months against reports issued, with the days between cut-off and issue for each.
The recomputed completion figures beside those reported, with every difference explained or unexplained.
A reconciliation of results presented to the queue and assessment populations, naming each item that did not reach management.
An ageing of undecided matters with the decision-maker named against each.

title.en: Frame the forum, the cut-off and what the account must carry

description.en: Settle with the executive forum which body receives the monitoring account, to what cut-off it is prepared, and the sections it carries each month, so the report is written to a standing specification rather than to whatever the month produced.

text.en: Name the forum that receives the account and the frequency it expects it on.
Fix the cut-off date and the lead time by which papers reach attendees.
Agree the sections carried: plan completion, evaluation results, queue ageing and decisions sought.
Record that this account goes to management, separately from the account the committee receives.
Settle how a matter is escalated between reports when it cannot wait for the next one.

title.en: Derive the monthly figures from the records behind them

description.en: Build the report as an extract from the plan, the queue and the assessment population at the cut-off, so its figures can be recomputed by someone else instead of being taken from the preparer's notes.

text.en: Build the completion figure directly from the plan lines due by the cut-off.
Pull the queue and assessment results at the same cut-off so the figures agree.
Take the readiness score from the snapshot and label what it measures on the page.
Add an ageing column to every open item, computed from its raised date.
Set out a decisions section listing what is being asked of management this month.

title.en: Table the monthly account and minute the decisions taken

description.en: Issue the account to the forum within the lead time, present the matters needing a decision, and record what was decided against each one so the next report can start from it.

evidenceHint.en: The issued report for each month with its issue date, the extracts it was built from, and the minute recording each decision taken and the name against it.

text.en: Prepare the report at the cut-off and issue it within the agreed lead time.
Present plan completion against schedule, including work not yet performed.
Put each matter needing a decision with a recommendation and a proposed owner.
Minute the decision taken on each matter, with the name and the date due.
Carry forward anything undecided into the following month's decisions section.

title.en: Chase the decisions management owes and age those open

description.en: Follow the matters the forum was asked to decide, month by month, so a result reported once and then left undecided is visible as an ageing item rather than quietly dropped.

evidenceHint.en: The dated schedule of matters put to the forum, showing the month each was raised, the decision recorded or its absence, and the age of every matter still open.

text.en: Collect the decisions section from every report issued in the period.
Match each matter to the minute that records a decision on it.
Age every matter with no decision, from the month it was first put.
Report the oldest undecided matters to the forum ahead of the next meeting.
Confirm the previous month's decisions reached the owner named against them.

templates.title: Internal audit charter approved with independence
templates.description: The written mandate under which internal audit operates: what it may examine, the records and people it may reach without asking permission, who decides its budget and the tenure of its head, and the reporting line to the audit committee that keeps its conclusions free of the management they concern.
templates.objective: To ensure internal audit works under a charter the board has approved, fixing its mandate, its right of access, and a reporting line that leaves it independent of what it examines.
templates.successCriteria:
A current charter carries the board's approval date and version, and was re-approved within the last twelve months.
It names what internal audit may examine and the records, systems and people it may reach without management's consent.
The committee, not management, decides the function's budget and the appointment and removal of its head.
Each auditor files a written independence declaration annually and again when an engagement opens.
No engagement was concluded by a person who performed or owned the control tested, and any exception names its compensating review.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the charter in force for the period with its version history and the minute approving each version.
Obtain the independence declarations filed by the head of the function and by every auditor, which is the population completeness is measured against.
Obtain the engagement list for the period from the AuditCycle rows and the fieldwork Audit rows attached to them.
Obtain the budget approval, the appointment decision and the pay review covering the head of the function.
Collect the minutes of any session the committee held with no management present.

Analysis:
Compare the charter in force against the version the minute approved, and date the interval since the last re-approval.
Test every declaration filed by the head of the function and a sample of fifteen auditor declarations against the engagements those auditors led.
Compare the lead auditor on each engagement against the performer and owner recorded for the controls tested; test all engagements rather than a sample, because the population is small and one breach is the failure.
Trace the budget, appointment and pay decisions to the body that took them and identify any taken by audited management.
Read the access clause against every instance in the period where a record or system was withheld or delayed.

Output:
Schedule of charter versions with approval dates and the months elapsed since the last re-approval.
Declarations obtained against declarations owed, naming each auditor who filed none.
Independence exceptions by engagement, naming the auditor, the control tested and the relationship that breached the terms.
Finding on whether the reporting, budget and tenure arrangements leave the function independent in fact and not only in the text.

title.en: Draft the mandate, the access rights and the reporting line it rests on

description.en: Write the charter's substance before it goes for approval: what internal audit may examine, what it may reach without asking the audited party, and who answers for its findings, its budget and the tenure of its head.

text.en: State the activities, entities and systems internal audit may examine without invitation.
Name the records and people the function may reach, and the narrow grounds on which access may be refused.
Fix the functional reporting line to the audit committee and the administrative line beside it.
Reserve the budget, the appointment and the removal of the head of function to the committee.
Bar the function from owning or operating any control it will later examine.

title.en: Separate the function's budget and tenure from the line it audits

description.en: Put the independence terms into the arrangements that actually decide: where the budget is set, who appoints and removes the head of function, and who reviews that person's objectives and pay.

text.en: Move the budget decision onto the committee's own agenda and minute the approval.
Give the committee the appointment and removal decision in writing rather than by convention.
Settle the objectives and pay review of the head of function with the committee chair.
Record any administrative reporting line and state what it may not decide.
Schedule a session each period at which the committee sits with no management present.

title.en: Confirm the independence of each auditor before an engagement opens

description.en: Collect and read the written declarations, once a year and again as each piece of work is assigned, and move the work elsewhere where a declared relationship reaches the control that is to be tested.

evidenceHint.en: The signed declaration for every auditor with its date, set beside the work they were assigned, and the reassignment note wherever a declared relationship reached a control under test.

text.en: Issue the declaration form to every auditor at the opening of the year.
Re-issue it as each engagement is assigned, naming the control population in scope.
Read each return against the performer and owner recorded for those controls.
Reassign the work where a declared relationship touches what is to be tested.
File the returns with the engagement record so a later reader can see them.

title.en: Challenge any engagement the independence terms should have barred

description.en: Look back over the completed work and test whether the charter held in practice: access given, conclusions not softened by the audited party, and nobody leading work the terms disqualified them from.

text.en: Draw the engagements completed in the period and the auditor who led each.
Compare each lead against the performer and owner of the controls that were tested.
Ask the audited managers whether any record or system was withheld or delayed.
Read the draft and issued reports for conclusions softened after management comment.
Take the breaches, and the charter amendments they argue for, to the committee.

templates.title: Risk-based internal audit plan approved annually
templates.description: The annual decision about where audit effort goes: an auditable universe drawn from the reporting scope and the risk register, each unit ranked and given a rotation interval, the engagements that fit the hours the function actually holds, and the coverage the plan knowingly declines.
templates.objective: To ensure the year's audit effort is directed by assessed risk rather than by habit, with the plan and the coverage it declines approved by the committee before the work begins.
templates.successCriteria:
An auditable universe exists that reconciles to the in-scope processes, accounts and systems, each unit scored against the risk register.
Every engagement cites the risk or scope entry that put it in the plan, and each unit left unvisited carries its rotation interval and the date it was last audited.
The plan states the hours and the specialist skills each engagement needs, against the hours the function actually holds.
The committee approved the plan before the year's work started, and the minute records the coverage the plan declines.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved plan for the year with the minute recording the date it was approved.
Obtain the auditable universe together with the risk register and reporting scope it was derived from, which together are the population coverage is measured against.
Obtain the AuditCycle rows raised for the period, each carrying the framework, the period and the status the plan promised.
Obtain the resourcing schedule: hours held, hours planned per engagement, and the skills each one needs.
Collect every in-year amendment to the plan and the paper that carried it back to the committee.

Analysis:
Reconcile the universe to the in-scope process, account and system lists, naming every unit present in one and absent from the other.
Re-perform the ranking for a sample of twenty units against the risk register scores and report any engagement the scores do not support.
Read the rotation interval and the date last audited for every unit not visited this year, and age those past their interval.
Compare planned hours against hours held, including leave and training, and judge whether the plan was deliverable on the day it was approved.
Trace each amendment to the paper that disclosed it and date that approval against the work it changed.

Output:
Reconciliation of the auditable universe to the reporting scope, naming units that appear in neither list.
Re-performed rankings, naming every engagement the risk scores do not support.
Ageing of units past their rotation interval, with the years elapsed since each was last audited.
Schedule of in-year amendments, showing which reached the committee before the changed work began.

title.en: Assemble the auditable universe from the reporting scope and the register

description.en: Build the list of units that could be audited at all, before any question of priority: the processes, accounts, systems and providers in reporting scope, each carrying the risk the register already records against it.

text.en: Draw the in-scope processes, accounts and systems from the reporting scope decision.
Add the outsourced services and shared platforms a reported figure depends on.
Attach to each unit the risk register entries and the scores already recorded.
Note the date each unit was last audited and what that engagement concluded.
Mark units where no audit skill exists in-house, so resourcing can address them.

title.en: Allocate the hours the function holds across the ranked units

description.en: Turn the ranked universe into a deliverable schedule: rotation intervals for what is not visited this year, engagements sized in hours and skills, and an honest statement of what the available capacity leaves out.

text.en: Score each unit on the register's risk and the years since its last engagement.
Assign a rotation interval to every unit the plan will not visit this year.
Size each proposed engagement in hours and name the skills it needs.
Subtract leave, training and contingency before committing the remaining hours.
Write down the coverage the hours will not reach, rather than leaving it unsaid.

title.en: Put the plan to the committee with the coverage it declines named

description.en: Take the plan for approval before the year's work starts, showing the risk basis for what is included and, in the same paper, the units the hours will not reach and the interval before each is next seen.

evidenceHint.en: The approved plan with the committee minute and its approval date, beside the schedule of units left unvisited and the rotation interval recorded against each.

text.en: Table the plan before the first engagement of the year is opened.
Show the risk basis beside each engagement rather than the engagement alone.
Present the declined coverage as a schedule the committee can challenge.
Minute the approval, its date, and any coverage the committee added.
Raise an AuditCycle for each approved engagement with its period recorded.

title.en: Amend the plan in year when the risk picture moves

description.en: Handle the acquisition, restatement, system replacement or incident that lands after approval: re-rank the affected units, move the hours, and take the change back to the committee before the altered work starts.

evidenceHint.en: Each amendment with the event that prompted it, the engagement added or dropped, the hours moved, and the committee paper that carried it before the changed work began.

text.en: Name the trigger that argues for a change and the units it touches.
Re-score those units and show what the new ranking displaces.
Move the hours explicitly, so a dropped engagement is visible rather than silent.
Carry the change to the committee before the altered work is opened.
Update the cycle records so the plan and the raised engagements still agree.

title.en: Contrast what the year delivered against what the plan promised

description.en: Close the year by measuring delivery against approval: engagements completed, dropped or carried forward, hours consumed against hours planned, and whether the units left unvisited were the ones the risk ranking said to leave.

text.en: List the planned engagements beside their delivered status and completion date.
Account for every engagement dropped or carried into the following year.
Compare hours consumed against hours planned for each completed engagement.
Test whether the units left unvisited match the ranking the committee approved.
Feed the shortfall into next year's universe as an input, not as a footnote.

templates.title: Internal audit engagements executed and reported
templates.description: Each engagement the plan scheduled is actually run: a programme of tests against criteria fixed at the opening, evidence obtained and retained with the fieldwork record, a conclusion on the area audited, and a report issued to the audited management and to the committee within the interval the charter sets.
templates.objective: To ensure each planned engagement is executed to a written programme by auditors who own none of the controls tested, and reported to management and the committee within a fixed interval.
templates.successCriteria:
Every engagement the plan scheduled ends completed or cancelled, and a cancellation names who decided it.
Each runs to a written programme whose tests and sample sizes were fixed at the opening, not after the results were seen.
The evidence behind each conclusion is retained with the engagement and legible to a reader who was not there.
No conclusion is reached by a person who performs or owns the control tested, which is what makes it stronger than a self-assessment.
A report reaches the audited management and the committee within the interval the charter sets, naming the conclusion and each finding raised.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved plan and the AuditCycle rows raised for the period, which together are the population of engagements owed.
Obtain for each engagement the fieldwork Audit row with its scope, criteria, auditors and status, and the checklist results recorded against it.
Obtain the working papers and the evidence retained behind each recorded conclusion.
Obtain the issued reports with their issue dates and the distribution each went to.
Collect the opening and closing records, including management's written response to each conclusion.

Analysis:
Compare engagements delivered against engagements planned and name every one not started, not finished, or finished after the year closed.
Take a sample of five engagements, or all of them where fewer ran, and read the programme against the objective and criteria set at the opening.
Re-perform two tests per sampled engagement from the retained evidence and compare the result against the conclusion recorded.
Compare each lead auditor against the performer and owner of the controls tested; work concluded by the control's own operator is a self-assessment and must be reported as one rather than as independent assurance.
Measure the days from fieldwork closing to report issue for every engagement, against the interval the charter sets.

Output:
Plan-to-delivery schedule naming each planned engagement that did not run and the reason recorded for it.
Re-performed tests beside the conclusion they support or contradict, by engagement.
Independence exceptions naming the engagement, the auditor and the control that auditor owns.
Ageing of report issue against the charter interval, stating the median and the worst case.

title.en: Frame the objective, the period and the criteria the work will test

description.en: Open each engagement by writing down what it is for and what it will be measured against, so the conclusion at the end answers a question that was asked at the start rather than one the results suggested.

text.en: State the objective in terms the audited management can agree or dispute.
Delimit the period, the locations and the control population in scope.
Name the criteria each test will judge against, and where they come from.
Fix the sample sizes before any testing begins, and record the basis.
Minute the opening meeting, including anything management asked to be excluded.

title.en: Build the programme and open the cycle that will hold its papers

description.en: Convert the scoping decisions into an executable programme and the record structure it will fill: the test steps, the evidence each one requires, and the AuditCycle and fieldwork Audit rows that will carry them.

text.en: Write each test step with the evidence it needs and the criterion it serves.
Attach the programme to the fieldwork Audit row raised under its AuditCycle.
Load the test steps as checklist items so each result is recorded separately.
Assign the auditors and confirm none owns a control the programme tests.
Agree the reporting deadline that will run from the close of fieldwork.

title.en: Run the fieldwork and record each result against its checklist item

description.en: Execute the programme as written, capture the evidence behind every result at the time it is obtained, and record deviations from the programme as they happen rather than reconstructing them afterwards.

evidenceHint.en: The fieldwork record for each engagement with its checklist results, the evidence retained behind every one, and working papers a reader who was not present can follow.

text.en: Perform each test on the sample fixed at scoping, and record any change to it.
Retain the evidence behind every result with the item it supports.
Record a not-tested result as such rather than leaving the item blank.
Raise a finding as soon as a test fails, not at the end of the engagement.
Note any access refused or delayed, with the date and the party involved.

title.en: Issue the conclusion to the audited management and to the committee

description.en: Report what the work concluded: the objective, the tests performed, the conclusion on the area audited and every finding raised, distributed within the charter interval and carrying management's own written response.

evidenceHint.en: The issued report with its date and distribution, the days elapsed since fieldwork closed, and management's written response to each conclusion it carries.

text.en: Put the draft to the audited management for factual comment with a fixed deadline.
Keep the conclusion in the words the evidence supports, recording any dispute beside it.
Assemble the AuditPack the committee receives, freezing the items it cites.
Issue within the charter interval, recording the date fieldwork actually closed.
Share the frozen pack under an expiring AuditPackShare link where a recipient holds no account.

title.en: Contest any conclusion signed by the operator of the control tested

description.en: Test the independence claim the report makes, engagement by engagement, and report anything concluded by the party that owns the control as the self-assessment it is rather than as assurance from outside.

text.en: Draw the engagements concluded in the period and the auditor who signed each.
Compare each signer against the performer and owner of the controls examined.
Re-read any conclusion the audited party redrafted before it was issued.
Report a breach as weaker evidence, naming what would have to be redone.
Ask what work was not done because the only qualified person was conflicted.

templates.title: Internal audit findings tracked to closure
templates.description: The register of what internal audit raised and what happened next: each finding held against the engagement that produced it, with an agreed action, a named owner and a due date, closed only when the function has re-tested the control. The population is the findings this function raised, which is not the evaluated deficiency log management keeps.
templates.objective: To ensure each finding reported by an internal audit engagement is owned, dated and actioned, and is closed only once the function that raised it has re-tested the control.
templates.successCriteria:
Every finding in an engagement report appears in the tracker against the engagement that raised it, and the counts agree.
Each open item carries an agreed action, a named owner and a due date, none of them blank when the item is accepted.
Closure rests on a re-test the function performed, with tester and date recorded; the owner's assertion does not close an item.
Items past their due date are aged and reported, and an extension records who granted it rather than the date quietly moving.
Where management accepts the risk instead of acting, the acceptance names the officer and goes to the committee.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain every internal audit report issued in the period and the findings each raised, which is the population the tracker's completeness is measured against.
Obtain the Finding rows carrying an engagement's auditId, with the status, assignee, due date and severity recorded on each.
Obtain the re-test records behind each closure, with the tester and date held against the finding as verifiedBy and verifiedAt.
Obtain the extensions granted and the risk acceptances recorded during the period.
Collect the ageing reports taken to management and to the committee.

Analysis:
Reconcile findings in the issued reports to rows in the tracker item by item across every report rather than a sample, since a finding reported and never tracked is the failure this control exists to catch.
Test all closures where fewer than twenty-five were made, otherwise a sample of twenty-five, for a re-test performed by the function rather than by the item's owner.
Re-perform the ageing of every open item from its agreed date and compare it against the ageing that was reported.
Read each extension for the approver named and the revised date, and identify due dates moved with no approval behind them.
Separate this population from the evaluated deficiency log management keeps, and confirm no item was moved between the two in a way that reset its age.

Output:
Report-to-tracker reconciliation naming each finding that never reached the tracker.
Closure testing naming every item closed without a re-test by the function.
Re-performed ageing beside the ageing reported, with each difference named.
Schedule of extensions and risk acceptances with the officer who granted each.

title.en: Delimit the population this tracker owns, against the deficiency log

description.en: Fix the boundary before the first entry is made: this register holds what internal audit engagements raised, while the evaluated deficiency log management keeps is a separate population with its own owner and its own cadence.

text.en: State that an item enters here when an engagement report raises it.
Name the management log this register is not, and who maintains that one.
Decide how an item appearing in both is cross-referenced without double counting.
Settle the fields an entry must carry before the function will accept it.
Agree with management who answers for an item from the moment it is raised.

title.en: Attach every raised finding to the engagement that produced it

description.en: Land each reported finding in the platform as a row that carries its own provenance and accountability, so the tracker is an extract of what exists rather than a spreadsheet written alongside it.

text.en: Raise each reported finding as a Finding row carrying the engagement's auditId.
Set the assignee, the due date and the agreed action on the row itself.
Adopt the status lifecycle from OPEN through READY_FOR_VERIFICATION to CLOSED.
Link the finding to the control it was raised against, so that control shows it.
Refuse an entry that arrives with no owner or no date on the day it is created.

title.en: Sweep the open items monthly and age what has passed its date

description.en: Work the open population on a fixed day each month: recompute how far past due each item is, put the list in front of the owner who holds it, and record any extension as a decision somebody made rather than a date that moved.

evidenceHint.en: The monthly ageing run listing each open item with its owner and days past due, the chase sent to that owner, and any extension carrying the name of who granted it.

text.en: Pull the open population from the tracker on a fixed day of the month.
Compute days past due from the agreed date, not from the last update.
Send each owner the items they hold and the date each one is due.
Record an extension only where an approver is named and a revised date set.
Report the aged population to management with the oldest item named first.

title.en: Re-test the control before an item is marked closed

description.en: Treat a closure request as a hypothesis to be tested: draw a fresh sample from the period after the remediation landed, and return the item to open where the evidence does not support what the owner claims.

evidenceHint.en: The re-test record behind each closure naming the tester, the date and the sample re-examined, held against the finding it closes with verifiedBy and verifiedAt set.

text.en: Take the closure request with whatever evidence the owner filed behind it.
Re-examine a fresh sample drawn after the remediation was put in place.
Record the tester and the date against the finding as verifiedBy and verifiedAt.
Return the item to open where the re-test does not support the claim made.
Close the row only once the re-test stands on its own record.

title.en: Judge each closure on whether re-test or assertion supports it

description.en: Look back over the period's closures and separate those resting on the function's own re-test from those resting on the owner's word, reporting the proportion rather than the count so the difference cannot be lost in a total.

text.en: Draw every closure made during the period from the tracker.
Read the record behind each for a re-test performed by the function.
Compute the share of closures supported only by the owner's assertion.
Reopen the closures the evidence does not support and re-age them.
Report the share and the reopened items to the committee in session.

templates.title: Control deficiencies identified and logged centrally
templates.description: Every route by which a control failure becomes known — a testing exception, a self-assessment, an audit finding, an incident, an external auditor's comment — lands in one deficiency log within a fixed window.
templates.objective: To ensure every control failure that becomes known, by whatever route, is recorded in one central deficiency log within a fixed window and against the control it affects.
templates.successCriteria:
Each deficiency reaches the central log within five business days of the date it became known, and both dates sit on the record.
Every entry names its source, the control affected and the account or assertion at risk.
Each identification route named in the map either produced entries in the period, or the absence is explained.
No rival deficiency list survives outside the log; one found is closed and its open items migrated with their original dates.
The artefact supporting each entry is attached to the record, not cited by location.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the identification map listing every route by which a deficiency becomes known and the owner of each route.
Export the central deficiency log for the period, with date identified, date entered, source, affected control and attached artefact for each item.
Obtain each route's own output: control testing exception reports, completed self-assessments, audit finding registers, the incident log and the external auditor's communications.
Collect any departmental issue list, tracker or spreadsheet held outside the log.

Analysis:
Take each route's own output as the completeness base and search the log for a matching entry; test every item from the external auditor and the incident log, and a sample of twenty-five across the remaining routes.
Compute date entered less date identified across the whole population and count the items outside the window.
Test a sample of twenty-five log entries for a named source, an affected control and an account or assertion, and for an attached artefact rather than a reference to one.
Compare any list found outside the log against the log itself, item by item, and treat each unmatched open item as an unlogged deficiency.
Confirm that a route which produced nothing in the period is explained rather than silent.

Output:
Completeness schedule per route: population size, items matched in the log, and every item not matched.
Distribution of logging delay, naming each item outside the window with its owner.
Attribute results for the sampled entries, naming those missing a source, a control or an artefact.
Schedule of deficiencies found only outside the central log, with the list they came from and their age.

title.en: Enumerate the routes a deficiency can arrive by

description.en: Name every activity that can reveal a control failure — testing, self-assessment, internal and external audit, incidents, management review — and the owner who must pass each one into the log.

text.en: Name each identification route and the person accountable for passing its output into the log.
State the window, in business days, between a deficiency becoming known and its entry.
Define the minimum entry: source, date identified, affected control, account or assertion at risk.
Decide what counts as a deficiency, so a housekeeping observation is not logged as one.
Note which routes are expected to produce nothing in a normal period, and how that is evidenced.

title.en: Establish a single log and retire the lists around it

description.en: Make one Finding population the only deficiency register, migrate what the departmental spreadsheets hold and close them, so completeness has one place where it can be measured.

text.en: Designate the platform's Finding population as the one deficiency register for the organization.
Carry source, date identified and affected control on each record so provenance is captured at entry.
Migrate open items out of departmental spreadsheets, keeping their original identification dates.
Close the migrated lists and withdraw write access, so nothing new accumulates outside the register.
Attach each supporting artefact to its record through FindingEvidence rather than citing a location.

title.en: Capture each deficiency inside the agreed window

description.en: As each route produces a failure, raise its record with source, affected control and artefact attached, and do it inside the window rather than at the period end when the report is due.

evidenceHint.en: The central register export for the period showing, for every item, the date it became known beside the date it was entered, with the source artefact attached to the record.

text.en: Raise the record when the failure becomes known, not when its cause is understood.
Enter the source route and the date it became known alongside the date of entry.
Attach the exception report, test working paper or auditor communication to the record.
Link the record to the control affected, so the register can be read by control.
Flag anything entered outside the window for the next completeness review.

title.en: Sweep each source for failures that never reached the register

description.en: Work from the routes' own output back into the register rather than reading the register alone, because a deficiency that was never entered cannot be found by reviewing what the register holds.

text.en: Take each route's own output for the period as the population, not the register.
Search the register for a matching entry and name every item that has none.
Test whether any departmental list has reappeared, and reconcile it to the register.
Measure the logging delay across the population and report the items outside the window.
Report unlogged items with their source and their age to the register's owner.

templates.title: Deficiency severity evaluated against defined criteria
templates.description: The organization's own written criteria — deficiency, significant deficiency, material weakness — applied to every logged item by magnitude and likelihood, singly and in aggregate, with the reasoning recorded.
templates.objective: To ensure every logged deficiency is placed in one of three defined tiers — deficiency, significant deficiency or material weakness — against written magnitude and likelihood criteria.
templates.successCriteria:
The written criteria state, for each of the three tiers, the magnitude and likelihood thresholds that place a deficiency in it.
Every open deficiency carries a tier, an evaluator, a date and reasoning tied to those thresholds.
Deficiencies touching the same account or assertion are evaluated in aggregate as well as singly, and that conclusion is recorded.
A tier reduced by reliance on a compensating control names the control and cites its own test result.
The platform's four-tier Finding severity is not treated as the ICFR tier; a record holding both carries the mapping rule.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the organization's written evaluation criteria in force during the period, with their approval date and the materiality figure they rest on.
Export the deficiency log with, for each item, the tier assigned, the evaluator, the evaluation date and the recorded reasoning.
Obtain the aggregation analysis for every account touched by more than one open deficiency.
Collect the latest test result for each compensating control relied on to reduce a tier.
Obtain the written mapping rule between the platform's Finding severity and the three ICFR tiers, where a record carries both.

Analysis:
Re-perform the tier assignment for every deficiency graded significant or material weakness, and for a sample of twenty graded below, applying the criteria to the facts on the record.
Judge the direction of each difference: a tier below what the criteria require is a reporting failure, one above is not.
Recompute the aggregation for each account with more than one open deficiency and set the aggregate tier beside the highest individual one.
Where a compensating control was relied on, read its test result and judge whether it covers the same assertion and period as the deficiency.
Compare each record's Finding severity against its ICFR tier and confirm neither was derived from the other outside the written mapping rule.

Output:
Re-performed gradings with the criteria clause applied to each, naming every deficiency graded below what the thresholds require.
Aggregation schedule by account and assertion, with individual and aggregate tiers side by side.
Schedule of compensating-control reliance, naming any control whose own test did not pass.
Count of records carrying both a Finding severity and an ICFR tier, and whether the mapping rule was followed on each.

title.en: Adopt thresholds that separate the three tiers

description.en: Write the criteria that place a deficiency in one tier rather than another — magnitude against a stated materiality figure, and the likelihood that a misstatement goes undetected — and have them approved and dated.

text.en: Define a deficiency, a significant deficiency and a material weakness in the organization's own words.
Express magnitude against a stated materiality figure rather than against adjectives.
State the likelihood test that separates a remote possibility from a reasonable one.
Set the rule for aggregating deficiencies that touch the same account or assertion.
Have the criteria approved and dated, so a grading can be read against the version in force.

title.en: Hold the ICFR tier apart from the platform severity field

description.en: The platform's Finding severity runs LOW to CRITICAL, which is an operational scale and not the ICFR one, so give the tier its own recorded home and write down how, if at all, the two relate.

text.en: Give the ICFR tier its own recorded home on the deficiency record or its evaluation memo.
Attach that memo through FindingEvidence so the grading travels with the deficiency.
Write the mapping rule between Finding severity and the ICFR tier, and state its limits.
Say on the record itself that Finding severity is not the ICFR classification.
Build the reporting extract on the recorded tier, never on the severity field.

title.en: Apply the criteria to each deficiency as it is logged

description.en: Place every new item in a tier on the facts already recorded, name the evaluator, and set down the reasoning against the clause of the criteria relied on.

evidenceHint.en: The evaluation memo for every deficiency graded in the period, naming its evaluator, the date, the clause relied on and the tier reached.

text.en: Read the recorded facts — control, account, assertion, exposure — before assigning a tier.
Cite the clause of the criteria that places the deficiency in the tier chosen.
Name the evaluator and the date, so the grading has an author who can be asked.
Where a compensating control reduces the tier, name it and cite its last test result.
Attach the memo to the deficiency record rather than filing it somewhere else.

title.en: Re-evaluate the open population in aggregate at each cut-off

description.en: Individually minor items over one account can amount to a significant deficiency together, so the open population is regraded at the quarterly cut-off and not only when each item arrived.

evidenceHint.en: The aggregation analysis at each quarterly cut-off, showing every account with more than one item open and the combined tier it reached.

text.en: Group the open population by account and assertion at the cut-off date.
Judge each group as a whole against the aggregation rule in the criteria.
Raise the tier where the group exceeds what any single item reached alone.
Record the aggregate conclusion even where it leaves every tier unchanged.
Carry any tier raised into the escalation and remediation populations.

title.en: Re-perform a sample of gradings against the criteria

description.en: Take the facts on the record rather than the tier already assigned and re-apply the criteria, testing in particular whether any deficiency was graded below what the thresholds require.

text.en: Re-perform the grading for every item at the top two tiers and a sample below.
Apply the criteria version in force at the evaluation date, not the current one.
