description.en: Write down the tests a change must meet before it counts as significant, together with who rules on borderline cases, so two people judging the same change reach the same verdict.

text.en: State the tests a change must meet to count as significant, such as touching a material account or a system of record.
Work two past changes through the draft threshold and check the verdicts match what hindsight now says.
Set a lower tier for changes that are logged and watched but not put through full assessment.
Record who rules on a borderline case and how that ruling is documented.
Issue the threshold to every named reporter so verdicts stay consistent between them.

title.en: Poll every named reporter at the close of the quarter

description.en: Collect a return from each source reporter on a deadline tied to the quarter close, apply the threshold to what comes back, and route the significant changes onward within the same period.

evidenceHint.en: The dated sweep record for the period showing a return from every reporter on the source register, nil returns included, with each candidate change and its significance verdict.

text.en: Request a return from every reporter on the source register, with a deadline tied to quarter close.
Capture each candidate change with the date it was first noticed, not the date it was reported.
Apply the significance threshold to each candidate and record the verdict against it.
Chase reporters who did not respond, and record a nil return only where there genuinely was none.
Hand every change judged significant to impact assessment and record the handover date.

title.en: Back-test the period's change log against minutes and contracts

description.en: Look for changes the sweep should have caught by reading evidence the sweep does not depend on, then trace each miss back to the source that failed to report it.

text.en: Read the board and committee minutes for the period and list the changes they disclose.
Review contracts signed, systems retired and senior leavers over the same period.
Set that list beside the change log and isolate anything the sweep never saw.
Trace each miss back to the source that should have reported it and record why it did not.
Report the misses to the risk assessment owner with a proposed fix to the source register.

templates.title: Control impact of significant changes assessed
templates.description: Each change accepted as significant is worked through to the specific controls it disturbs, with the risk it alters stated and a reviewed conclusion recorded before the change takes effect.
templates.objective: To ensure a change accepted as significant is worked through to the named controls it disturbs and the risk it alters, before the change reaches the ledger.
templates.successCriteria:
Every change marked significant in the period carries a completed impact assessment, none left open past the date the change took effect.
Each assessment names the individual controls affected, rather than the process or system in general.
The assessment states the risk the change introduces, removes or alters, and the reasoning behind that conclusion.
An assessment concluding that no control is affected carries the reasoning that supports it, not a bare answer.
Each assessment shows a preparer, a reviewer and dates, with the reviewer independent of the change being assessed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the change log for the period and the population of changes marked significant.
Obtain the completed impact assessment for each change in that population.
Obtain the control inventory the assessments draw identifiers from, at the version then in force.
Collect the effective date of each change and the sign-off date of its assessment.
Request the assessments concluding that no control was affected, as a separate population.

Analysis:
Reconcile the assessment population against the change log to find significant changes carrying no assessment.
Check that each assessment cites controls that exist in the inventory, named individually rather than by process.
Compare each sign-off date against the change's effective date and quantify the assessments that landed late.
Read the no-effect conclusions and judge whether the reasoning holds against the process the change touched.
Walk the affected process for a sample of assessed changes to find controls disturbed that the assessment never named.

Output:
List significant changes with no assessment, and assessments signed after the change took effect.
Record the controls the walkthrough found affected that the assessment omitted.
State whether reviewer independence held across the population, naming each exception.

title.en: Trace the change through to the accounts it can reach

description.en: Follow the accepted change along the process it alters, from transaction initiation to the ledger entry, so the assessment starts from the accounts and assertions actually exposed rather than from a guess.

text.en: Walk the change through the process from transaction initiation to the ledger entry it produces.
Identify the accounts and assertions the change can reach, naming each one explicitly.
Pull the controls currently recorded against those processes from the control inventory.
Note which of those controls depend on the system, data or person that the change alters.
Identify the process owners who must contribute to the assessment and agree their input dates.

title.en: Build the assessment format every accepted change is put through

description.en: Create the working paper an assessment is completed on, with fields that force named controls and stated reasoning, so a conclusion cannot be reached by assertion alone.

text.en: Draft the questions an assessment must answer: risk introduced, controls affected, response required.
Require affected controls to be cited by identifier, with process-level answers not accepted.
Add a field for the reasoning behind a no-effect conclusion so it cannot be a bare tick.
Fix who prepares and who reviews, keeping the reviewer clear of the change being assessed.
Pilot the format on one recent change and adjust the fields that produced unusable answers.

title.en: Assess the accepted change against the controls it disturbs

description.en: Complete the assessment while the change is still in design, naming each affected control and the effect on it, and obtain independent review before the change goes live.

evidenceHint.en: The signed impact assessment for the change, citing every affected control by identifier, with the risk conclusion and the preparer and reviewer names and dates.

text.en: Complete the assessment format while the change is still in design, not after go-live.
Cite each affected control by its inventory identifier and state the effect the change has on it.
State the risk the change introduces or removes, and whether the existing controls still cover it.
Obtain review from someone independent of the change and record both names with their dates.
File the assessment against the change log entry so the log and the assessments reconcile.

title.en: Challenge the conclusions that found no control affected

description.en: Re-examine the assessments that concluded nothing was disturbed, since that conclusion closes a change with no further work and is the one most likely to be reached for convenience.

text.en: Select every assessment in the period concluding that no control was affected.
Walk the underlying process for a sample and look for controls the change touched in practice.
Test whether the reasoning given would survive the same change made in another process.
Refer any assessment that understated the effect back for rework, with the gap stated.
Report the rate of overturned no-effect conclusions to the risk assessment owner.

templates.title: Control design updated following assessed changes
templates.description: The design actions an impact assessment calls for are carried into the controls themselves: descriptions, owners and evidence amended, obsolete controls retired, the amended control operated once, and unactioned conclusions aged and escalated.
templates.objective: To ensure the design actions an impact assessment calls for reach the controls themselves, so a documented conclusion cannot stand in for a control that was never amended.
templates.successCriteria:
Every assessment conclusion calling for a design action has that action recorded with an owner and a due date.
The control documentation in force carries the amendment, with its version number and effective date.
Controls the change made obsolete are retired from the inventory and the testing plan, not left unperformed.
Each amended control shows at least one completed execution under the new design, with the evidence it now produces.
Open design actions are aged monthly and those past their due date are escalated to a named recipient.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the impact assessments for the period and the design actions each one raised.
Export the design action tracker showing owner, due date, status and completion date.
Obtain the control documentation before and after amendment, with version numbers and effective dates.
Collect the first executed instance of each amended control and the evidence it produced.
Obtain the monthly ageing reports and the escalations they triggered.

Analysis:
Reconcile the actions raised by the assessments against the tracker to find conclusions never actioned.
Compare the amended documentation against what the assessment asked for and note where it falls short.
Confirm each amended control has operated at least once under its new design and inspect the evidence produced.
Check that retired controls left the inventory and the testing plan, rather than being marked inactive in place.
Age the open actions independently and set your result beside the ageing that was reported.

Output:
List assessment conclusions with no corresponding design action, naming the assessment they came from.
State how many amended controls have yet to operate once under the new design.
Report the oldest open design action, its owner, and the escalation history against it.

title.en: Turn each assessment conclusion into a dated design action

description.en: Convert the conclusions of completed assessments into tracked actions, one per affected control, each with an owner able to alter that control and a due date tied to when the change takes effect.

text.en: Read the conclusion of each completed assessment and extract the design change it requires.
Raise an action per affected control, rather than one action covering the whole change.
Assign an owner who can actually alter the control, and a due date tied to the effective date.
Flag conclusions requiring no design action, with the reason recorded against them.
Load the actions into the tracker that the monthly ageing is run from.

title.en: Amend the affected control descriptions, owners and evidence

description.en: Rework the control documentation so it describes how the control now operates, retire what the change made redundant, and add whatever new control the assessment called for.

text.en: Rewrite the control description so it matches how the control will now operate.
Reset the owner, frequency and expected evidence wherever the change moved any of them.
Retire controls the change made redundant and take them out of the testing plan.
Add any new control the assessment called for, with its own owner and evidence.
Version the documentation and record the date the new design takes effect.

title.en: Operate the amended control once and keep its first output

description.en: Put the redesigned control into live operation at its first scheduled occurrence and retain what it produces, so the design change is shown to work rather than only to have been written down.

evidenceHint.en: The first execution of each redesigned control on live data, with the output it produced, the date it ran and the owner who performed it.

text.en: Run the control in its amended form on live data at its first scheduled occurrence.
Retain the output the new design produces so the evidence expectation can be tested.
Confirm the named owner performed it, rather than the person who designed the change.
Record the date of that first run against the design action so completion is dated.
Raise a defect where the amended design proved unworkable in live operation.

title.en: Escalate design actions still open past their due date

description.en: Age the open actions each month and push the overdue ones upward, separating those whose change is already live from those still in design, because the first group is running on stale controls.

text.en: Age the open design actions each month against the due dates recorded for them.
Separate actions whose change is already live from those still in design.
Escalate anything overdue whose change has taken effect, naming the recipient.
Record management's response and any revised date that was agreed.
Report repeat slippage on the same control to the risk assessment owner.
